## 17BN. `node --test tests/` — the invocation that stopped working (2026-09-25)

The demo's own suite reported **failed** on a machine running Node 26, while the same run's check
that a report filed in the demo reaches `issues.Issue` **passed**. Both facts were true, and the
failing one was not a failing test. The log had no failing test in it at all:

```
Error: Cannot find module '.../school-management-demo/tests'
  code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND'
# tests 1 / # pass 0 / # fail 1
```

`node --test tests/` — a bare directory — expanded to the test files inside it on Node 18 and is
resolved as a **module entry point** by Node 26, which dies before running a single test. One
"failure", zero tests executed, and an error that reads exactly like a broken suite.

**This was a hole in the verification, not bad luck.** The suite had been run on Node 18 and passed
573/573. A `node >= 18` assertion establishes a floor and says nothing about a ceiling — and the
demo has no `engines` ceiling and no lockfile, so whichever Node a machine happens to have is the
one it uses. A version check that only tests the floor keeps reporting OK while the thing underneath
it stops working. Reproduced by fetching Node 26.5.0 to match the failing machine exactly.

**The fix is the invocation.** `tests/*.test.js` is expanded by the shell, so Node is handed 41 real
file paths and never has to interpret a directory:

| | `node --test tests/` | `node --test tests/*.test.js` |
|---|---|---|
| Node 18.19.1 | 573 pass, 0 fail | **573 pass, 0 fail** |
| Node 26.5.0 | `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, 0 run | **573 pass, 0 fail** |

`package.json`'s `test` script carried the same invocation, so **`npm test` in this repository was
broken for anybody on a modern Node**, and had been since the demo landed. All 41 test files are
flat in `tests/`, so the glob loses nothing and correctly skips `helpers.js` and the
`stories-*.txt`.

**A second bug, found while fixing the first.** The surrounding script counted assertions with
`grep -c '^ok '` and excerpted failures with `grep '^not ok'` — both TAP, which is Node 18's default
reporter. Node 26 defaults to `spec`, coloured symbols, so the count printed `0` and, far worse, **a
genuinely failing suite would have printed a blank explanation**. Pinning `--test-reporter=tap`
makes the output the same on every Node rather than the same on the one it was written against.

### Left open

- **Nothing pins the demo's Node.** An `engines` field would turn "this stopped working three majors
  ago" into a refusal at install time. Not added here because `engine-strict` is already set for
  this project and a ceiling needs a real decision about what the demo supports.

---

## 17BO. `/dziennik`: the school demo as a page with no server behind it (2026-09-25)

The owner's terms were narrow and they decided the whole design: publish the school-management demo
on edmat.net, **hardcode the data**, run it as a subpage with **no risk of escalating privileges**,
link it from the user menu and the footer, and allow it **one** outbound call — filing an issue.

That ruled out the obvious answer. A reverse-proxied Node process keeps sessions, login and ~21,000
lines of route logic reachable on the public site, which is precisely the surface the terms exclude.
So the demo is published with **no backend at all**.

### What made it possible

`public/app/core.js` has exactly one `fetch`, inside `rawFetch` — the same discipline as this site's
own `lib/api/client.ts`, and for once the payoff is not "we changed the base URL" but "we removed
the network". Every one of the 20 screens asks its questions through that function, so replacing it
replaces the whole backend.

### Recorded answers, not reimplemented logic

`scripts/record-snapshot.js` drives a real instance over the DevTools protocol, through a recording
proxy, and keeps the JSON body of every successful API GET, keyed by role. `build-static.js` bakes
the result in and `snapshot.js` answers `rawFetch` from it.

**Completeness is defined by the app's own navigation, not by a list.** The first version reused
`smoke.js`'s matrix, which pairs each screen with the user who owns it — right for a smoke test,
wrong here, because the published page lets a visitor pick any role and click anything. Opening the
logbook as the head teacher hit "not recorded", which is the first click a visitor makes. So the
walk signs in as a role, reads back the hash links the app itself rendered, and visits each: the
same definition of "what this role can reach" that the published page will use, so the two cannot
disagree. 137 responses became **263**.

### The page cannot reach the network, as a property of the file

Not "guarded so it cannot be reached" — the build **removes** it. `core.js`'s `fetch` is replaced by
a throw (EdSnapshot returns above it) and `print.js`, which probes `/api/pdf` *outside* `rawFetch`,
is replaced wholesale by a stub that says printing needs the full version. The build then counts
`fetch(` in everything it ships and **fails** unless the total is exactly one: `snapshot.js`'s
forward to `/api/issues/`, same-origin because the page is served from edmat.net.

That guard earned itself immediately: it found `print.js`, a second outbound call nobody had
accounted for.

Writes are refused locally with `demo_read_only`. There is no server to write to, and a demo that
faked a save would be lying about the one thing a school most needs to trust; queueing it would mean
holding invented pupil data in a stranger's browser for a sync that can never happen. The role is
**chosen, not authenticated** — `/api/auth/session` is a recorded answer like any other — so there
is no password to get wrong, no token to steal and no privilege to escalate. The worst a visitor can
do is read a different part of a file that was public the moment it was published.

The service worker is not shipped and any worker from an earlier visit is unregistered: it caches
API responses, and a stale cache answering over the snapshot is a silent wrong answer.

### Served without touching Apache

Built into `frontend/build/dziennik/`, so the vhost that already serves the SPA serves this too — no
Alias, no new env var, no `<Directory>` block, no server-side step at all. It works because the demo
routes on the **hash** (`#/lekcja`), so every request under `/dziennik/` is a real file or the
directory index, and the SPA's `FallbackResource` (scoped to its own `<Directory>`) never sees it.

Polish by default, seeded into `localStorage` before `i18n.js` runs: the demo falls back to
`navigator.language`, which is right for software a school installs and wrong for a page on a Polish
site — a visitor with an English browser met a Polish school's logbook in English. `?lang=` and the
in-app switcher still win.

### In the site

`school_demo` is the 27th `FeatureFlag`, seeded ON, and it is the first that guards **no endpoint**:
the demo has no Django surface, so what it governs is the two links. Turning it off hides the
entrance and does **not** take the page down — `/dziennik` is served by the vhost, and a saved URL
keeps working. That honest limit is written in the model, the migration and the runbook, because a
kill switch that does less than the others must say so. The menu entry is added to the
`accountItems` snippet, which renders into the desktop popover and the phone drawer from one place,
so the flag cannot hide it in one and leave it in the other.

### Verified

- **`scripts/verify-static.js` (new)** walks the BUILT files with no server running — for every
  role, every route that role's own navigation offers — and fails on a snapshot miss, a console
  error, an uncaught exception, a missing `<h1>`, or a literal `undefined`/`NaN`/`[object Object]`
  in the rendered text. That is the regression test for the snapshot: a recording made correctly and
  then built wrongly looks identical until somebody clicks. **All 11 roles pass** — 8 in the main
  pass and the remaining 3 in a follow-up after the fixes below, not all 11 in one run.
- **It found two real things and one bug in itself.** The student and the parent both "missed"
  `/api/events`; asking the server directly returned **403** — they are genuinely not allowed to see
  the staff events list, so the snapshot was right to hold nothing and the *replay* was wrong to
  call it "not recorded". Refusals are now recorded and replayed with their real status, which is
  also the more honest demo: a school should see that the product refuses a pupil. Separately the
  verifier crashed nine roles in, because `/json/list` can answer before Chrome has a page target;
  guarded and retried now, and `--roles=` lets one failure be re-checked without re-walking
  everything (a full pass is ~15 minutes).
- **`top-up-snapshot.js` (new)** heals one `role=path` gap in seconds instead of a 20-minute
  re-record, by asking the server that one question. No browser: a miss is a known URL, and the
  browser was only ever needed to DISCOVER which URLs a screen asks for.
- The built bundle contains **one** `fetch(` in total.
- `npm run check` 0 errors, 0 warnings; both catalogues 3597 keys, sets identical.
- `manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` clean.

### Left open

- **The demo is read-only, and that is the trade.** Nothing saves. A school clicking "add a grade"
  is told this is a recorded demo. The alternative — bundling the real server into the browser
  behind `fs` and `crypto` shims — is a much larger job and was not what was asked for.
- **A screen no navigation links to is not recorded**, because the walk follows links. Anything
  reachable only by typing a hash, or behind a button that changes route, will miss.
- **The verifier is slow** (~1–2 min per role) and is not wired into `pack.sh`, so it is a thing
  somebody runs, not a gate.
- **Query-shaped routes are recorded as they were captured.** Anything the page asks for with a
  parameter it computes fresh — a date other than the frozen 2026-10-23 — will miss.

## 17BP. `/conference`, and the bug that only a signed-in visitor could see (2026-09-25)

Three commits after the §17BO publish, every one found by the owner using the live site rather than
by anything automated. Replayed as `publish/2026-09-25f`, pushed (`99766ea..9ed4860`); bundle
`FUW/UPDATE-20260925-f.tar.gz`.

**`/conference` — a stable address (`e1ad302`).** `seed_conference_demo` gives the event whatever
pk the database hands out, so `/events/130` is right on one installation and wrong everywhere else.
The route finds the event by the `TEST=FAKE ` marker its title carries (`FAKE_PREFIX`, mirrored from
`backend/testing/personas.py`) and forwards. Deliberately not prerendered — the answer depends on
the database it is asked about.

**It found the wrong conference (`986d6a7`).** `getEvents()` defaults to `when=upcoming`
(`starts_at >= now`), and the demo conference is seeded with day one set to *today* so that it looks
lived-in. It has therefore always already started, is in neither `upcoming` nor `past`, and never
appeared. Two events carry the marker — the demo and the personas' near-empty Sandbox, which starts
in a fortnight and so *does* appear — and the route forwarded to the Sandbox, convincingly. Fix:
`when: 'all'` (the service now takes `'upcoming' | 'past' | 'all'`) plus a deliberate choice: of the
marked events that have started, the one still running, else the latest started, else any. A query
parameter's default is a decision the call site has to make; inheriting it is how the wrong row got
picked.

**`/dziennik` lost every report from anyone signed in to edmat (`3294696`).** The demo is served
from the same origin as the site. A visitor with an edmat session had their `sessionid` cookie
attached to the report POST by the browser's `credentials: 'same-origin'` default; DRF's
`SessionAuthentication` then authenticated them and enforced CSRF, which the request carries no
token for — `403 CSRF Failed: CSRF cookie not set.` The report was dropped; the static build has
nowhere to save locally; `/admin/issues/issue/` showed nothing. Anonymous visitors were fine, which
is exactly why every check passed: the deploy check runs server-side with no cookie,
`verify-static.js` walks screens and never files a report, and every browser verification used a
fresh profile. The only person who could see it was somebody logged in — the owner, on production,
after it shipped. Fix: `credentials: 'omit'`. `lib/api/client.ts` already does this with a comment
giving exactly this reasoning, and `config/settings.py` records an earlier CSRF bug from the same
interaction: the rule was written in the one place that makes fetches, and the demo's `rawFetch` is a
second seam in a second codebase that inherited none of it.

**How it was reproduced.** A single-origin server (static demo at `/dziennik`, `/api` proxied to
Django — production's topology) driven over CDP, first with a fresh profile (201, issues #30/#31),
then with a session cookie set (403). The fix verified the same way:
`{ok:true, forwarded:true, remoteId:"33"}` with the cookie present.

### Left open

- **Nothing files a report as a signed-in visitor**, which is the case that broke. A check that
  sets a session cookie and submits one report would have caught it in seconds. On `todo.md`.
- **`/conference` is a redirect, not a landing.** The owner asked for it to be developed further
  as the session ended. The natural next step is the `/dziennik` shape: a page that says what the
  demo conference contains (programme, venue, documents, tickets, rota, cloakroom), names the
  seeded accounts a visitor can sign in as (`backend/testing/personas.py`, `DEFAULT_PASSWORD`,
  all contained to the conference by `assert_contained`) and links each surface of
  `/events/[id]/{rota,cloakroom,scan,ticket,badges}`. Whether the persona password may appear
  on a public page is the owner's call — the accounts are contained, but public credentials on
  production are still a decision. On `todo.md`.
- The reports `/dziennik` files are `is_public=False`, so they reach the admin and not `/issues`
  without "include private". Whether the demo should file publicly is undecided.

## 17BQ. `manage.py import_exercises`: a way back into the corpus, and a skill that explains it (2026-10-01)

**Why.** Adding exercises in bulk had no supported path. `/submit` is one exercise at a time through
the moderation queue, by design. The only batch tool was `import_legacy_corpus`, and it had been dead
since the taxonomy restructure (commit 420bf41) without anybody noticing — running it on 2026-10-01
produced `FieldError: Cannot resolve keyword 'field'` on the first row. Three independent breakages:
`DisciplineTranslation(field=…)` and `Branch(field=…)` (the FK is `discipline` now), a
`Branch(university=…)` the model no longer has, and a glob over `content/branches/*/branch.yaml`
when the corpus on disk is `content/courses/*/course.yaml`. It is kept, unrepaired, as provenance:
its slugs are the pre-restructure shape (`uw-matematyka-am2` — a university's subject), so a
"fixed" run would recreate exactly the conflation the restructure removed.

**What was built.** `exercises/management/commands/import_exercises.py` — same file format (YAML front
matter + `##` sections, Polish or English headings), current schema, any branch. Idempotent by
`(branch, number)`, the exercise's own `unique_together`. A file with no `number:` gets one allocated
from the branch's highest (stepping over numbers the batch claims explicitly) **and written back into
the file**, because a batch whose numbers live only in the database duplicates itself on the second
run — and there is no external-id column to key on instead. `--dry-run` validates and rolls back.

Validation runs over the whole batch first and **one bad file imports nothing**, with every problem in
every file listed in one report. What it refuses was chosen from what the schema actually punishes:
unknown front-matter keys (a mistyped `tag:` would be silently dropped), `verified:` (derived from the
solution pool — the error says so and says what to do instead), a `## heading` that is not one of the
four (its text would vanish), unbalanced `\( \)` / `\[ \]`, two files claiming one number, a topic the
branch does not have unless `--create-topics`.

Deliberate asymmetries, each with the reason in the module docstring: topics are `.set()` from the
file (structure the file is asserting), tags are `.add()`ed (a reader may have applied one, and
`.set()` would undo that on every re-run); no activity row and no tag-follower notification; nothing
sanitizes here because `ExerciseTranslation.save()` and `SolutionEntry.save()` already do, which is
also why a `<script>` in a source file is dropped rather than refused; `recount_verified` is called
per row instead of trusting the entry signals, so a row with no solution at all is still correct.

**The skill.** `.claude/skills/import-exercises/SKILL.md` plus `reference/format.md` (every key,
every section heading, every refusal) and `reference/alternatives.md` (the submission API, the
translation route, why `import_legacy_corpus` is dead, and the four things a hand-written ORM script
gets wrong). Written for an LLM that has never seen this repo: the first section is "one exercise is
not one row". A row was added to the root `CLAUDE.md` doc table so it is reachable without
`.claude/` ever being read.

**Verified by running it.** The validation report on a deliberately broken file; a real import into
the dev database (two rows, one numbered 9001, one allocated 389), the write-back, a second run
reporting `0 created, 2 updated`, and the resulting rows inspected directly — `verified=True` on the
one with a solution, `False` on the one without, `source.type='exam'` from `Egzamin`, the pinned
entries published and authorless. Both demo rows were then removed again. `manage.py test exercises`
is **131 tests, OK**; the eight new ones (`ImportExercisesCommandTests`) lock in each property the
skill promises — including the one found while reviewing the first draft: an import must never move
`published` back **up**, because an unpublished row is a moderator's removal or a report-driven
auto-hide, and re-running the batch it came from is not an appeal.

### Left open

- The content sweep **was** run against a real import, which is step 6 of the skill's own
  procedure: `dump_text_fields` + `check:katex` over 2 255 rows including the two imported ones,
  **0 issues**. Two traps worth the line it took to find them, now in the skill: the system Node is
  18 and cannot run `tsx` at all (Node 24 lives at `~/.cache/edmat-tools/node24/bin`), and invoking
  the script directly instead of through `npm run` loses `--max-old-space-size=8192`, which the
  full corpus needs — it dies in a V8 heap dump that looks nothing like a content problem.
- **No figures.** An exercise whose statement needs a picture cannot be imported — attachments and
  inline images are user-facing endpoints only. The skill says to wait rather than ship the row
  with the picture missing.
- Also not built, and named in the skill: `ExerciseMaterialLink`, `ExerciseRequirement`, subtopics,
  a per-file author, any unpublish/delete path, and CSV/LaTeX input.

## §17BQ — the owner's 2026-10-01 list: a trimmed bar, a stated mission, two Polish addresses, and the other half of the needs board

One checklist, given and then twice extended while the work was in flight. Branch
`ux/mission-nav-tutoring-volunteering`, based on `e450276` — the tree `UPDATE-20260925-f` was
packed from, which is what was on prod when this started.

**Shipped the same day** as `FUW/UPDATE-20261001.tar.gz`, applied to webek4 by the owner and
verified from the live site rather than assumed: `/tutoring`, `/korki` and `/materialy` answer as
real prerendered pages on edmat.net, the trimmed bar is there with Events as an icon, an old
`/services/new` link forwards to `/korki/new`, and `/volunteering` is live. Runbook:
`deploy/UPDATE-2026-10-01.md`.

Three decisions were taken with the owner before any code, because each would have changed the
shape of the work: localized URLs as *real* localized paths rather than aliases; `/volunteering`
for the public offers board (so the shifts rota's hours page moves under it); and the offers model
in the `needs` app rather than as a `services.Service` kind or a new app.

### The navbar carries the mission, and Events is a calendar

The bar had grown to seven browse links and was saying that Materials, Courses and Concepts are as
central as the exercises. They leave it: Exercises, Help wanted, Tutoring, About, and Events last
as an icon at every width. Nothing is killed and no flag changed — Materials and Courses are still
home-page tabs, all three are still `/about` cards, every route is untouched behind an untouched
switch. What went away is the claim the bar was making.

Because the item lists are snippets rendered into both the desktop popover and the phone drawer,
removing a link removes it from both — which is the point. Events being an icon means its rule
carries no media query, so stages 0, 1, 4 and 9 of the staged collapse went with the links they
collapsed and About took the vacated stage-0 width.

Four entries left the account menus in the same pass, all by owner decision and none killed: "New
concept", "Add a course", "New organisation" and the school-logbook demo link. Each surface keeps
its own create control; what stops is the site offering them from every page. Three flags lost
their last reader in the header and are no longer read there at all.

### `/about` says what EdMat is for

Three numbered pillars under the hero, ordered because the order is the argument: people run
courses here; materials are catalogued and reviewed rather than merely uploaded; **tutoring is the
motivation**. The third says the quiet part — a tutor's listing is where standing earned here turns
into students, which is a better answer to "why would anybody write all this down?" than altruism
alone — and repeats, where somebody actually reads it, what `FINANCES.md` requires.

### `/tutoring`, and `/korki` in Polish

A deliberate exception to the neutral-English URL rule, taken with the owner, who was told the rule
and chose it anyway. `/materials` ↔ `/materialy` followed an hour later, when the answer to "rename
'Zacznij materiał z innymi' to what?" turned out to be "make this only available in /materials and
/materialy" — so that entry moved to the materials hub rather than being renamed, and the hub now
carries both ways to make a material side by side.

Three pieces, all needed: `urlPatterns` in `vite.config.ts` (order matters, and the catch-all is
not optional — without it Paraglide's default pattern starts emitting `/en/...`); the `hooks.ts`
reroute that already existed; and `localizedPath()` at the call site. It is reactive, because
`locale.svelte.ts` overwrites `getLocale` with a rune: the picker rewrites the address with no
reload. Both Polish addresses are prerendered by name, because `pl` is the base locale.

**One thing cost an afternoon and is written down so it is not repeated.**
`svelte/no-navigation-without-resolve` accepts an href typed exactly `ResolvedPathname`, which
`localizedPath` returns — so turning type-aware linting on (`projectService`, src only, no
type-checked rule set) removed every disable comment, and the rule still caught a planted bare
href. Then `npx eslint .` took 13 minutes and died with a heap out-of-memory core dump, against 19
seconds without it. A verification command that cannot finish is worse than a comment. Eighteen
comments, each naming the helper.

### A solution can be a scan, a structure, a sketch or a PDF

"Make adding solution as PDF, image, Chemistry, etc. work" — it did not, and the reason was narrow:
the composer on the exercise page had a `RichEditor` and no `InsertStrip` beside it. Three of the
four ways go into the body and cost nothing but mounting the strip. A PDF cannot, so
`SolutionEntryAttachment` is `community.CommentAttachment` again — same limit, same
`process_attachment`, same allowance, same random stored name. A failed upload does not lose the
entry: the words are already saved, so failures are counted and said out loud.

The same strip went onto all four content fields of `/submit` and onto the tutoring listing's
description, which also started rendering (`MathContent`) — and therefore started being sanitized
on write, in the same commit, with the seven refusal tests that widening owes.

### Several files, several materials

"Adding material form should allow multiple files" cannot mean several files on one material:
`coauthoring.MaterialVersion` holds exactly one payload, and that invariant is load-bearing enough
that its own docstring explains why it is not even a DB check constraint. So several files become
several *materials*, which is what somebody uploading five chapters as five PDFs wanted anyway;
what they did not want was to fill the form in five times. Everything above the payload is chosen
once. With more than one file each gets its own title row, seeded from its filename.

One request per material, in sequence — each allocates a number in a bounded retry loop against a
single-writer SQLite. A failure part-way through does not undo what landed, and the page says how
many got in rather than calling a partly-successful submit a failure.

### Volunteering offers, in different languages

`needs` now holds both sides. The shared vocabulary is why living in one app pays: an offer reuses
`NEED_KIND_CHOICES` and `SKILL_LEVEL_CHOICES` verbatim.

"In different languages" turned out to be two questions. `language` is what the offer is *written*
in — the platform's existing content axis, so `?content_locales=` narrows the board and the hidden
count rides back in the usual header. `spoken_languages` is what the volunteer can *help* in, which
is a fact about the person and the one somebody searching usually means: an advert typed in Polish
by somebody who also speaks Ukrainian is exactly the row a family looking for Ukrainian-speaking
help needs to find. Collapsing the two would have lost whichever was collapsed away.

`?speaks=` filters in Python, because `JSONField.__contains` raises `NotSupportedError` on SQLite.

### One inbox, if you ask for it

`Profile.combined_inbox`, default off — which is exactly what everybody already has, down to the
two icons. On: the envelope leaves the header, the bell counts both, and the unread conversations
appear above the notifications. It is deliberately not one of the notify-on-* switches it sits
above: those decide whether a row is ever *created*; this only decides where two existing lists are
drawn.

### What the browser found that nothing else did

Two selector mistakes in the verification script looked like product bugs and were not (the
strip's picture and PDF controls are `<label>`s wrapping file inputs, not buttons; the settings
page's first submit button is not the save button). One real bug was found by **looking at the
screenshot**: the offer form had a 150px hole under its title box, because `flex: 1 1 12rem` on
every `.field` is read as a *height* for the ones that are direct children of a column flex
container. `svelte-check`, eslint and a production build all pass on it. House rule 2, again.

### Verified

`manage.py test` per app: `services` 76, `exercises community` 200, `needs` 44, `moderation` 119,
`accounts` 128 — all OK. `npm run check` 0/0, `npx eslint src` clean, `npm run build` green with
`korki.html` and `materialy.html` in the output. A real browser against real servers: an offer
posted through the real form and found again by its spoken language, `/korki` ↔ `/tutoring`
rewriting live as the picker moves, a real PDF attached to a real solution and opened in place, and
the inbox preference turning the envelope off and back on, and three PDFs picked at once becoming
three materials with the renamed one keeping its new name. 40 checks, 0 failures, no console
errors.

### Left open

- **`moderation.FeatureFlagTests` had been failing on this branch before any of this** —
  `school_demo` was seeded on 2026-09-25 and never added to its expected set. Fixed here, with
  `volunteering`, but it is worth noticing that a stale assertion sat green-adjacent for a week
  because nobody ran that suite.
- **`npm run lint` still fails on three files this work did not touch** (`e2e/decisions.mjs`,
  `e2e/event-shifts.mjs` were already unformatted; `Footer.svelte` was too and picked up a
  reformat in passing). `prettier --check` runs before eslint, so the whole command is red until
  somebody formats them.
- **The e2e scripts were edited but not run.** They need both servers and seeded demo users, and
  the run belongs with a browser pass rather than with the edit; `node --check` passes on all
  eight. The ad-hoc script that WAS run covers the same ground for the new surfaces.
- **No merged inbox FEED** — the conversations are a strip above the notifications, not rows
  interleaved by time, which would need one endpoint that can order two tables together.
- **No way to answer a volunteering offer except to message the volunteer**, no matching between
  the two boards, no `/wolontariat`, and no thread/report/activity row on an offer.
- **The footer still links `/dziennik`.** The owner named the user menu; the footer is a different
  surface, and widening the ask is not this pass's call.

## 17BS — Discussions under the standing pages: a thread where there is no row (2026-10-06)

Owner's ask, in one sentence: a comment section under each section of `/about` and its subpages,
subtle, drawn on click, with replies "using today's infrastructure"; a superadmin able to turn off a
specific location; and switches for who may write there — "anyone (anons as well), users, verified
users, staff, and pending".

**The one thing that had to be invented, and the three that did not.** `/about`, the seven
`/about/<feature>` showcase pages and the manual's twelve are prerendered prose with no row in any
table, and a `Comment` reaches its target through a `GenericForeignKey` — so there was nothing to
point at. `community.DiscussionLocation` is that row, and it is the whole of the new schema.
Everything else was already here: the thread, the reply tree, the votes, the report flow, the
tombstones, the sanitizer and `CommentNode.svelte` all came for free from the generic `Comment`,
which is exactly what that model was built to make possible.

**"Pending" turned out not to be a fifth audience.** Four of the five options the owner listed
answer *who* and one answers *what happens to what they wrote*, and as one field "verified
contributors, and hold what they write" cannot be said at all. Owner chose two fields:
`audience` (anyone | users | verified | staff) and `moderated`.

**Anonymous writing is always held, whatever `moderated` says** — also an owner decision, and the
right one for a reason the implementation then made obvious: every moderation surface here assumes
an account behind the row, somebody to notify, to suspend, to show a history of. A visitor has none,
so the only honest place for their comment is in front of a human before anybody else reads it.

**Holding needed no new state and no second queue.** `accounts.minors.hold_for_review` already did
exactly this for a minor's comment — set `auto_hidden_at` and file a `Report` in the author's name,
so the existing queue can show, restore and remove it. Reusing it is what turned a "held comments
queue" into nothing at all. It cost one widening: `Report.reported_by` is nullable now, because the
server holding something has no name to file it in. Nothing reads a reporter's name (the queue
payload carries counts and reasons, deliberately), and `Comment.author` became nullable in the same
pass, with its three readers taught about it.

**A page-level row is a ceiling, and that is what makes per-section switches usable.** A row with
`section=''` applies to every section on its page; where the two disagree the narrower wins and
`moderated` is an OR. Without it, "close discussion on this chapter" would have meant finding and
editing a dozen rows.

**Rows are created lazily and the page allowlist is a pattern, not a list.** The manual's sections
live in `frontend/src/lib/content/guide/*.ts`, which Python cannot read, so the frontend declares
what it draws and the server validates its shape — the same division `community/targets.py` already
settles for comment target names. The cost is named rather than hidden: a well-formed junk key makes
a location row nobody will ever read, visible to a moderator as a row with no comments.

**One real bug, and the tests caught it in the way that matters.** The first `effective_policy`
started from `DEFAULT_AUDIENCE` and narrowed, so a location explicitly set to `anyone` came back as
`users` — the widest setting a moderator can choose was the one setting that did nothing. Every
refusal test for an anonymous writer passed anyway, because the refusal they expected was the
refusal the bug produced; what failed was the one test asserting that an anonymous writer MAY write.
A second, smaller version of the same mistake: an unknown audience value was normalised only when
two rows had to be compared, so a single row carrying one came back verbatim and matched no branch
at all. Failing closed has to be the behaviour of the common path, not of the comparison.

**Verified:** `manage.py test community.test_discussions` 42/42; the full suite; `check`,
`makemigrations --check`; `npm run check` 0 errors 0 warnings over 6337 files; `npm run lint`;
`npm run build`; catalogues 3928 keys each; and `e2e/about-discussions.mjs` 25/25 with zero console
errors, against both real servers, with the screenshots looked at. Two of that script's own
failures were worth keeping: it asserted against a panel that was still showing "Loading…", and a
long chain of page loads exhausted the dev server into `ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES` — which reads
exactly like the feature being broken and is `e2e/CLAUDE.md` trap 3.

**Left open.** No per-step threads inside a manual chapter (one per chapter, deliberately — a
chapter is a numbered list of short steps). No delete endpoint for a standing-page thread, so the
browser script leaves its comments behind. An anonymous writer sees their own held comment in the
response to their own POST and never again, because there is no account to tie it to. The held
count in the moderation list is a number, not a link into the queue filtered to that location. And
`/privacy`, `/levels` and `/legal` have no discussions — they are standing pages too, but they are
legal text, and talk under them is a different decision.

## 17BR — The learning cycle: eight parallel steps, and what integrating them found (2026-10-05 → 2026-10-06)

The design is `prompts/00-DESIGN.md`; the eight step briefs are `prompts/02`–`09`; the five launch
decisions are `prompts/README.md` §9. Eight worktrees from one prep commit (**`f90e221`** — flags
0047, an empty `flashcards` app, `config/creation.py` wired into four create paths, `/api/creation/`,
the flashcards service stub with `createDeckFromExercises`'s signature fixed before the app existed,
and a marker comment at every mount point), eight agents, **all on Opus 5 by owner decision** rather
than a cheaper model for the small steps — the steps were not small, and the three that looked it
(G, H, F) each turned out to touch a dozen files.

The prep commit is the reason eight branches could run at once without a single shared-file
collision: every seam one step needed from another was a **named module in the owning app that
imports nothing from the consumer** (`flashcards/work.py`, `flashcards/record.py`,
`courses/record.py`), and the integrator wires them. Nobody edited `config/settings.py`,
`config/urls.py`, `moderation/models.py`'s flag enum, or `notifications/services.py`.

**One deliberate deviation from the design.** `00-DESIGN.md` §4.1 said decks are private only. Read
literally that would have made step C's "make a deck from this lesson" and step E's "take this home"
produce decks nobody but their maker could open, so a deck placed on a node is studyable by
everybody who can view that node (`flashcards/CLAUDE.md`, decision 1). `is_public` exists, defaults
off, and a minor may not set it.

### What integration found

Steps G, F, E, D, C and B merged on 10-05. **A and H did not**, and `UPDATE-20261006` was packed and
applied to production without them — which is the real lesson of this cycle and the reason this
preamble exists. The symptom was not a failing test but a live one: migration 0047 seeds
`flashcards` **on**, and steps C, D and E each ship a "make a deck" button behind that flag, so
production showed three buttons whose `POST /api/decks/` answered 404 — `backend/flashcards/` was
still the prep stub, three lines of docstring and an empty router. House rule 3 in reverse: not a
killed feature still showing its buttons, but a feature *never merged* still showing them, because
the flag that gates them is seeded by the prep commit rather than by the step. **A flag belongs to
the migration of the step that implements it, or it advertises work that may not arrive.**

The stopgap was the kill switch doing its job (switch `flashcards` off, no redeploy). The fix was to
merge A and H on 10-06 and cut `UPDATE-20261006-b`.

Four more things the merge itself turned up, each a shape worth recognising again:

- **`resolve_union.py` folded a function shut.** A's labels block and the `completionRefusalMessage`
  above it end in the same four lines (`		}`, `	}`, a `return`, `}`), so the union spliced A's
  whole block — an `import` included — *inside* that function's body. `svelte-check` would have
  caught it; the reason to look first is that the same fold once silently removed a closing brace
  from this file (commit `19e9660`). **Union-merging code is a guess that has to be read.**
- **The prerender list needed a comma, and G had said so.** G's own comment ended "Step H appends
  its `/about/guide/**` pages below, which means putting a comma on the last line here" — and the
  union left exactly that comma out, in `svelte.config.js` and again in `check_accessibility.ts`.
- **Two apps had implemented the same metric.** `identity.record.lessons_done_by_branch` (B, read-only
  over `courses`) and `courses.record.activity_by_branch` (C, in the app that owns `LessonProgress`)
  both answer `lessons_done`, and `_activity_block` **sums** across providers — so registering both,
  as `prompts/10-integration.md` §3 said to, would have doubled every number on every profile. Only
  flashcards' provider is registered; `identity/apps.py` records why, and one of the two duplicates
  still has to go (`todo.md`).
- **`svelte-check` reported 139 errors that were one stale codegen.** Every `decks_*` key "did not
  exist" because Paraglide had not recompiled after the catalogues merged. `svelte-kit sync` does not
  compile Paraglide; a build does. 0 errors, 0 warnings over 6295 files afterwards.

Two test-side assertions were also wrong rather than the code they describe — a permission-matrix row
that expected 404 where `courses/views.py` documents a **scoped, not refused** 200, and
`moderation.tests`' flag set, which was missing 0047's three keys (and had already gone stale once
the same way, for `school_demo`). Pre-merge the serial suite was 2580 tests with those two failures;
post-merge, see the board entry for the numbers actually run.

## 17BR.E — Events: take-home decks from a session, and event ↔ course through the organisation (2026-10-05)

Learning step E (`prompts/06-event-takeaways.md`, branch `learn/e-events`, from prep `f90e221`).
Two panels on an event, both small, both the same shape of idea: **what a reader takes away from a
session**, and **what else the people who ran it are running**.

### Take home

A programme session already points at the corpus — `SessionLink` is material XOR exercise XOR set
XOR url (AUDIENCE-BRIEF §3.2). What was missing was the one thing a person actually wants at the
end of a workshop: everything it pointed at, in one place, to study later. `backend/events/
takehome.py` is that one question, and **two surfaces ask it**:

- `GET /api/events/{id}/sessions/{session_id}/exercises/` → `[{id, title}]`, the list the "Take
  home" button hands to `POST /api/decks/` in one call;
- `SessionSerializer.takehome_count`, the number `Programme.svelte` reads to decide whether to draw
  the button at all.

Keeping them one function is not tidiness. A serializer that counted `links` itself would draw a
button on a session whose only exercise link points at something a moderator has since hidden, and
the button would then produce an empty deck — the exact "two surfaces disagreeing" the root
`CLAUDE.md`'s boundary 2 exists to stop. The count is the length of the list, deliberately, not a
cheaper `COUNT` (house rule 5: recount, never track — and the rows are already in memory).

Three decisions inside it, each written in the module rather than inferred:

- **A linked set is read THROUGH the session even when the set is private.** `study.ExerciseSet` is
  private by default and `ExerciseSetViewSet.retrieve` still refuses a stranger — but an organiser
  who puts a set on a published programme has published its *membership* to that room, which is
  what the link is for. So `takehome.py` reads `ExerciseSetItem` directly and never consults
  `is_public`. Nothing is copied: the ids are live references (`00-DESIGN.md` §1 rule 2); the
  snapshot happens later, in the deck.
- **Order is the programme's order** (`SessionLink.Meta.ordering`, then each set's own
  `ExerciseSetItem.Meta.ordering`), first occurrence wins, so an exercise that is both linked
  directly and inside a set makes one card, not two.
- **Unpublished exercises are dropped**, matching `/api/exercises/bulk/`, which is what the review
  screen will load them with. A link to a since-hidden exercise is honestly absent rather than a
  card with no front.

On the frontend the button sits beside "Add these to My Set" in `Programme.svelte`, behind
`flashcards`, for a signed-in reader only (a deck belongs to a person). **An organiser's deck is
PLACED on the event** — `prompts/README.md` §9: placement is this cycle's sharing, so everybody who
can see the event can study it — and a visitor's deck is simply theirs. Not asking a visitor
whether to place it is house rule 6 from the other side: do not offer a refusal.

### Event ↔ course, through the organisation

`00-DESIGN.md` §1 rule 1: a new link between two surfaces goes **through a hub** first. So there is
no `Event.course` and no `Course.event`. A conference and the courses that came out of it are
related because one body ran both, and the body outlives either — which is also the only shape that
can say "a faculty hosted it and a student circle ran it", as `organizations/CLAUDE.md` already
argues against a nullable FK.

`GET /api/events/{id}/related-courses/` walks it: the event's `OrganizationLink` rows → those
organisations, narrowed by `organizations.access.can_view` → their `runs` links whose target is a
course → narrowed by `courses.views._visible_courses`, **asked, never re-implemented**. Both
narrowings are load-bearing and `_readable_links` already makes the point from the other side: a
link is a claim about two things, so it is only as public as the less public of them. A circle that
ran this event and also runs an unlisted course must not advertise that course's title here.

Two further choices worth naming:

- **It answers `[]` when `organizations` is off, not 403.** The whole-surface refusal belongs on
  `/api/organizations/…`, which `feature_gate` already gates; this endpoint is the *event page's*,
  and a neighbouring endpoint must keep working while returning nothing for the killed feature
  (house rule 3, the `my-schedule` precedent). The staff bypass is spelled exactly as `feature_gate`
  spells it, so the panel and the API agree about who still sees data.
- **It serialises with `courses.serializers.CourseSerializer`**, the shape `/api/courses/` already
  answers with, rather than a narrower summary of its own. The rows are the same rows under the same
  visibility rule, so there is nothing a second shape could narrow — and the frontend reuses
  `mapCourse` and `CourseCard` unchanged. `mapCourse` gained one word (`export`) and a comment
  saying why.

`RelatedCoursesPanel.svelte` sits at the `learning: event ↔ course (E)` marker, names the body
before it lists the courses (a list of courses on an event page with no stated reason is a
connection the reader has to guess at), and **draws nothing when there are no courses** — the
organisation badges are already on the page one marker up, so a "Run by" line with nothing under it
would repeat them. It checks `organizations` itself rather than being wrapped in `FeatureGate`,
which renders an "unavailable" notice: right for a route, wrong for a panel mid-page on somebody
else's event (the `VenuePanel` / `OrganizationsPanel` precedent, found both times by looking at a
screenshot).

### Verified

From the worktree, Node 24 on `PATH`, ports 8135 / 5235.

- `manage.py test events organizations config --keepdb` — **354 tests, OK** (336 s). Of those, the
  new `events/test_takehome.py` is **24**, run alone first and again inside the suite.
- `manage.py check` — 0 issues. `makemigrations --check --dry-run` — **no changes detected** (this
  step adds no migration and no model).
- `npm run check` — **0 errors, 0 warnings**, 5991 files. `npm run build` — built in 2 m 44 s,
  adapter-static wrote `build/`.
- `npx eslint .` — **6 errors, all pre-existing, all in e2e scripts this step did not touch**
  (`course-claims`, `galleries-and-applications`, `login-return`, `material-open-and-titles`,
  `prerender-check`); 0 in `src/`. `prettier --check .` likewise fails on four files this step did
  not touch — see "Left open".
- `e2e/take-home.mjs`, both real servers, seeded demo users — **53 checks, 0 failures, 0 console or
  page errors**, four screenshots looked at.
- Catalogues: 3667 keys each, symmetric difference empty, eleven new `takehome_*` keys.

**The first e2e run failed three checks and all three were the script, not the app**: it counted
`.course-card` and the Take home button before the panel's two fetches and the programme's own fetch
had landed. That is `e2e/CLAUDE.md` trap 8 in both directions — an absent panel "passes" before it
could have appeared, and a present one "fails" because the count ran first. The script now waits for
the programme's session title and for the panel's own text before any count, including before the
two kill-switch *absence* checks, which were otherwise vacuous.

**`POST /api/decks/` does not exist on this branch** — it is step A's — so the e2e intercepts it with

visitor. The real call is verified at integration, after A merges (`prompts/README.md` §9).

### Left open

- **No link from the "deck made" confirmation to the deck.** `/flashcards/[id]` is step A's route

## 17BR.G. The design showcase under `/about/<feature>` (✅ built, frontend only, 2026-10-05)

Step G of the learning cycle (`prompts/00-DESIGN.md`, `prompts/08-about-showcase.md`), built on
`learn/g-about` from the prep commit `f90e221` beside the seven features it describes.

**The problem.** This cycle adds flashcards, a learning record, school mode, a completion
certificate, concept paths and event take-home decks. A visitor who has never signed in can read
`/about` and learn that EdMat has courses and materials; they cannot see what a course with a deck
placed on it looks like, what a learning record says, or what a school on EdMat is. Every obvious
answer to that — seed a demonstration account, mock an API, take screenshots — has a cost: demo rows
in production tables, a second code path, or pictures that go stale the first time a card is
restyled.

**What was built.** Seven prerendered pages, `/about/{exercises,flashcards,learning-record,courses,
schools,concepts,events}`, each drawn with the **real components** fed **sample objects of the real
TypeScript types** from `lib/content/showcase/*.ts`. `ExerciseCard`, `CourseCard`, `EventCard`,
`ConceptCard`, `MaterialCard`, `EducationCard` and `TranscriptView` are the app's own; a thin twin
in `lib/components/showcase/` stands in only where the real thing fetches (`DeckTile`,
`RecordBlocks`, `CertificateSample`, `PathSteps`, `SampleRows`). Nothing is seeded, nothing is
fetched, and the pages render with the API down — which is the `/dziennik` posture of §17BO applied
one page at a time rather than to a whole second product.

Because the samples are components rather than images, they cannot go stale: a restyled card
restyles the showcase in the same commit.

**The decision that shaped everything else: `inert`.** Drawing a real `ExerciseCard` means its title
is a real `<a>` to `/exercises/9001` — an id that exists in a content file and in no database. Live,
every card on these pages would be a dead end. So `SampleFrame` wraps each sample in an `inert`
container: not clickable, not focusable, and out of the accessibility tree — which is the honest
description of what it is. That makes the `<figcaption>` load-bearing rather than decorative (it is
what a screen reader gets), so every caption in `lib/content/showcase/` names what the picture
actually shows. The e2e proves the attribute is doing work rather than sitting there: it clicks a
sample card with `force` and asserts the URL did not move.

**One sample is deliberately live** — the flashcard on `/about/flashcards` turns over, reveals its
hint and takes a grade, and the line under the buttons says "Nothing was saved" every time, because
there is no deck behind it. The brief drew that line (a flip is fine, a grade that stores nothing is
fine, an API call is not) and the e2e holds it: it counts requests to the API base after the page
has settled and asserts that operating the sample adds none.

**The text lives in `lib/content/`, not the catalogues**, the exception `about.ts`/`privacy.ts`/
`levels.ts` already opened: one piece of writing in both languages in one file, so a reviewer can
see whether the Polish still says what the English does. Only the chrome — the "Sample" badge, the
grade words, the back-link — is in the catalogues, under the `showcase_` prefix (34 keys, both
catalogues, 3690 each, key sets identical, and none of the 34 unused).

**Honesty about what is not on.** A showcase page is a *description*, so it renders whether or not
its feature is switched on; what it does is say so, in a warning band, when the flag is off
(`flashcards`, `learning_record`, `courses`, `organizations`, `concepts`, `events` — each page
answers to the one it describes, with the usual `|| isModerator` bypass). The index on `/about` is
deliberately **not** flag-gated, unlike the feature cards a few sections below it: hiding the
explanation of a killed feature leaves a reader with no way to find out what the site does.

**The school is invented.** A first draft named a real Warsaw secondary school and then put named
pupils and named guardians on its roster. Inside a sample frame, on a page that says nothing is
live — and still the wrong thing to do, so the school is `Hilbert Secondary School` /
`Liceum Ogólnokształcące im. Davida Hilberta`. The university on `/about/learning-record` stays
real, because it is this site's own provenance and `content/about.ts` already names it.

**Three things a screenshot found that nothing else did.** A deck tile read `made from a set
·private to its owner` — Svelte had eaten the space after a separator interleaved into the template,
so the two labels are joined in JavaScript now. The learning record's four-column activity table had
its last column cut mid-digit at 390px, which reads as broken data rather than as a table that
scrolls; it has a `min-width` so the overflow is real and the figures whole. And the demonstration's
limits on `/about/schools` rendered as an indented block with no bullets, because the global reset
removes list markers.

### Verified

  6055, because `svelte-kit sync` had just regenerated the Paraglide output alongside it).
- `npx eslint src e2e/showcase.mjs scripts/check_accessibility.ts svelte.config.js` — **clean**;
  `prettier --check` clean on every file this step touched.

## 17BR.D — Concept paths: the prerequisite closure, "before this, know…", and a deck from a concept (2026-10-05)

Step D of the learning cycle (`prompts/00-DESIGN.md`, `prompts/05-concept-paths.md`), on
`learn/d-concepts` from the prep commit `f90e221`. Two things, both inside `concepts`, both built on
an edge that already existed and that nothing had ever walked.

**The edge.** `ConceptLink(relation='prerequisite')` has said "know this first" since §17BD, one hop
at a time, drawn as a row of chips on a concept's own page. One hop is not the answer a reader
wants. Somebody stuck on an eigenvalue exercise is not helped by being told "eigenvalue"; they are
helped by "linear map, and before that vector space". That is a graph walk, which a chip row cannot
grow into by itself.

**`concepts/paths.py`** is that walk and nothing else: `prerequisite_closure(concepts, *, depth=4,
limit=20) -> [(concept, distance)]`, breadth-first, **pure over `ConceptLink`** — no request, no
user, no visibility. Three bounds, each of them the point rather than a safety net. Depth ≤ 4,
because past four hops the answer stops being a hint and becomes a syllabus (a reader who needs six
prerequisites needs a course, which is step C). ≤ 20 concepts, truncating the FAR end because
breadth-first reaches the near rungs first and they are the ones that matter to somebody stuck now.
And cycles cut, by never revisiting and by starting with the seeds already marked seen — the data
really can contain one, because two people each filing the same pair from their own end is an
honest disagreement about which comes first, not something to refuse at write time.

The purity is a decision with a cost, and the cost is written in the module: an invisible concept
can sit in the MIDDLE of a chain and be counted as a hop while being dropped from the answer. The
alternative — passing a visible pool into the walk — would make the distances depend on who is
reading, so two people would be told different numbers about the same graph. Visibility is asked
once, afterwards, by `views._closure_payload`, which is also where the prefetch for resolving each
rung's title lives.

**Three endpoints.** `GET /api/concepts/{slug}/prerequisites/` and `GET /api/concepts/{slug}/
exercises/` are behind the `concepts` gate like everything else on that page.
`GET /api/concept-links/learn-first/?target_type=&target_id=` is **not**: it answers `[]` rather
than 403 when the switch is off, joining the one carve-out this app already has, because it is read
by an exercise's own page on every load and sits two lines from the chip row that already behaves
that way. One of the two refusing while the other answers is how a reader gets half a row.

**The union matters.** `learn-first` seeds the walk with ALL the concepts a target is about, so an
exercise about three things gets one list and a shared prerequisite is one rung at its nearest
distance. It also means an exercise about *every* concept in a chain honestly has nothing left to
learn first — which `seed_concepts` produces, since it links the same two exercises to every concept
of a branch. The e2e pins that answer rather than treating it as a gap.

**Two renderings of one set of rows.** `LearnFirst.svelte` draws a flat chip row on the exercise
page, nearest first, a rung more than one hop back marked with a dashed border rather than a number
(a count would need a plural rule in two languages to say something the shape already says). On the
concept page the same component draws a **path**: farthest first, arrows between, ending at the
concept being read — "Limit → Integral → Derivative → **Mechanika kwantowa**". A list and an order
are different answers to the same data, and on a concept page the order is the one worth having. It
renders nothing at all when there is nothing: no heading, no empty state, the `LinkedConcepts`
precedent.

**The deck button.** `DeckFromConcept.svelte` on `/concepts/[slug]`, behind `flashcards`, hidden
when the concept has no exercises a reader may see — a button that always fails is worse than no
button. It calls step A's one pre-agreed shape, `createDeckFromExercises` with `source: {kind:
'concept'}`. There is deliberately no link to the deck that comes back: `/flashcards/[id]` is step
A's route and does not exist on this branch, and a link to a route that is not there is exactly the
bug house rule 2 records finding in a browser.

**One bug found by looking at a screenshot**, which is the only way it could have been found.
`serializers._target_title` named a concept TARGET by walking to its first published revision — so
the prerequisite CHIP read "Pochodna — po ludzku" (somebody's secondary-school article, first in the
table) two lines above the prerequisite PATH reading "Derivative". One screen, one concept, two
names. It had been wrong since §17BD and nothing had put the two namings side by side before. Fixed
by routing it through `_resolved_head`, which is the third caller of the resolve-for-this-reader
logic and therefore the one that earned the extraction (house rule 13).

### Verified

`manage.py test concepts config --keepdb` — **146 tests, OK** (19 of them the new `PathTests`:
the walk, the cycle, the depth and limit clamps, a shared prerequisite at its nearest distance, a
`related` link that is not a prerequisite, a query-count bound, and the three endpoints including
both kill-switch postures). `manage.py check` — no issues. `makemigrations --check --dry-run` — no
changes (this step adds no model and no migration). `npm run check` — **0 errors, 0 warnings**, run
twice (before and after the serializer fix). `npm run build` — green, run twice. `npx eslint` and
`prettier --check` on every file this step added or touched — clean. Both catalogues **3666 keys each, key sets identical**, ten new
`paths_*` keys.

`frontend/e2e/concept-paths.mjs` against real servers on 8134/5234, signed in through the real form
as `michal`: a prerequisite chain built in the real picker, closed into a deliberate cycle, then
read back three ways — **30 checks, 0 failures, 0 console errors**. Screenshots looked at, and the
`_target_title` bug above came out of one of them.

### Left open

- **`LearnFirst` does not refresh when a concept is linked beside it.** It fetches once per
  (target, session); linking a concept from the exercise page updates the chip row and leaves the
  "before this, know…" line stale until a reload. A shared store for "what this target is about"
  would fix both; one more fetch on every link would not be worth it.
- **No truncation notice.** When the walk hits depth 4 or 20 concepts it simply stops, and the
  reader is not told there was more. The honest version needs the walk to report that it cut, which
  is a shape change to a function three endpoints share.
- **A deck from a concept's PREREQUISITES**, a depth preference, and a "learning path" a reader can
  follow and tick — all named in the brief as out of scope; the third is a course.
- **`POST /api/decks/` was MOCKED in the e2e** (`prompts/README.md` §9): step A owns that endpoint
  and it answers 404 on this branch. The button, the ids it collects and the confirmation are real;
  the deck is not. The integrator verifies the real call after A merges, and adds the link to
  `/flashcards/[id]` that this step deliberately did not write.
- **`/api/concepts/{slug}/exercises/` does not narrow by band or language**, although `client.ts`
  appends both to every list-shaped GET. It is the input to "every exercise linked here", and one
  silently missing from a deck because its statement has no English translation would be a deck that
  disagrees with the chip row above it. Stated here rather than discovered later.
- **`prerequisite_closure` has no `pool` parameter**, so a concept nobody can see still costs a hop.
  Named in `paths.py` itself; it would change the fixed signature the brief froze.

### Found outside this step's scope, not fixed

- **A worktree's LOG SHARDS are not migrated by copying `db.sqlite3`.** Every write that records an
  `AuditEvent` — adding a link, removing one — answered **500 after creating the row**, with
  `no such table: telemetry_auditevent`. The data was right and the UI showed an error, which is
  about as misleading as a symptom gets, and it cost two e2e runs to tell apart from a code bug.
  Fixed for this worktree by migrating the nine `logs_*` aliases; `prompts/README.md` §3's
  worktree recipe does not mention them and every parallel branch of this cycle has the same hole.
- **`npm run lint` fails on four files this step did not touch** (`e2e/decisions.mjs`,
  `e2e/event-shifts.mjs`, `project.inlang/.meta.json`, `project.inlang/README.md`); `prettier
  --check` runs before eslint, so the whole command is red until somebody formats them. Noted in
  §17BQ's "Left open" too, and still true.
- **KaTeX fonts 403 on the dev server in a worktree**, because `node_modules` is a symlink to the
  main checkout and therefore outside Vite's `fs.allow` root. A build is unaffected; the e2e
  forgives them by name.

## 17BR.F. The creation gate: founding is for verified contributors until USOS (2026-10-05)

Learning cycle, step F (`prompts/07-creation-gate.md`, design `prompts/00-DESIGN.md` §2 row
"creation → verification"). Branch `learn/f-gate` from the prep commit `f90e221`.

**The problem.** Until the USOS connection exists (`LAUNCHCHECKLIST.md` §3a — an OAuth 1.0a client
and a consumer key from the university, neither of which engineering can unblock alone), this site
has no way to tell a real person from a fresh account. Reading, joining, enrolling, attending and
booking are all reversible and already moderated. **Founding** is not: a course, an event, a
tutoring listing and an organisation each put a name in front of strangers, carry a roster, and
invite other people to turn up somewhere.

So those four create paths — and nothing else — now ask one rule module, and the owner's decision
(00-DESIGN.md §4.6) is that it refuses anybody who is not staff and not a verified contributor.

### `config/creation.py` — one module, four answers, and the order is the design

The prep commit shipped the shape and wired it into the four views and `GET /api/creation/`; this
step wrote the body. `creation_block_reason(user, kind)` answers, in this order:

1. **`anonymous`** — the only useful thing to say to somebody with no account, and every answer
   below it needs a profile to read. In practice all four viewsets are `IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly`,
   so an anonymous POST is a 401 before this module is reached; the word exists for
   `GET /api/creation/`, which is `AllowAny` so a signed-out header draws the same menu logic.
2. **staff pass** — `feature_gate`'s own `is_staff` bypass, for its own reason: a moderator has to
   be able to found something in order to see what the restriction does before deciding to flip it.
3. **`minor`** — the older, narrower rule, which answers to no flag at all.
4. **`verification_required`** — last, because it is the only one a moderator can turn off and the
   only one USOS will retire.

`creation_requires_verification` is **inverted** (`is_enabled=True` means the restriction is on)
and is read with plain `is_feature_enabled`, not `feature_gate` — it removes a *rule* from four
endpoints everybody must still reach, which is the shape `age_verification` already has on
registration and `material_uploads_verified_only` on a material version. It fails OPEN, which for
an inverted flag means the restriction HOLDS when the row is missing: the safe direction for an
anti-abuse gate, and a test pins it. `Profile.is_verified_contributor` is the only signal;
`identity/standing.py: ceiling_for` is a different axis and is deliberately not imported here
(standing is a ceiling, never authority).

**One deliberate widening, named rather than slipped in.** `courses` had no minors check at all —
`events`, `services` and `organizations` each did. Because the rule module answers `minor` for every
kind, founding a course is now closed to an under-16 the way hosting an event and listing tutoring
already were. That is a product decision and it is one line to delete if the owner wants it back.

### The frontend: three states, not two

`GET /api/creation/` is asked once per signed-in session by `Header.svelte`, which is mounted for
the whole app, so every page — including a `…/new` page opened directly — reads one answer without
asking again. `lib/state/creation.svelte.ts` keeps **three** states on purpose: allowed, refused
because X, and not-told-yet. Collapsing the third into either of the other two produces a lie on
screen — a "Run a course" button that answers 403 when pressed, or the sentence "new courses are
started by verified contributors" shown to a verified contributor for as long as the request takes.
So before the answer arrives the hub draws neither the button nor the sentence. A signed-OUT reader
is the one exception (`allows()` is true for them): the refusal they would meet is `anonymous`, and
the four `…/new` pages already answer that with a sign-in prompt, which is a better destination than
a missing menu entry.

Surfaces, all of them because house rule 3 is about links rather than pages: the Add… menu's "New
event" and "New listing" (and `hasAnythingToAdd`, so the trigger itself goes when nothing is left),
the four hubs, the four `…/new` pages, and two more found by grep rather than named in the brief —
`/courses/mine`'s own "Run a course" and `CourseContribute`'s "create an event instead". One
component, `CreationGateNote.svelte`, draws the sentence at all eight; it renders nothing unless
there is a real refusal to explain, which is what lets the hubs drop their `isAuthenticated`
wrappers.

### What this cost the existing suites, and why that is in this section

Six suites founded things through the API as ordinary accounts and started answering 403. Each one
now makes its fixture a verified contributor with a comment pointing at `config/creation.py`
(`courses/tests.py`, `events/tests.py`, `services/tests.py`, `services/test_location.py`,
`organizations/tests.py`, one test in `exercises/test_sorting_locale.py`), and
`events/test_permission_matrix.py` has two rows whose answer genuinely changed — `stranger POST
/events/` and `attendee POST /organizations/` go from `201` to `(403, 'verification_required')`.
Writing that down matters more than the edits do: if a seventh suite starts failing with that word,
it is this rule and not a regression in the app under test.

### Verified

`manage.py test config courses events services organizations exercises --keepdb` — **907 tests, OK**.
The first run, before the test edits above, was `config courses events services organizations` →
783 tests, 8 failures and 2 errors, and every single one of the ten was the gate meeting a suite
that founded something through the API; `config services events.test_permission_matrix` went 139
tests OK once they were fixed. `manage.py check` clean, `makemigrations --check --dry-run` → "No
changes detected".
`npm run check` 0 errors / 0 warnings, `npx eslint src e2e/creation-gate.mjs` clean, `npm run build`
green, message key sets identical at 3665 each.

`frontend/e2e/creation-gate.mjs` against real servers on 8136/5236: **57 checks, 0 failures, no
console errors**, run four times — the last against a database whose telemetry log shards had
finally been migrated, because the cycle's worktree recipe copies `db.sqlite3` but not
`backend/logdata/*`, so until then every `AuditEvent` write answered 500 *after* creating its row.
The checks: the endpoint's four callers; ola (ordinary) losing both Add… entries, all four
hub controls and the `/courses/new` form while getting a sentence and a `/levels` link in their
place; kasia (staff) keeping everything with no sentence anywhere; the flag flipped off through the
real API giving ola every control back; and, with the two submission switches off as well, the Add…
trigger itself disappearing. Screenshots looked at, and one change came out of looking: the
organisations hub drew the refusal above its own introduction, so the reader met "you may not" before
"what this is".

### Left open

- **The "request verification" button is a link to `/issues`**, not a flow. There is no "ask to be
  verified" object, so the sentence points at the issue reporter, which is what somebody would use
  today anyway. Named in the brief as left open; it stays left open.
- **No per-kind flag and no grace list.** One switch governs all four kinds. `creation_status`
  deliberately asks the rule per kind rather than fanning one answer out, so the first per-kind rule
  is a change in one module and not a second implementation in the menu.
- **`course_browseEmpty` still says "You could be the first."** on a hub whose create button the
  gate has just removed. The sentence directly above it explains why, but the copy is now slightly
  wrong for a refused reader and the key belongs to `courses`.
- **`hasAnythingToAdd` does not count `canPosts`** — pre-existing, not introduced here: with only
  the `posts` switch on, the Add… trigger disappears while "Write a post" would still be inside it.
  Left alone because fixing it is a behaviour change outside this step's scope.
- **The gate is not shown on `/users/[id]`, `/settings` or anywhere else that merely MENTIONS
  founding.** Only the eight surfaces that offer it carry the sentence.
- **Nothing tells a verified contributor that they are one.** `/levels` explains the idea; the
  profile has no badge for it.
