## 17BR.C. Learning step C — a class is a course a school runs, and a certificate that carries its own basis (2026-10-05)

Branch `learn/c-courses`, from prep `f90e221`; brief `prompts/04-courses-school-mode.md`. Four
things on `courses`, the largest app, and the first of them turned out to need no schema at all.

### School mode is a question asked of `organizations`, not a model

The brief's own instruction ("no new model for 'class' — it is a course run by a school") is
`00-DESIGN.md` §1 rule 1 applied: a link between two surfaces goes through a hub first, and
`organizations.Organization` is the hub that answers *who runs this*. `Organization.kind='school'`
has existed since the management layer and nothing had ever used it. So `courses/rules.py`
asks one question — is there a **`runs`** link from an **active** organisation of kind **`school`**
to this course — and school mode is whatever that answer changes.

It changes exactly two things, both about **staff**, and both `can_curate` rather than
`is_staff_member` (an assistant marks the register):

1. `staff_sees_all_progress` — the register, whatever `progress_visibility` narrows it to;
2. `staff_sees_guardians` — the roster names each pupil's guardians.

A participant's own view is byte-identical in a class and out of one, and neither widening lets
staff *write* a `LessonProgress` row: that is still the participant speaking about themselves, and
a class does not put words in a child's mouth. `supports` deliberately does not count — a faculty
lending its name has not taken responsibility for a roster — and nor does a *university* running a
course, which is the common case and must not acquire a guardian column.

**Three decisions inside that are worth the words they cost.**

*`progress_visibility='off'` is not widened.* The brief says "regardless of `progress_visibility`",
and taken literally that would have included `off`. It should not: the other three modes are
*narrowings* — there is a tracker, and this is who reads how much of it — so a class lifting the
narrowing for its own staff takes nothing from anybody. `off` is different in kind. The field's own
comment in `models.py` says it "blinds staff too… an instructor who turns tracking off has told
their participants nobody is watching", and a school override would quietly make that untrue, for
children, after the fact. A class that wants the register turns tracking on, which is one setting,
already an administrator's to set, and visible to the participants. Written at length in
`staff_sees_all_progress` because it is a deliberate narrowing of the brief.

*The two widenings are one decision but not one rule.* The first draft had `staff_sees_guardians`
call `staff_sees_all_progress`, which was three lines shorter and wrong: a guardian is who a teacher
writes to about a child, which has nothing to do with whether the course keeps a tracker, so a class
with tracking off lost its guardian column for no reason anybody could have explained. They share a
private `_school_staff` helper instead, and a test pins the difference.

*The `organizations` kill switch does not reach school mode.* Turning the organisations surface off
takes away the directory, the panel and the new "run by" line — links as well as pages, house rule
3 — and must not un-school a class in the middle of a term, which would change what a teacher is
shown about a child and what the roster says about them. The flag governs a *surface*; the link is a
fact about the course either way. Said out loud in the module, in `backend/courses/CLAUDE.md` and in
a test, because it is the one place in this step where a flag does less than a reader would expect.

### Performance: one query for every class on the platform

`CourseSerializer` now reports the school on every row, including a fifty-row directory, so
`schools_running_courses()` returns the whole `{course_id: Organization}` map in one query and the
serializer stashes it on the DRF context, which a `ListSerializer` shares with all of its children.
`is_school_course()` is the single-object form for the paths that hold one course. Both read one
`_school_link_queryset()`, because two spellings of "is this a class" is how the roster and the
register would start disagreeing about one child. The honest limit is that the map is loaded whole;
it is bounded by the number of classes every school runs, and the fix the day it is not is a
narrowed query rather than a cache.

### `CourseCompletion` — issued by hand, and carrying its own grounds

One model, one migration (`courses` 0020), `(course, participant)` unique, `revoked_at` rather than
a delete (house rule 12), `issued_by` SET_NULL so a teacher closing their account does not take away
certificates other people are holding.

**It is never derived.** `completion_block_reason` checks "every lesson done" at issue time from
`LessonProgress`, and `completion_note` freezes the count into the row as words — *"6 of 6 lessons,
by the participant's own statements"*. That sentence is the whole honesty of the document: the course
did not measure anybody, the participant said so, and a member of staff put their name to it. It is
also why the count is stored rather than recomputed when the sheet is drawn: a week added next term
must not retroactively turn an issued certificate into a lie, and a lesson deleted must not turn it
into "13 of 11". `lessons_total` is sent beside it, live, so a reader who notices the two differ can
see that they differ rather than being shown one number dressed as the other.

**No grade, no mark, no rank** (§4.5 and §5). There is no field for one, and a test asserts that a
client sending `grade`/`mark`/`rank` gets them back in nothing — so adding such a field becomes a
visible decision rather than a quiet one.

Two cases the rules answer that nobody asked about: a course with **no lessons** answers `not_done`
("0 of 0" is vacuously complete and would certify turning up to an empty course), and
`already_issued` counts a **revoked** row, because re-issuing is `revoke`'s inverse and this step
does not build it.

Refusal → status, all five words: `not_staff` **404** (this app's own convention for a staff action —
`decide`, `update` and `staff_detail` all answer that way), `not_participant` **400** (the request
named the wrong person and no waiting fixes it), `not_done` / `already_issued` / `already_revoked`
**409** (the world is not what the caller thought). `views._COMPLETION_REFUSAL_STATUS` is the one
map; `frontend/src/lib/utils/labels.ts` has a sentence for each and names `rules.py` back.

**The bug a test found, and would not have been found by reading.** `CourseCompletionViewSet` first
scoped its queryset by `_visible_courses` alone — "listed, or run by you, or enrolled in by you".
A test written to prove the issuer keeps reading what they signed failed with a 404, and the same
hole was worse one step over: a private class is exactly what a school runs, so a **pupil who leaves
a class lost their own certificate** the moment their enrolment ended — at the one moment they are
most likely to want to show it to somebody. `get_queryset` now admits the caller's own rows and the
ones they issued as well, and `can_read_completion` is still the object-level half that decides who
may read one (house rule 4 wants both, and here the filter was the half that was wrong).

The printed sheet is the volunteer certificate's posture, copied deliberately and in full: bilingual
**on one sheet** (the holder may hand it to a Polish school office while reading the English
interface), the browser makes the PDF, and it says in both languages that it is unsigned, that EdMat
has no standing to certify anybody, and that it carries no grade. A withdrawn certificate still
resolves — that is what the tombstone is for — and says so, outside the sheet and inside it.

### Lesson → deck, against a mocked endpoint

"Make a deck from this week" sits beside each session's heading, behind `flashcards`, for **staff and
participants alike**: a deck made from this week's exercises is a study aid and whoever is studying
should be able to make one. What differs is the *placement* — only staff attempt to hang the deck on
the course, because placing something on a course is a curatorial act the API refuses for anybody
else with its own word, and a participant getting a private deck is the honest outcome.
`lessonExerciseIds` reads the course payload the page already holds (the lesson's exercise items,
then every linked set's visible rows, deduplicated, in the order drawn) rather than asking again:
the server has already decided what this viewer may see, and an unpublished exercise is already gone
from it. The flag is read from the store rather than wrapped in `FeatureGate`, which renders an
"unavailable" notice — right for a route, wrong for a control inside somebody else's lesson (the
`VenuePanel` precedent).

`POST /api/decks/` belongs to learning step A and **404s on this branch**, so `e2e/school-mode.mjs`
mocks it with `page.route` and says so twice in its own output, per `prompts/README.md` §9. What that
verifies is C's half — that the button is there behind the flag, that it sends the lesson as `source`,
the course as `placement` and exactly the lesson's exercise ids in order — and the call itself is
verified at integration. The `/flashcards/[id]` link the result offers is A's route too; it is
asserted to exist and deliberately not followed.

### `seed_school_demo` — one lived-in school

`testing/school_demo.py` plus a thin command, `seed_conference_demo`'s shape down to both of the
promises that module makes about itself, because this seed can run on the live database and the
reasoning is identical: every seeded course and the school carry `FAKE_PREFIX` (imported, never
re-spelled — two seeders writing the marker differently is what makes "is this real?" unanswerable),
and `assert_contained()` runs **inside the build's transaction** over its own hand-maintained
`CONTAINMENT_MODELS`, so a build that cannot keep the promise leaves nothing behind.

What it builds: a school, a head teacher who owns the body and a teacher who administers it (two
people, because an organisation with one owner is the single point of failure `organizations/work.py`
reports — a demo producing that warning row demonstrates the warning rather than the school), two
classes with **different `progress_visibility` on purpose** so the widening can be compared side by
side, twelve pupils, eleven of them minors made the way the guardian flow makes one, nine families
including a sibling pair sharing a guardian and one pupil with two, **one pupil who has turned
sixteen and therefore has no guardianship at all** — the row that proves the roster reports an
absence rather than drawing nothing — forty-four progress statements, twenty exercises filed from
whatever the corpus holds, and one certificate.

It **checks what it is about to write against the real rules**, which is `conference_demo`'s habit
with its rota: `completion_block_reason` before the certificate and `progress_writable_by` before
each statement, so a hand-edited plan fails the command rather than seeding data the API would have
refused. Idempotent by rebuild (accounts, school, classes and enrolments `update_or_create`d;
chapters, lessons, filed items, statements and the certificate deleted and rebuilt) — and the items
are deleted *before* the chapters, because `CourseItem.lesson` is SET_NULL and deleting the chapters
alone leaves a loose pile of unfiled exercises behind on every re-run. `remove_school_demo` deletes
the organisation links by hand, because a `GenericForeignKey` has no cascade and a link row pointing
at a deleted course would be dropped silently by `_readable_links` on every page — a tidy-looking
leak rather than a visible one.

### Also

**"Run by &lt;organisation&gt;"** is now on the course page, for every course with a `runs` or
`supports` link from any kind of body. `getNodeOrganizations` has existed since the management layer
and was wired nowhere; the line distinguishes the two kinds, because a badge that could not tell
"this is ours" from "we are behind it" would be read as the stronger claim every time.

**`courses/record.py: activity_by_branch(user)`** → `{branch_id: {'lessons_done': n}}`, the shape
step B's registry consumes; the integrator registers it and this app never imports `identity/`.
Counts only, grouped by `Course.subjects`, and a lesson counts once per branch its course claims —
picking one branch per course would be the server inventing a primary subject the course never
declared.

### Verified

From the worktree, on ports 8133/5233:

- `manage.py test courses organizations config --keepdb` — see the board entry for the count; the
  new file is `courses/test_school_mode.py` (**58 tests**, refusal-weighted: the two widenings and
  their controls, `off` and `supports` and a university and a dissolved school all answering no,
  the guardian column reaching staff of a class and nobody else, a revoked guardianship reporting
  an absence, every one of the five refusal words with its own status, a stranger and a classmate
  both getting 404 on a certificate, revoking twice, a school leaver keeping their own, the branch
  record, and the seeder — built twice, containment refusing both an outside `CourseStaff` row and
  an `is_staff` flag, and `--reset`).
- `manage.py check` clean; `makemigrations --check --dry-run` — no changes detected.
- `seed_school_demo`, then again, then `--reset`, then again: idempotent, one of everything, the
  password printed, containment reporting 25 accounts over 8 authority surfaces.
- `npm run check` — **6022 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings**; `npm run build` clean (adapter-static).
- `npm run lint` — my files formatted and eslint-clean; the pre-existing failures are below.
- `e2e/school-mode.mjs` against both real servers, screenshots looked at.

### What the screenshots found (house rule 2)

Three things, none of which any assertion caught, and two of which were in my own work:

1. **The certificate printed a BLANK PAGE.** `lib/styles/_print.scss` is imported by `global.scss`
   and is therefore site-wide: `@media print { body * { visibility: hidden } .print-area,
   .print-area * { visibility: visible } }`. Anything not inside a `.print-area` simply is not
   there on paper. The e2e's "print: the controls are hidden" check passed — correctly — against a
   sheet that printed nothing at all, because the controls *were* hidden and the text *was* in the
   DOM. Fixed with the class, plus two checks that assert the sheet is still visible and its
   heading still has a box, so it cannot come back quietly.
2. **The course header said "Run by" twice, one line apart, meaning two different things.**
   `course_byInstructorPrefix` is "Run by" / "Prowadzi" and names the PERSON; my new line was
   worded identically in both catalogues and named the ORGANISATION, so the page read "Run by
   Barbara Nowakowska / Run by TEST=FAKE Szkoła Podstawowa nr 148". Now "Organised by" /
   "Organizator:", with an e2e check that both lines are present and different.
3. **The seeded classes had no dates**, so the certificate's "Termin / Dates" row was absent and
   the sheet read as undated. `TERM_STARTS_ON`/`TERM_ENDS_ON` are a fixed Polish school year rather
   than "now ± n months", because a demo whose term slides cannot be screenshotted twice and give
   the same picture; `conference_demo`'s moving clock exists because a conference *in progress* is
   the interesting state, and a class in progress is not.

### Found outside this step's scope — NOT fixed here

- **Four other printable pages print a blank sheet, for the same reason**, and have since they were
  written: `routes/events/[id]/certificate/` (the volunteer certificate this one's posture was
  copied from), `routes/events/[id]/badges/`, `routes/events/[id]/rota/` and
  `routes/events/[id]/ticket/`. Each has a careful `@media print` block that hides its own chrome,
  and none carries `.print-area`, so the global rule hides the whole body including the thing being
  printed. Only `my-set` and `CloakroomSlip` have the class. The fix is one class per page and the
  check that goes with it; it is four other steps' files and this one did not touch them.
- **Another agent in this cycle killed every `vite` process by pattern**
  (`for pid in $(ps aux | grep -E "vite" ...)`), which took this worktree's dev server down
  mid-run. `prompts/README.md` §5 rule 11 already says to kill by PID; worth restating where
  agents will read it.
- **`npm run lint` is red on the prep commit** — see the last item below.

### Left open

- **`POST /api/decks/` and `/flashcards/[id]` are learning step A's and were mocked / not followed.**
  The integrator verifies the real call and the real link after A merges (`prompts/README.md` §9).
- **No notification when a certificate is issued or withdrawn.** §5 rule 12 forbids a new
  notification type while eight branches are open. It wants two: `course_completion_issued` to the
  holder and `course_completion_revoked` to the holder, both in the `courses` preference category.
- **No re-issue after a revoke.** `already_issued` counts a revoked row, so a certificate withdrawn
  by mistake cannot be replaced without a shell. The right shape is probably an `unrevoke` action
  rather than a second row, since the pair is unique and the holder could not tell two apart.
- **No guardian sign-off on a certificate**, no class timetable, no gradebook — all three named out
  of scope by the brief, the last of them permanently (`00-DESIGN.md` §5).
- **The `/dziennik` demo is still not linked at the data level**, by owner decision. The connection
  this step makes is by example: `seed_school_demo` builds what a school looks like *here*.
- **`seed_school_demo` picks its subject branch from whatever the corpus holds** (preferring a slug
  mentioning physics), so on this dev database two physics classes sit under
  `analiza-matematyczna`. The command prints which branch it chose rather than hiding it.
- **A guardian sees nothing of their child's class.** They are named on the roster to staff and can
  be messaged, but there is no guardian view of a class, which is the obvious next step and is a
  whole surface rather than a field.
- **`npm run lint` still fails on files this work did not touch** — `e2e/decisions.mjs`,
  `e2e/event-shifts.mjs` and `project.inlang/{.meta.json,README.md}` are unformatted, and five e2e
  scripts (`course-claims`, `galleries-and-applications`, `login-return`,
  `material-open-and-titles`, `prerender-check`) carry six eslint errors. All pre-existing on the
  prep commit; `prettier --check` runs first, so the whole command is red regardless of this step.

## 17BR.B. The learning record: what somebody shared, and what they did here (2026-10-05)

Learning step B of the eight-branch learning cycle (`prompts/03-learning-record.md`, from prep
`f90e221`). One new section on a public profile, and the one rule that shapes all of it is
`prompts/00-DESIGN.md` §1 rule 3: **an EdMat activity count is never drawn beside an institutional
grade as if it were one.** EdMat does not assess anybody, and a table with a "score" column holding
both "3.5 in Analiza Matematyczna" and "5 sets built in Analiza Matematyczna" would quietly claim
that it does.

So the record is two blocks that cannot be concatenated by accident — computed separately, gated
separately, and handed to the frontend as two lists with no column in common.

### The shape

`backend/identity/record.py`, a new rule module beside `identity/standing.py` rather than inside it.
`standing.public_view` answers "how much of this person's *institutional* record may a stranger
see", and it is the three education consents itemised; a count of flashcard reviews is not an
institutional record and must not inherit that function's shape, its caller or its gate.

```
learning_record(profile_user, viewer, *, locale) -> None | {
    is_owner, withheld_reason,
    grades:   None | [{branch: {slug, title}, average, count}]     # share_school AND share_grades
    activity: None | [{branch: {slug, title}, sets, lessons_done, cards_reviewed}]  # share_activity
}
```

`taxonomy.Branch` is the hub that makes one per-branch table honest: two different *kinds* of fact
about the same corner of the curriculum, in two blocks, under one subject name.

- **`share_activity`** — the fourth consent of the shape `share_school`/`share_diploma`/
  `share_grades` already established, default `False`, migration `identity/0003_share_activity.py`.
  It joins the other three in `EducationView.patch`'s own loop rather than getting an endpoint of
  its own; they are edited on one screen.
- **A provider registry.** `ACTIVITY_PROVIDERS` + `register_activity_provider(fn)`, each provider
  `Callable[[User], dict[int, dict[str, int]]]` — branch id to metric to count. `sets_by_branch`
  and `lessons_done_by_branch` live in this module because `study` and `courses` had nothing to
  hand and this step owns neither app's schema; anything that measures its own app registers
  itself at app-ready time, so `identity` imports no app that might not be installed. The union of
  metric keys is filled with zeros so one table has one set of columns, and a key no provider
  declared is **added** rather than dropped — silently discarding somebody's measurement is worse
  than an unlabelled column. `register_activity_provider` is idempotent because `ready()` can run
  twice in one process and a provider counted twice is a wrong number that looks like real data.
- **Counts are recounted on every read** (house rule 5), with the honest limit stated in the
  module: nothing caches, so a profile with thousands of rows pays for them on every view.
- **`GET /api/users/{id}/learning-record/`** behind `feature_gate('learning_record')` — a sibling
  path in `identity/urls.py`, not another field on `accounts.UserPublicView`. That response backs
  every byline in the app, and a display-name lookup has no business computing a per-branch
  aggregate over somebody's sets and course progress. It answers **`null`, not 404**, when nothing
  is shared: the account exists and its profile renders, and 404 would say the person does not.
- **`viewer` never widens anything.** Every gate reads the profile owner's own consent. The
  argument exists so the account holder gets the record back with `is_owner` set even when both
  blocks are withheld, and can be told *this is what other people see* — which for an unshared
  record is "nothing". Without it, the one person who needs to know their consents are off would be
  the one person shown no section.
- **A minor's record is never public, whatever the consents say.** `accounts/minors.py` says a
  minor has no public profile; a learning record is a public profile section. The flags are not
  silently rewritten — a guardian may have set them and the account may stop being a minor's — so
  `withheld_reason: 'minor'` says why instead (house rule 6).

### The frontend

`LearningRecordView.svelte` draws two `section.block`s with a rule between them, two headings and
two leads saying what each block is *and is not* — never one table with an average column that
happens to be empty for the EdMat rows, which would read as one measurement with gaps in it. Every
number arrives computed, averages included: they follow rules (ECTS-weighted, and no number at all
for a branch mixing grading scales) that already live in Python, and re-deriving them in the
component is how this figure and `TranscriptView`'s own start disagreeing on one screen.

The row + modal sit at the `learning: learning record (B)` marker on `routes/users/[id]/+page.svelte`,
and the row's summary is built from the two blocks separately — a total would be the one number this
feature exists not to produce. The settings toggle is the fourth checkbox in `EducationPanel.svelte`'s
consent block. **The brief named `EducationModal.svelte`; the three consents actually live in
`EducationPanel.svelte`**, and the modal renders that same component with `embedded` — so the
fourth toggle went where the other three are and appears on both surfaces from one definition.

### The minors fix in `study`

`retrieve` on `ExerciseSetViewSet` is the one `AllowAny` action in `study` — that *is* the "send a
set to a friend" feature — so a shared set was the one surface where a stranger holding a link read
a child's display name, in flat contradiction of `accounts/minors.py`. It shipped unnoticed because
the sharing feature predates the minors regime. `owner_display_name` is now `''` for a minor and
`owner_anonymous` says that it was withheld rather than missing (house rule 6), and the set page
prints `study_anonymousOwner` ("A learner on EdMat") instead and links to no profile. Withheld for
**every** reader including the owner and their guardian: one answer means no second code path for a
cache or an export to get wrong, and the owner of a set already knows whose it is. `owner` (the
numeric id) is untouched, so the owner's own "this set is still private" notice keeps working.

### Two bugs the run found, neither visible to any check

1. **`sets_by_branch` counted a set once per *item* in it.** `ExerciseSetItem.Meta.ordering` is
   `['order']`, and Django adds every ordering column to the SELECT list of a `distinct()` query —
   so the DISTINCT was over (set, branch, **order**). It read 21 sets for an account with five.
   `.order_by()` with no arguments is the fix and is load-bearing, not tidying; `lessons_done_by_branch`
   needed the same for `['-updated_at']`. Caught by asserting an exact number, not a populated-looking
   table (e2e trap 8).
2. **The record was being served from the anonymous read cache.** `/api/users/` is on
   `config/cachemw.py`'s `PUBLIC_PREFIXES` because a public profile is content — but this body is
   decided entirely by a consent and a kill switch, which makes it the control plane in exactly the
   sense `/api/feature-flags/` is, and worse: what goes stale is somebody's decision to stop
   publishing their results. The browser run caught it as an anonymous caller still being served a
   200 record with the switch off while a signed-in one was correctly refused. Excluded by regex
   rather than invalidated on write, for the reason that module's own `/api/feature-flags/`
   paragraph gives — `?lang=` makes one logical record several cached URLs. Pinned by
   `telemetry.tests.AnonymousReadCacheTests.test_the_learning_record_is_never_cached`.

3. **A killed feature went on asking.** `featureFlagsStore.isEnabled` fails OPEN until the first
   `/api/feature-flags/` response lands — right for drawing a link, wrong for firing a request the
   API will refuse — and the record was requested from inside the profile's `load()`, which raced
   that boot request. With the switch off every profile view logged a 403. House rule 3 means a
   killed feature stops *asking*, not merely stops linking, so the request moved into its own
   `$effect` keyed on `isLoaded` with the usual id guard (frontend trap 2), which is the shape
   `routes/tasks/` and `RotaPanel` already use and which the store's own comment asks for.
4. **"Udostępnione przez Osoba ucząca się na EdMat."** The minors fix first fed a neutral stand-in
   into `sharedSet_sharedBy`'s `{name}` slot. That slot holds a proper noun, which does not
   decline — but Polish `przez` governs the accusative, and in English the stand-in started a
   capital letter mid-sentence. `study_anonymousOwner` is now the **whole line** in both
   catalogues. Nothing asserted it; it was visible only in the screenshot.

### Verified

`manage.py test identity study config telemetry --keepdb` — **169 tests, OK** (`identity` 83, up
from 36; `study` 21; `config` 16; `telemetry` the rest, including the cache carve-out's own
`AnonymousReadCacheTests`, 9).
`manage.py check` clean, `makemigrations --check --dry-run` "No changes detected". `npm run check`
**0 errors, 0 warnings** over 6008 files, `npx eslint src` clean, `npm run build` green. Catalogue
key sets identical at 3684 keys each.

`frontend/e2e/learning-record.mjs` against both real servers on `8132`/`5232`, as an anonymous
reader and as a non-staff account: both blocks shared, the `sets` column **recounted
independently** from her sets and those exercises' branches and matching row for row, the two
blocks' row shapes having no column in common, consent withdrawn leaving grades untouched and
activity `null`, a real guardian-created minor's public set showing no name and no profile link,
and the kill switch refusing an anonymous and a non-staff caller while staff keep their tools and
the profile page still renders. **52 checks, 0 failures**, zero console errors. Screenshots in
`e2e/screens/record-*.png`, looked at — which is the only reason bug 4 above was ever found.

### Left open

- **`cards_reviewed` reads 0 everywhere** until step A's `flashcards.record.activity_by_branch` is
  registered. The metric is declared now so the shape is stable before the app exists, and the e2e
  asserts the zeros rather than skipping the column.
- **No time window** ("this term"), no per-course record, and no record on a course roster for
  staff — step C's school mode may want one, and the seam for it is a provider plus a `node`
  argument that `learning_record` does not currently take.
- **Nothing caches the counts**, and `lessons_done_by_branch` reads `courses` on every profile view.
  Stated in the module rather than pre-optimised.
- **No notifications** of any kind on the record.
- **`Course.progress_visibility` is deliberately not consulted** by `lessons_done_by_branch`: that
  setting decides who sees one course's roster progress, while this is the person's own statement
  about themselves, published by their own consent and aggregated to a branch. Worth re-reading if
  step C changes what that field means.
- **KaTeX's webfonts 403 in every learn/* worktree** — `frontend/node_modules` is a symlink, so
  Vite serves them from outside `server.fs.allow`. Dev-server only, reproducible on content that
  predates this branch, and now `frontend/e2e/CLAUDE.md` trap 26; this script filters them by URL
  and prints the count rather than hiding it.
- **The telemetry log shards needed migrating by hand** in this worktree (the prep recipe copied
  `db.sqlite3` but not `backend/logdata/*`), or any write recording an `AuditEvent` 500s *after*
  writing its row. Not caused here and not fixed here beyond the local database — the prep recipe
  is the right place.
- **`npm run lint` is still red on four files this branch never touched** — `e2e/decisions.mjs`,
  `e2e/event-shifts.mjs` and the two generated `project.inlang/` files, all unformatted before this
  branch existed. `prettier --check` runs first, so the whole command fails on them. `npx eslint .`
  separately reports six errors, all in e2e scripts that predate this work (`course-claims`,
  `galleries-and-applications`, `login-return`, `material-open-and-titles`, `prerender-check`);
  nothing this step added appears in either list.

## 17BR.H — The manual: `/about/guide`, eleven chapters, forty-three real screenshots (2026-10-05)

Branch `learn/h-manual`, from the learning-cycle prep `f90e221` (`prompts/01-prep.md`). Step H of
`prompts/00-DESIGN.md`; the brief is `prompts/09-manual.md`.

### What it is

A user manual at `/about/guide`: a hub listing eleven chapters, and one page per chapter at
`/about/guide/<slug>` — `start` `exercises` `submit` `courses` `events` `tutoring` `concepts`
`help` `messages` `moderation` `flashcards`. Every chapter is a list of steps, each step a heading,
one or two paragraphs and — for most of them — **a screenshot of this site actually running**,
taken by `frontend/e2e/guide-screenshots.mjs` against real servers and a seeded database. Forty-three
pictures, 2.2 MB, all of them under `frontend/static/guide/<chapter>/<nn>-<name>.png`.

### Three decisions worth the words

**The pictures are taken, not drawn, and they are taken by a script.** A drawn diagram of a screen
goes stale silently; a screenshot goes stale loudly, the next time the script runs. The script is
the deliverable as much as the pictures are: `ONLY=exercises node e2e/guide-screenshots.mjs`
re-takes one chapter after a UI change. Step G's showcase pages make the opposite trade on purpose
— they draw the real components from sample data, so they never go stale at all, and they show
designs that do not exist yet. The manual shows what is there; the showcase shows what is meant.

**One set of pictures, of the ENGLISH interface.** The Polish chapter text describes the same
screens and its screenshot `alt` text is Polish. A second set would double `static/guide/` — which
`npm run build` copies verbatim into the deploy bundle — to tell a reader who can already see which
button is which what that button is called in their own language. Named as a cost, not hidden.

**A chapter about a switched-off feature is labelled, not removed.** House rule 3 is about *links
to* a feature; a page of prose describing one is not a link, and a reader is entitled to know what
the software does even on a deployment where it is off. The hub and the chapter say so instead.

### How the content is held

`lib/content/guide/`: `types.ts`, one file per chapter with an `EN` and a `PL` const and a
`…ChapterFor(locale)` resolver, and `index.ts` with `GUIDE_CHAPTERS` (slug, `titleFor`, `docFor`,
`blurbFor`, the kill switch, an optional `showcase` path into step G's pages) plus the hub's own
text. That is the fourth use of the deliberate exception `content/privacy.ts` opened — long-form
writing lives in one file in both languages, because a reviewer cannot tell whether the two have
drifted when they are scattered across sixty catalogue keys. Only the chrome is in the catalogues,
twelve keys under `guide_`.

Routes: `/about/guide` (hub) and `/about/guide/[chapter]` — **one dynamic route, not eleven
directories**, because every chapter is the same page with different text. The twelve addresses are
listed in `svelte.config.js`'s `prerender.entries`; a dynamic route is exactly the case the
prerenderer cannot enumerate by itself. `npm run build` writes `about/guide.html` and
`about/guide/<slug>.html` for all eleven.

### Three things the build and the browser taught

**Vite serves nothing outside its workspace root, and a worktree's `node_modules` is a symlink.**
Every page with mathematics logged a 403 for KaTeX's own fonts (`/@fs/.../katex/dist/fonts/…`) and
drew the formulas in a fallback face — on the dev server only, because production bundles the
fonts. The first run of the screenshot script logged 74 console errors and photographed
wrong-looking mathematics. `vite.config.ts` now allows the real path of the shared `node_modules`
alongside `searchForWorkspaceRoot(process.cwd())`; the next run logged **1**. Found by the
integrator on step G's branch and applied here before any picture was kept.

**`boundingBox()` is viewport-relative.** Clipping a screenshot to a region measured after a click
that scrolled the page photographs something 600 px away — the submit form's preview panel came out
as its own Topics field. Every measurement now scrolls home first (`rect()`), and so does every
capture, because `fullPage` draws a sticky header wherever the page happens to be scrolled to.

**An idempotency guard has to read the right end of the thing.** The script's "has this demo
message already been sent?" check asked the SENDER's `GET /api/messages/`, which is the signed-in
reader's *inbox* and was empty every time, so five identical messages piled up before a screenshot
showed them. It asks the recipient now.

### Verified

`npm run check` 0 errors / 0 warnings (2348 files). `npx eslint .` clean on everything this branch
wrote. `npm run build` green, with `about/guide.html` and all eleven `about/guide/<slug>.html`
present and `build/guide/` carrying the 2.2 MB of pictures. `e2e/guide-screenshots.mjs` against
real servers on 8138/5238: 48 checks, 0 failures, 43 pictures, largest 105 KB, total 2.19 MB
(budget: 400 KB each, 8 MB total). `npm run check:a11y` over the hub and all eleven chapters.
**Every one of the 43 screenshots was looked at**, which is how the three findings below were found.

### Found by looking at the screenshots (written up in `todo.md`, not fixed here)

- **`/needs/new` is not a route.** It falls through to `/needs/[id]` with the id `new` and answers
  "Something went wrong." A need is posted from the `NeedsPanel` on the thing that needs the help,
  which is what the chapter shows instead.
- **The `NeedsPanel` add-form's text inputs and textarea have no border or background** — they are
  invisible against the panel. The selects and the date field are fine.
- **A concept's "Connections" block prints a linked exercise's title as raw LaTeX** in the chip row
  a manager sees, while the same exercise renders correctly as a card lower down the page.

### Left open

- **No Polish-UI screenshots.** The cost is the whole of `static/guide/` again, ~2.2 MB in the
  deploy bundle, for pictures whose only difference is the button labels.
- **No video, and no search over the manual.** Eleven chapters is a list, not a corpus.
- **Six surfaces have no chapter**, and the hub says which: flashcards (step A, this cycle), the
  learning record (step B), co-authoring, the management layer (organisations, tasks, plans,
  decisions, work), the conference desks (tickets, cloakroom, shifts, venues), and the activity
  feed with reporting and the legal notice channel.
- **The flashcards chapter is a placeholder** until step A has merged. Replacing it is
  self-contained: steps in both languages in `lib/content/guide/flashcards.ts`, a
  `chapters.flashcards` block in the screenshot script, and dropping `pending` from the entry.
- **The screenshot script leaves marks on the database it runs against.** It posts one exercise
  submission per run (that is the only way to photograph what the form says afterwards, and it is
  what gives the moderation chapter a real pending row), and it makes the seeded course "Analiza od
  zera" public, books an hour with a seeded tutor and posts one help-wanted row — all idempotent
  except the submission. Reject the spares from `/moderation` if they pile up.
- **Leftover rows from earlier browser runs are hidden, not deleted.** `hideScratch()` masks
  `asdasd`, `Linking check …`, `Published hours …` and friends before each shot, which is the
  brief's "crop or mask anything else". A fresh database would not need it.
- **The showcase links carry `rel="external"`** so the prerenderer does not crawl into step G's
  not-yet-merged `/about/<feature>` pages and fail the build. The integrator may drop that attribute
  once they exist.

## 17BR.A — Flashcards: decks, SM-2 review and placements (2026-10-05, `learn/a-flashcards`)

Learning cycle step A (`prompts/00-DESIGN.md`, `prompts/02-flashcards.md`), from prep `f90e221`.
The thirty-fifth app, `flashcards`: **decks** of **cards**, a **per-person SM-2 schedule**, a review
screen, and **placements** that put a deck on a course or an event. It is also the app steps C, D
and E build against — their "make a deck from this lesson / session / concept" buttons all call one
endpoint of this app's, whose shape was fixed in the brief before any of it existed.

### The four decisions

**Placement is this cycle's sharing mechanism.** `00-DESIGN.md` §4.1 said decks are private only.
Read literally that would have made C's and E's buttons produce decks nobody but their maker could
open — a feature that does nothing. So the integrator decided at launch (`prompts/README.md` §9)
that a deck **placed** on a node is studyable by everybody who can view that node, while `is_public`
(world-readable) stays off by default and closed to minors. A public deck *library* is the next
step. `rules.can_study` has exactly three answers — owner, public, or a placement on a viewable node
— and `rules.can_edit` has one: the owner.

**That gap is the whole permission model.** A participant who tries to rename the deck their
lecturer placed gets **404**, not 403: the queryset let them *see* it because it is on their course,
and "you may look but not touch" is not something this API says about a deck. The honest answer to
"can I change this" is `POST /api/decks/{id}/copy/` — a private copy they own, a membership snapshot
with no placements. A placement is a course's decision to point at somebody's deck, never a
transfer.

**A deck is a snapshot, not a link.** `courses.LessonExerciseSet` already documented this shape and
every word of its reasoning carried over: the card list is copied once, each card's exercise or
concept is a live FK, and a later edit to the source set does not rewrite somebody's homework.
`Deck.source_set` is `SET_NULL` for the same reason that model's is.

**The schedule is a measurement, so it is private by construction.** `ReviewState` is unique per
`(user, card)` and no endpoint answers with somebody else's row; `ReviewLog` is append-only and read
back only in aggregate, per `taxonomy.Branch`, through `record.py` behind step B's consent flag.
Two people studying one placed deck provably keep two schedules — there is a test for it, because
one shared row is exactly the bug this model shape exists to make impossible.

### SM-2 as one pure function

`scheduling.review(state, grade, now) -> state`: plain dicts, no queries, no models, no clock of its
own. That is what let the algorithm be tested as a **table of grade sequences against expected
intervals** rather than through an endpoint. Four grades (again / hard / good / easy) map onto the
paper's six with two deliberate departures, both written down where the code is: **a lapse is due
again immediately** (interval 0), because somebody pressing "again" means "show me again", not
"tomorrow" — and it is also why the review queue is safe to re-request, being recomputed rather than
held; and the **ease factor is clamped to [1.3, 3.0]**, because a run of "easy" on an unclamped ease
schedules a card years out, which is a deletion with extra steps. "Due" is the server's day, because
there is no per-account timezone on this site and half-day precision nobody can act on would be a
lie dressed as rigour.

`rules.apply_grade` is the only writer: one `update_or_create` and one insert in a short `atomic()`,
no `select_for_update` (`backend/CLAUDE.md` rule 1). There is nothing to lock against — the row's
only writer is the person it belongs to.

### What the exercise card does NOT carry

It does not store or inline the statement. The review screen loads a deck's exercises in **one**
request through `GET /api/exercises/bulk/?ids=`, the endpoint already built for this shape of caller
(My Set's PDF export is the other one), which already asks `exercises/entries.py: visible_entries`
for the hint and solution pool. A second resolve in `flashcards` would have been the
two-surfaces-disagree failure the rule-module boundary exists to prevent, and a 50-card response
would have carried fifty statements for a screen that shows one at a time. A **concept** card is the
other way round — its faces are two short strings from `concepts/resolve.py`, so inlining them saves
the review screen a second endpoint and costs nothing.

`rules.visible_cards` skips an exercise a moderator has pulled, and keeps showing it to the deck's
OWNER — `courses.LessonExerciseSet.visible_exercises`'s rule, for its reason: a curator who cannot
see the gap cannot fill it. The card row is never deleted for it.

### Found by running it

- **`npm run check` reported 356 errors on a clean worktree** before a single line of this app was
  written: `src/lib/paraglide/` is generated and gitignored, so a fresh worktree has no compiled
  messages at all and every `$lib/paraglide/messages.js` import fails. One
  `npx paraglide-js compile` fixed it. Worth knowing for the other seven branches of this cycle.
- **The e2e's first kill-switch check passed against a page that said "Loading…".** It asserted
  "no `.decks-panel`" on a course page whose course had not arrived yet — a vacuous pass of exactly
  the kind `e2e/CLAUDE.md` trap 8 warns about, and visible in one glance at the screenshot. It now
  waits for the course's own `h1` first, and a `5b` section asserts the account-menu entry is
  **present** with the switch on, because a kill-switch check that never saw the link proves nothing.
- **Sign-in timed out until the script waited for the layout's own `/feature-flags/` request.**
  Filling the form before the bundle hydrates submits it natively and goes nowhere (trap 25).
- **KaTeX's fonts 403 on every dev server in a worktree.** `frontend/node_modules` is a symlink to
  the main checkout (`prompts/README.md` §3), which is outside Vite's `server.fs` allow list, so 30
  font requests are refused per run and maths renders with fallback metrics. Environmental, not a
  product fault — `npm run build` copies them — so the script buckets and *reports* the count rather
  than swallowing "403", which would also swallow a real one.
- **The two placement serializers are not duplication.** One embeds the node (read from inside a
  deck), the other the deck (read from a course page). One carrying both would be a cycle, and a
  client asking for either would get the other.

### Verified

From the worktree, on ports 8131/5231:

- `manage.py test flashcards config --keepdb` — **99 tests, OK** (144 s), of which 64 are this
  app's. The schedule as a table first,
  then every refusal before any happy path: 404 for a stranger and for an anonymous caller, a
  participant refused a rename on **both** PATCH and PUT (the `UpdateModelMixin` hole that shipped
  once in `needs`), the four `place_block_reason` words with `already_placed` as **409** and the
  rest as 403, a minor refused `is_public`, a private node not named in a stranger's read of a
  deck's placements, every endpoint 403 for a non-staff caller with the switch off and the course
  endpoint still working beside it, and the event case proving `config/nodes.py` really dispatches
  rather than `courses` being special-cased.
- `manage.py check` — 0 issues. `makemigrations --check --dry-run` — no changes (one migration,
  `flashcards/0001_initial`).
- `npm run check` — **0 errors, 0 warnings** (2336 files on the final run). `npm run build` —
  clean, 1 m 38 s.
  `npx eslint src/` — clean. Prettier clean over `src/`, `messages/` and `e2e/flashcards.mjs`.
- `node e2e/flashcards.mjs` — **42 checks, 0 failures**, zero console/page errors, seven sections
  and ten screenshots, all looked at. It drives: making a deck from a saved set on `/my-set`;
  `/flashcards` and the deck page; flipping a card with **Space** and grading three on **keys
  1, 3, 4**, after which the API's counts are 1 due / 0 new / 2 scheduled — the numbers SM-2 says,
  with the lapse still due; placing the deck on a course and a **participant** of that course
  opening the course page, seeing the panel and grading a card on their own schedule while the
  owner's is untouched; the switch off taking the panel and the account-menu entry away while the
  course page still renders; phone width with no horizontal overflow; and the Polish default.

### Left open

- **No shared or public deck library**, and no per-Branch browse. `is_public` works; nothing lists.
- **SM-2, not FSRS.** One pure function with one call site, so swapping it is a one-file change.
- **No notification for cards due** — a three-file change (`notifications/services.py`'s
  `_PREFERENCE_FIELD_FOR_TYPE`, the `NOTIFICATION_TYPES` derived from it, and
  `frontend/src/lib/utils/labels.ts`) that eight parallel branches would have collided on.
- **No offline grading**; every grade is a round trip.
- **A concept card is never frozen** — it follows the concept's current revision.
- **Concept and free-text cards contribute nothing to the learning record**, because
  `Concept.branches` is a many-to-many and one review would have to be counted once per branch or
  split between them. Named rather than guessed at.
- **Cards cannot be reordered in the UI.** `PATCH /api/cards/{id}/ {order}` works; there is no
  drag handle on the deck page.
- **`record.py` and `work.py` are registered by nobody on this branch** — the integrator wires them
  (`prompts/10-integration.md`). Both have tests here, so the wiring has a proof already.
- **`npm run lint` does not pass on this branch and did not at `f90e221` either**, in files this
  step never touched: Prettier flags `e2e/decisions.mjs` and `e2e/event-shifts.mjs`, and eslint
  reports six errors across five `e2e/*.mjs` scripts. Reported, not fixed — they are nobody's
  step-A business and fixing them would put unrelated churn in this branch's diff.

## 17BT — The closing cycle: five branches that built nothing new (2026-10-06 → 07)

The fourth parallel build and the first one with no prep commit, because nothing was registered,
flagged or migrated: the five steps below closed the two "left open" blocks `todo.md` carried after
the learning cycle (§17BR) and the standing-page discussions (§17BS). `prompts/11-closing-design.md`
is the design — its §4 per-file ownership table was the cycle's one new rule and held: the only
three files two steps both needed (`events/test_permission_matrix.py`, `community/test_discussions.py`
and their `databases` line) were routed to one owner each, and the merged tree's
`testing/check_databases_declared.py` prints **0**. Briefs `12`–`16`, integration `17`, all five
agents on Opus 5, launched from the orchestrating session and cut from `490c195` (`4a57d6d` plus
the briefs). Each step's own section follows, in merge order.

**Merged as they landed** (owner's instruction mid-cycle, replacing the C, D, B, E, A order the brief
chose for conflict-smallness): E `4d1f209` → `25aeb5f`, D `1e2d775`+`e5ddf81` → `bc753a2`,
B `a2eabd3` → `0d42d5a`, C `06a6d05` → `eafef7c`, A `ac2bf0f` → `87001af`. Every conflict was
`HISTORY.md` "both appended", resolved by union; `test.md` auto-merged four times without
duplicating a paragraph; no catalogue or `labels.ts` conflict at all (E added three keys, nobody
else added any; 3931 keys, identical sets). No branch added a migration. Before each merge the
branch's own numbers were re-run on its worktree: E 131 community tests, D 64 flashcards, B 85
identity + matrix, all OK with zero request-log tracebacks on the fixed classes.

**The three numbers the cycle is judged on** (`11-closing-design.md` §8), measured on the merged
tree with the machine otherwise idle:

1. `manage.py test --parallel 4 --keepdb` **completes**: 2700 tests, OK, **20 min 59 s** wall-clock
   (12 min 43 s of tests, the rest building ten in-memory databases), **198 lines** of output and
   zero `Failed to write a request log row` — against a serial run of ~52 min and tens of thousands
   of traceback lines the week before.
2. `npm run lint` is **clean over the whole tree** (Prettier + eslint), so it is a gate now;
   `npm run check` 6340 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings; `npm run build` clean; `check:katex` 2254 rows,
   0 issues.
3. `npm run check:a11y` audited **48 pages, 0 load problems, 0 violations on all nineteen new pages**
   (the manual's twelve, the showcase's seven). Its three findings are older and elsewhere —
   `heading-order` on `/events` and `/tutoring`, `color-contrast` on `.badge--waiting` at
   `/material-projects?tab=mine` — and are on the board.

Browser scripts on the main checkout's servers (8000 / 5173): `flashcards.mjs` 43/0,
`about-discussions.mjs` 35/0 with the exact count, `guide-screenshots.mjs` 63/0 (50 pictures,
2.39 MB; the re-taken set was byte-different and visually the same, so only C's seven are
committed, as C decided), `learning-record.mjs` 52/0, `about-page.mjs` 15/0. The learning record on
the merged tree: `ACTIVITY_PROVIDERS` is exactly `sets_by_branch`, `courses.record.activity_by_branch`,
`flashcards.record.activity_by_branch` — one `lessons_done`, as B verified on its branch.

**What integration found, so nobody relearns it:**

- **A hand-started `runserver` has no CORS origin.** `run.sh` exports
  `DJANGO_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` for the Vite port; a bare `manage.py runserver` does not, so every
  browser call is blocked and a script dies as a `waitForSelector` timeout that looks exactly like a
  code bug. Found by E, passed to the others mid-cycle; every browser run above set it.
- **`check:a11y` takes `--base`/`--api` arguments, not `E2E_BASE`.** Run with the environment
  variable alone it audits the default port, finds nothing listening and reports every page as a
  load problem. The first integration run did exactly that; the numbers above are the second.
- **`about-page.mjs` had been red since §17BQ** (eight cards asserted, eight `<h2>`s on the page
  then, nine and ten now — §17BR.G said "the integrator should set that number once" and the
  learning cycle's integrator did not). Set to the page on 2026-10-07: nine cards, eight with
  tutoring off, ten `<h2>`. The script's own labels had said "seven remain" over an assertion of
  eight.
- **`learning-record.mjs` fails on a database where `seed_profile_showcase` has not been re-run
  after the courses step** (the joined course has no subjects, so the provider answers nothing); B hit
  the same on its copy. Re-running the command is the fix, not the code.
- **Clearing `backend/cachedata/*` under a running backend can 500 the next anonymous list read**
  (`OSError: Stale file handle`) — found by C and D independently; stop the backend first.
- **Five agents plus a parallel suite can fill this machine's root filesystem.** A's first
  `--parallel` run lost six tests to `No space left on device` in `mkdtemp` media roots; its
  second run and the integration run had the disk to themselves.
- **The parallel suite's wall-clock is a shared-machine number twice over**: A measured 24½ min with
  four agents beside it, integration 21 min alone. `--keepdb` keeps nothing here (in-memory
  SQLite test databases), so ~9 min of every run is the build; A named the `TEST['NAME']` trade
  and nobody has taken it.

**Left open by the integration itself:** the pre-existing a11y findings above; the orphaned
`e2e/screens/about-discussions-4-moderation.png` E named; the footer printing the site's name twice
(C, from a screenshot); the `decks_includeHint` / `decks_includeSolution` keys with no control
(C); the three "make a deck" buttons never driven against the real `POST /api/decks/` (D); the
plural-free count strings site-wide (D); `/flashcards` signed out not linking to `/login` (D);
