## 17BT.E — Discussions: an exact count, a link to the held, and no row for a key nobody will read (2026-10-06)

`prompts/16-discussions.md`, branch `close/e-discussions`, cut from `490c195`. Three of §17BS's six
left-opens were engineering rather than product, and this is them, plus the two one-line debts the
cycle's ownership table routed here. No migration: none of the three changes touches a model.

### 1. The browser script asserts an exact count, because it now clears up after itself

`about-discussions.mjs:188–191` asserted "a count ≥ 1" because the script left its comments behind
and `todo.md` asked for a delete endpoint. House rule 12 forbids the hard delete that bullet wanted,
so the first thing to establish was what the collapsed line's number actually counts.

It turned out to be two different numbers depending on whether the thread had been opened. Before a
click it is `policy.commentCount`, from `DiscussionPolicyView`, which has always counted public
comments only — `is_removed=False, auto_hidden_at IS NULL`. After a click
`SectionDiscussion.svelte` replaced it with `thread.comments.length`, and the thread deliberately
carries tombstones (so a thread whose middle was removed keeps its shape) and, for staff and for
their own author, rows that are still held. So the same line could read "(1)" collapsed and "(3)"
open, with two of the three being a placeholder and a thing waiting for a moderator.

`publicCount()` in the component is the fix — one definition, used in both places the count is set
— and the reason is written into `discussions.py` under "What \"N comments\" counts", because it is
the third place that number is printed and the next person to add a fourth will look there.

With tombstones out of the count, **no new endpoint was needed**. The script's signed-in comment is
deleted by its own author through `DELETE /api/comments/{id}/`, which tombstones it; its anonymous
comment was *held*, so it was never public and never counted, and staff remove it through the
report queue `accounts.minors.hold_for_review` already filed for it — the first and second of the
three shapes the brief listed, and the third (a staff-only tombstoning action in `community/views.py`)
was not built. The script reads both counts from the server before it writes anything and asserts
`===` against what it computed.

### 2. "Waiting: 5" is a link

`DiscussionLocationsPanel.svelte` printed the held count as text, so a moderator who could see the
number had to go and find the comments. A held comment IS a report, so the rows are already on the
Reports tab — what was missing was any way to tell which location a reported comment came from.

One additive, read-only key on a report row: **`discussion_location`**, the location key
(`'about/guide/courses#enrolling'`, or `'about'` for a page-level row) when the reported comment's
target is a `DiscussionLocation`, `None` for everything else. `community.discussions.report_location_key`
builds it, so the spelling of a key stays in the app that owns it, and both files say the other
reads it (house rule 13). It costs no query: `build_report_queue` has already bulk-resolved every
reported comment's direct target by the time it asks.

The Reports tab reads `?location=` once at mount, exactly the way it reads `?tab=`, filters its rows
on that field and prints a visible line saying it is filtered with a "show all" button — a filter
nobody can see is a queue that looks empty for no reason. The panel's link is
`/moderation?tab=reports&location=<key>` and carries `data-sveltekit-reload`, because the panel
lives *inside* `/moderation` and a client-side navigation from that route to itself would reuse the
component and never re-run either read-once line.

The filter is client-side, over the queue the tab already fetches whole. `moderation/services.py`
says where that stops being enough: the day one location carries more held comments than a moderator
will scroll past, it wants a real `WHERE` on the endpoint rather than a bigger payload.

### 3. A row is created by a write that succeeds

`DiscussionLocation` rows are lazy, and the POST created one *one line above* the parent check that
needs it — so a reply naming a comment in another thread was refused 400 and still left a location
behind, which a moderator then found in the list with no comments under it. The row is now resolved
with `create=False`, every refusal happens, and only then is it created; an absent row is not a
special case, it just means no parent can belong here. A 403 and a malformed body never reached the
creation line and still do not; all three have tests. A *held* comment still creates its row, which
is not the same question — it is stored, and a stored comment needs something to hang off.

What is left over from before that rule, plus the well-formed junk keys `PAGE_RE` permits by design,
is what `manage.py sweep_discussion_locations` removes. A candidate needs all three of: no comments
of any kind (a tombstone is a record that something was said here), default settings, and
`updated_by IS NULL`. The three together are the whole argument that this is not the hard delete
house rule 12 forbids — nobody decided anything about such a row. `--dry-run` prints the candidates
and changes nothing. `DiscussionLocationViewSet` still has no `destroy`, and the command's docstring
says why the two are different questions.

### 4. The two one-liners

`e2e/about-discussions.mjs` was the one file in the tree Prettier rejected, so `npm run lint` is now
clean over the whole tree — the second of the three numbers this cycle is judged on
(`prompts/11-closing-design.md` §8). And both `test_discussions.py` classes now declare
`databases = set(all_log_shards()) | {'default'}`, which step A's sweep skipped on purpose.

### Verified

From `/Projects/edmat/.claude/worktrees/close-e-discussions/`, servers on 8145 / 5245, Node 24.

- `manage.py test community.test_discussions` — **55 tests, OK** (42 before; 13 new). Both classes
  in the file now declare `databases`, and neither they nor the three new classes print a
  `Failed to write a request log row`.
- `manage.py test community` — **131 tests, OK**. The 47 remaining log-shard tracebacks all come
  from five classes in `community/tests.py` (`CommentTests`, `CommentVoteTests`,
  `CommentEditDeleteTests`, `ReviewTests`, `ReviewReplyTests`), which is step A's file, not this
  one's; named here so nobody looks for them in `test_discussions.py`.
- `manage.py check` — no issues. `manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` — **no changes
  detected**. No migration, as the brief predicted.
- `manage.py sweep_discussion_locations --dry-run` on the development database — `4 discussion
  location(s); 0 candidate(s).` All four are `about#…` rows the browser script created through the
  moderator API, so every one of them has `updated_by` set: the "somebody decided this" condition
  refusing to delete, on real data. Driven end to end as well, by hand: a junk row
  `about/nonsense#sweepme` was created, listed by `--dry-run` (which removed nothing), removed by
  the bare command, and the next `--dry-run` was back to `4 … 0 candidate(s)`.
- `e2e/about-discussions.mjs` — **35 passed, 0 failed, 0 console/page errors** (25 checks before;
  0 KaTeX webfont 403s needed suppressing on this run, and the counter prints the number either
  way). The count assertion is now `=== missionBefore + 1`; the script's own two comments are gone
  at the end, confirmed by an authenticated re-query **by id** rather than by text, because runs
  from before this change left comments with the same words at the same locations.
  Screenshots: `about-discussions-1-anon-open.png`, `-2-thread-and-refusal.png`, `-3-flag-off.png`,
  and two new ones, `-4-held-count-link.png` (the panel, "Oczekujące: 1" drawn as a link) and
  `-5-reports-filtered.png` (the Reports tab showing one row and the line
  "Pokazane są tylko komentarze oczekujące w about#origin. pokaż wszystkie zgłoszenia").
- `npm run check` — **0 errors, 0 warnings** (2412 files). `npm run build` — clean.
  `npm run lint` — **clean over the whole tree**, which it has not been for some time.
- Both catalogues: 3931 keys each, key sets identical, the three new `discussions_*` keys appended
  to the existing contiguous block.

Two things the verification itself taught, both worth writing down:

- **A hand-started `runserver` breaks CORS, and the page looks merely slow.** `run.sh` keeps
  `DJANGO_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` in step with the ports; a worktree agent starting the two servers
  itself does not, and every API call from `localhost:5245` is then refused by the browser. What
  the script reported was `waitForSelector('.section-discussion__toggle')` timing out, which reads
  exactly like a slow dev server — raising the timeout to 60s and re-running "confirmed" it twice.
  Only a console dump named it. Start the backend with
  `DJANGO_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS="http://localhost:<vite>,http://127.0.0.1:<vite>"`.
- **`svelte/no-navigation-without-resolve` cannot be satisfied by a `resolve()` inside a template
  literal on its own line.** `eslint-disable-next-line` covers the line the `<a>` opens on, not
  the `href=` three lines down where the rule reports, so the one-line form other call sites use
  (`ArticlePool`, `TagChip`) silently does not transfer to a multi-attribute anchor. The block
  form (`<!-- eslint-disable … -->` / `<!-- eslint-enable … -->`) is what works.

### Left open

- **An anonymous writer still sees their own held comment exactly once**, in the response to their
  own POST. `todo.md` bullet 2, unchanged: a signed cookie would fix it and that is a decision
  about tracking visitors, not a bug to fix quietly.
- **One thread per manual chapter, not one per step** (bullet 4) and **`/privacy`, `/levels` and
  `/legal` have no discussions** (bullet 5) — both product decisions nobody has taken; left.
- **No server-side `?location=` filter on the moderation queue.** The Reports tab filters
  client-side over the additive field, which is enough while a standing page produces single
  digits and the tab fetches the whole queue anyway for its counts. It stops being enough when one
  location carries more held comments than fit in a payload a moderator waits for — at that point
  it wants a real `WHERE` on `ModerationQueueView`, not a bigger response.
- **No new notification type** when a comment is held at a location a moderator looks after
  (`prompts/README.md` §5 rule 12). The one I wanted was "a held comment is waiting at a page you
  switched to `anyone`".
- **The sweep is a command, not a schedule.** Nothing runs it; it is for after a bulk change or
  when the moderator's list looks longer than it should. A cron entry is a deployment decision.
- **`community/tests.py` still lacks `databases` on five classes**, so `manage.py test community`
  still prints tracebacks. That file is step A's by the cycle's ownership table and this step did
  not touch it.
- **Two files in `frontend/project.inlang/` are now in `.prettierignore`.** `paraglide-js compile`
  writes `.meta.json` and `README.md`, both already gitignored, and a newer compiler formats them
  differently from the copies sitting in older checkouts — so any worktree that recompiled failed
  `npm run lint` on two files nobody wrote. Ignoring them is what makes "lint is clean" a property
  of the repository rather than of whether you happened to run the compiler.
- **`frontend/e2e/screens/about-discussions-4-moderation.png` is now orphaned** — no script writes
  that name any more (the two new screenshots are `-4-held-count-link` and `-5-reports-filtered`).
  Left in place rather than deleted in a commit about something else.

## 17BT.D — The browser pass: running what had only ever been written (2026-10-06, `close/d-browser-pass`)

Closing step D, `prompts/15-browser-pass.md`. The learning cycle shipped two browser scripts and
nineteen new pages and ran none of them; `todo.md` bullet 5 said so out loud, and added that no
green `svelte-check`, suite or build above it was a substitute. House rule 2 in one step: run
`e2e/flashcards.mjs` and `npm run check:a11y` for the first time, **look at the screenshots**, and
fix what that finds in the one app and the seven showcase pages nobody else is in this cycle.

### What the first run found: three script faults, one app fault, no backend fault

The script failed on its first real run and lied twice before failing. All three of those were the
script — which is the expected shape, because it was written on `learn/a-flashcards` beside an app
that was still being built, against shapes rather than against a server:

1. **429 at the eighth sign-in.** `POST /api/auth/login/` is throttled **10/min per IP**
   (`accounts/throttles.py`, `config/settings.py: 'login'`). Three `tokenFor` calls plus one
   browser sign-in per section is eleven inside a minute on a warm dev server, so section 6 died
   in `waitForURL` — and a sign-in that times out reads exactly like a broken login page, which is
   `e2e/CLAUDE.md` trap 1 wearing a different endpoint's clothes. Clearing `cachedata/` does not
   help; the run refills the counter itself. The form is now driven **once per account** and every
   later context starts from that account's saved `storageState`. That is not a test-only
   shortcut: the token lives in `localStorage` (`lib/state/token.svelte.ts`), so it is precisely
   the session a signed-in person has on their next page load, and the form itself is still
   driven for real. It needed one companion, `open()`, which waits for the root layout's own
   `/feature-flags/` request before anything is clicked — restoring a session skips the sign-in
   navigation that used to give the bundle time to hydrate (trap 25).

2. **"the deck page lists the placement" was vacuous** (trap 8). It waited for a `.panel`
   containing the course's title — and the "Where this deck is placed" panel contains the SELECT
   whose chosen option is that same title, so it matched the instant the option was picked, before
   the POST. The check passed and the screenshot it then took showed **"Not placed anywhere."**
   Nothing asserted the bug; it was found by opening `flashcards-4-placed.png` and reading it. The
   app was right all along (`place()` re-reads the deck), and the check is now scoped to the
   placement list and asserts the row's `href`.

3. **"and offers a place-it-somewhere select" counted every `select` on the page**, including the
   header's language picker (trap 6) — a check that would have passed on any page in the app.

With those three fixed: **43 checks, 0 failed, 0 console/page errors**, seven sections, eleven
screenshots, all looked at. `flashcards-4-placed.png` was the informative one, for the reason
above. The 43rd check is new, and it is the app fault:

**The one real bug: `/flashcards/[id]` overflowed 69 px at 390 px wide.** A `<select>` is sized by
its widest option, and two of that page's three selects carry user-supplied titles — a course, an
event, a saved set. `.grow`'s `min-width: 0` does nothing about it, because the select is a grid
item inside the label and its own `min-width` is still `auto`, so it refuses to shrink and the flex
row's `flex-wrap` never gets a chance. On a phone the "Place this deck on a course or an event you
run" row ran off the right edge with the **Place button cut in half** — on a page `check:a11y` had
just called clean, because axe does not look at geometry. Fixed with `width: 100%; min-width: 0`
on the control itself, and pinned by the new check. **No backend bug was found, so
`backend/flashcards/tests.py` is unchanged** and no migration was wanted anywhere.

### `npm run check:a11y`: 48 pages, and the nineteen new ones were already clean

Run for the first time over the cycle's pages. **0 violations of any impact on all seven showcase
pages and all twelve manual pages**, before and after — there was nothing to fix, which is the
honest result and worth recording as one. The run reports `0 had a load problem`, so this is not
the empty-page false negative the script's own `MIN_BODY_TEXT_LENGTH` guard exists to catch.

Three findings elsewhere, all pre-existing and none in this cycle's files, left for whoever owns
them: `heading-order` (moderate) on `/events` and `/tutoring`, where a card's title is an `h3`
under an `h1`; and `color-contrast` (serious) on `.badge--waiting` on `/material-projects?tab=mine`.

### Looking, which is the part no checker does

Forty screenshots: the seven showcase pages and the three `/flashcards` routes, at 1280 px and
390 px, signed out and as `michal@edmat.example`, each with its horizontal overflow, its body-text
length and a raw-LaTeX probe measured alongside. The showcase pages are prerendered sample data and
came out pixel-identical signed in and signed out apart from the header, which is what they should
be. No raw LaTeX anywhere — the look script waits for `.katex` before shooting (trap 26). The one
page that broke was the deck page, above.

Two things that look like faults in a screenshot and are not, checked rather than assumed: the
learning record's two sample tables are **clipped at phone width on purpose** — `RecordBlocks` sets
`min-width: 26rem` and `SampleFrame` is `overflow-x: auto`, with the reasoning in the component
("squeezing 'Cards reviewed' until its numbers are cut off mid-digit looks like broken data rather
than a table that scrolls"); and the review screen's `0 due · 3 new · 0 scheduled` line does not
move while a session runs, which the route's own docstring states as a decision.

### Verified

- `node e2e/flashcards.mjs` on 8144/5244 — **43 checks, 0 failed, 0 console/page errors**. Eleven
  screenshots re-taken and looked at.
- `npm run check:a11y` over 48 pages, 0 with a load problem — **0 violations on the seven showcase
  pages and the manual's twelve**; 1 serious + 2 moderate nodes elsewhere, all pre-existing.
- Forty phone/desktop screenshots of the ten pages this step owns, signed out and signed in, each
  with a measured overflow; 0 px on every one after the fix.
- `manage.py test flashcards --keepdb`, `manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check --dry-run`,
  `npm run check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` — numbers on the board entry.

### Left open

- **The app's count strings do not pluralise**, so `/flashcards` reads "3 cards waiting across
  **1 decks**" in English and "1 fiszek czeka w 1 taliach" in Polish. Not a step-A regression and
  not fixed here: zero of the ~1000 keys in either catalogue use an ICU plural, a few write
  "(s)", so this is a site-wide copy convention and mending `decks_*` alone would make the site
  inconsistent with itself. It wants one decision and one sweep.
- **Signed out, `/flashcards` says "Sign in to keep decks and a review schedule." and does not
  link to `/login`.** A sentence, where every other gated page offers the door.
- **Nobody has driven the three "make a deck" buttons against the real `POST /api/decks/`.** Steps
  C, D and E of the learning cycle each verified their lesson / session / concept button against a
  *mock* and said so (`prompts/README.md` §9); integration never closed that. It is the next
  browser script, not a check to bolt onto this one.
- **`flashcards.mjs` still cannot be run twice in a minute on a fast machine** without the login
  throttle noticing, if anything else on the box is signing in. Five logins per run is under the
  limit with room, not with margin.
- **The three a11y findings above are not mine** and are untouched.
- **`e2e/CLAUDE.md` has no trap for the stale-file-handle 500** that clearing `cachedata/` under a
  running backend produces. It is written in this script's header and in `test.md`; the catalogue
  belongs to no step this cycle, so it was not edited.

## 17BT.B — Seams: one `lessons_done`, and the two matrix rows that never landed (2026-10-06, `close/b-seams`)

Closing step B (`prompts/13-seams.md`). Two small backend edits the learning cycle's integration
left on the board because each one wanted a decision rather than a quiet hand. Both decisions were
taken before the branch was cut (`prompts/11-closing-design.md` §2), so this section is mostly
about what the edits touched and what reading them turned up.

**One implementation of `lessons_done`.** Steps B and C of the learning cycle each wrote a
provider for the same metric, on branches that could not see each other:
`identity.record.lessons_done_by_branch` (read-only over `courses`, registered at the bottom of
`identity/record.py`) and `courses.record.activity_by_branch` (in the app that owns
`LessonProgress`, tested, and deliberately *not* registered). `identity.record._activity_block`
**sums** across providers, so registering both would have doubled every number on every profile —
a wrong count that looks exactly like real data, which is why `identity/apps.py: ready()` had
carried a long docstring explaining that it was leaving the question to the board.

The owner's decision was to keep C's and delete B's: the provider lives where the rows live
(`prompts/README.md` §5 rule 13), and `identity/record.py` now imports no app's models but
`study`'s. Concretely — the function and its `register_activity_provider` line are gone; the module
docstring, which named it four times and explained that it "lives here because `courses` had
nothing to hand", says instead what the shape is and why; `identity/apps.py: ready()` registers
`courses.record.activity_by_branch` beside the flashcards one, and its docstring, which argued at
length for *not* doing this, now says only what is still true (the hook lives in the app that owns
the rows, the integrator wires it, `ready()` runs more than once so the registry is idempotent);
`courses/record.py`'s own docstring says where it is registered rather than that somebody will;
and `accounts/management/commands/seed_profile_showcase.py` points its comment at the survivor.

**Three things worth recording about the deletion.** The survivor's counting is *not* identical
code: B's used `.order_by().values_list(pk, branch).distinct()` and C's is a plain `values_list`
over the many-to-many, but both count one row per (progress, branch) pair, so the numbers agree —
checked against the seeded account rather than assumed. C's guards `AnonymousUser` and `None` and
B's did not; nothing relied on B's raising, because `_activity_block` is only ever reached behind
the profile owner's own `share_activity` consent, and that guard is now documented in the function
rather than left as an unexplained difference. And the label beside the column still says *said
they finished* rather than *completed* in both catalogues: nothing here changes what the number
means.

**The test moved rather than being deleted, and got stronger on the way.** Nothing in
`identity/tests.py` had asserted B's function by name — every test went through the endpoint — so
what was missing was a pin on the *seam* rather than on either implementation.
`test_exactly_one_registered_provider_counts_lessons_done` asks every registered provider what it
answers for an account with one finished lesson and asserts that the list of those that answer
`lessons_done` at all is exactly `['courses.record.activity_by_branch']`. That is the shape of the
failure (two things count this metric) rather than the name of the function that caused it once, so
a second implementation under any name would fail it; and it is why
`grep -rn lessons_done_by_branch backend/` now finds nothing at all, prose included.
`test_only_lessons_somebody_said_they_finished_are_counted` is the other half, unchanged: a lesson
marked done reads `lessons_done: 1` through the endpoint, whichever function counted it.

**The two permission-matrix rows.** `prompts/10-integration.md` §3 asked for six blocks; four
landed. The two that did not are both endpoints where the matrix's usual shape does not quite fit,
and each block says so in its own comment rather than quietly filling a column with the nearest
thing.

`/api/course-completions/{id}/` has **no 403 row, by design**. Every refusal on a certificate is a
404: a 403 would confirm that somebody finished a course, which is the fact the document exists to
carry. So the block pins the holder (200), the issuer-and-course-staff (200), a stranger, an event
attendee and an event *volunteer* — the "staff role that may not" column — all at 404, anonymous at
401 (`IsAuthenticated`), and `revoke` with the word `rules.revoke_block_reason` answers:
`(404, 'not_staff')` for the holder, who keeps the sheet and does not withdraw it. One
`CourseCompletion` was added to `setUpTestData`, written straight to the model because
`POST /courses/{id}/completions/` refuses `not_done` until every lesson is ticked off and this
fixture is about who may read one afterwards.

`/api/creation/` is the opposite problem: **every persona gets 200 and the whole answer is in the
body**, because the Add… menu asks this endpoint what it may draw and must therefore get an answer
for a signed-out reader too. A row that pinned only the status would pass whatever the gate said.
So the row tuple grew an **optional seventh element**, a body predicate `check(data) -> bool`,
documented in the file's header box and checked after the status and the refusal word; `test_matrix`
reads `row[:6]` and `row[6] if len(row) > 6`, so none of the ~700 rows written before it changed.
The six rows pin `anonymous` for a signed-out reader, `minor` for the child, `verification_required`
for three different adult personas — including the organiser, because running an event is not
standing — and `None` for a verified contributor. That last one needed a persona nobody had:
`persona.verified` is a **new** account rather than a tick on an existing one, because `attendee`
is the persona three founding rows above already pin at `(403, 'verification_required')` and
verifying them would have turned those into 201s without anybody noticing.

**And the one-line fix step A could not make.** `PermissionMatrixTests` now declares
`databases = set(all_log_shards()) | {'default'}`, with the same one-sentence comment
`events/tests.py:33` carries. The file is step B's under this cycle's ownership table
(`11-closing-design.md` §4), so the line was step B's to add.

### Verified

- `manage.py test identity courses.test_school_mode events.test_permission_matrix flashcards
  --keepdb` — **207 tests, OK** in 325 s (identity 84; the other three 123), and **zero**
  `Failed to write a request log row` tracebacks and zero tracebacks of any kind in the output,
  which is what the new `databases` line buys.
- `manage.py test events.test_permission_matrix --keepdb` on its own — **1 test** (the table is one
  method over ~700 subtests), OK in 12 s, no log-row traceback.
- `grep -rn lessons_done_by_branch backend/` — **nothing**, exit 1.
- `manage.py check` — 0 issues. `makemigrations --check --dry-run` — **no changes**. No migration:
  nothing here touches a model.
- **By eye, with both servers up on 8142/5242**: signed in as the seeded sharer (`u-kasia`, whom
  `seed_profile_showcase` gives two finished lessons on a course under *Rachunek
  prawdopodobieństwa*; `share_activity` is not set by the command and was switched on for the
  check), her profile's "Historia nauki" modal draws **one** "Ukończone zajęcia" column and the
  number **2** — not 4, and not twice.
  `frontend/e2e/screens/close-b-record-lessons-done-once.png`, looked at.
- The API's own answer beside it, for the same account:
  `[{analiza-matematyczna: sets 5, lessons_done 0, cards_reviewed 0},
  {rachunek-prawdopodobienstwa: sets 3, lessons_done 2, cards_reviewed 0}]`, and
  `ACTIVITY_PROVIDERS` is exactly `['identity.record.sets_by_branch',
  'courses.record.activity_by_branch', 'flashcards.record.activity_by_branch']`.

### Left open

- **The matrix has no verified-contributor rows anywhere else.** `persona.verified` exists now and
  is used by six rows; every other founding row in the table still pins the refusal and not the
  success, so `POST /organizations/`, `POST /events/` and the two course paths are proved to refuse
  an unverified adult and never proved to let a verified one through. Six more rows, not a design
  question — left out because this step's brief says no new rows beyond the two blocks named.
- **`/api/courses/{id}/certificate-*` has no rows because it does not exist**, but the *third*
  completion endpoint does: `POST /api/courses/{id}/completions/`, the issuing action, is pinned
  only at `GET`. Its four refusal words (`not_staff` 404, `not_participant` 400, `not_done` 409,
  `already_issued` 409) are asserted in `courses/test_school_mode.py` and nowhere in the
  cross-persona view. Noticed while reading the view; written on the board rather than added here.
- **No `already_revoked` row.** Pinning the 409 needs a second, pre-revoked `CourseCompletion` in
  the fixture (the unique constraint is over `(course, participant)` with no condition, so it
  cannot be the same pair), and every matrix row is rolled back, so the revoke row above cannot
  set it up for a later one.
- **`test.md` is not updated.** The ownership table gives that file to closing step A, and the two
  new row blocks are inside a suite `test.md` already describes.
- **`seed_profile_showcase` still does not set `share_activity`**, so the account it fills has
  finished lessons and a learning record that nobody but its owner can see until somebody ticks
  the consent by hand. Arguably right — a seed command turning a privacy consent on is its own
  small dishonesty — and arguably why the showcase's own record went unlooked-at until now. Named,
  not changed: it is a product decision and not this step's.

## 17BT.C — The manual's eleventh chapter: flashcards, written against the real screens (2026-10-06, `close/c-manual-flashcards`)

Closing cycle step C (`prompts/14-manual-flashcards.md`), closing `todo.md` "Learning cycle — left
open" bullet 3. `/about/guide`'s eleventh chapter had been the honest placeholder `learn/h-manual`
wrote on 2026-10-05, before the flashcards app existed: it told the reader it was not written yet
and sent them to `/about/flashcards`. The app has existed since `eb6086a`, so the placeholder's own
docstring was now the only thing standing between the manual and a complete table of contents, and
it said exactly what replacing it meant. This is that, and nothing else — no backend change, no
migration, no new catalogue key.

**The chapter.** `frontend/src/lib/content/guide/flashcards.ts` is a seven-step `GuideChapterDoc` in
each language, same steps, same pictures, same order, `alt` text written separately in each: make a
deck (from a saved set, and the three other buttons that make one); your decks and what is waiting;
what is in a deck; adding a card; reviewing; the four grades; and placing a deck where people will
find it. The order is the order a reader meets the screens, which is also the order
`e2e/flashcards.mjs` drives them in, because that is what the app does
(`backend/flashcards/CLAUDE.md`, §17BR.A).

Three things the prose is careful about, each because the app is careful about it:

- **Placement is the sharing**, and the chapter says so in those words (`prompts/README.md` §9) —
  a deck placed on a course is studyable by everybody who can open that course, on the owner's
  cards and on the reader's own schedule, and a course only its participants can see keeps its
  decks that way because the panel is only drawn for somebody who could already open the page.
- **"Placing is a pointer, not a handover"** is the reader's version of `can_study` being wider
  than `can_edit`. The chapter names the honest answer the deck page gives a reader who wants to
  change somebody else's deck: "Save a copy to my account".
- **The schedule is described, not the algorithm.** "What you press decides when the card comes
  back; Again means now, in this same sitting" is as much SM-2 as a manual should contain, and the
  design's own sentence — a card comes back on the day you were about to forget it — is the lead.

The closing `note` names what is missing: no public deck library to browse, no reminder when cards
fall due, no offline study. It points at `/about/flashcards` for the design, as every chapter with
a showcase does.

**The pictures.** `chapters.flashcards` in `frontend/e2e/guide-screenshots.mjs`, 183 lines, writing
`static/guide/flashcards/01…07`: seven pictures, 186 KB, every one clipped and taken by the script
against the real app, as the file's own forty-line header insists. Nothing in `seed_demo_*` makes a
deck, so the block creates its rows the way `chapters.help` does — idempotently, through the real
API, under `ania@edmat.example`, who is the one demo account that has both a saved set to make a
deck from and a course to place it on. It finds-or-creates the same "Before the midterm" set the
exercises chapter photographs (repeated rather than shared, so `ONLY=flashcards` does not depend on
that chapter having run), a deck of three exercise cards from it, a second deck of two text cards
so the list has two rows and two source labels, and one placement on the seeded course `arrange()`
publishes. **It grades nothing**: flipping a card is all the browser does, so the due counts in
picture 2 are the same on the tenth run as on the first, and the schedule the account carries is
unchanged by having been photographed.

**`index.ts`**: `pending` dropped from the entry, the blurb rewritten in both languages, and the
chapter deleted from the hub's own "Not written yet" list — that list is for parts of the site with
no chapter, and flashcards now has one. The `pending` flag itself stays in the interface and
`guide_pendingBadge` stays in both catalogues: the mechanism is for the next chapter written ahead
of its screens, and no chapter uses it today.

### Verified

Both servers on 8143/5243 from this worktree, **with `DJANGO_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` set by hand** —

## 17BT.A — `manage.py test --parallel 4`: 138 classes, one line each, and a checker that cannot lie (2026-10-06)

Closing cycle, step A (`prompts/12-test-shards.md`, design `prompts/11-closing-design.md`). Branch
`close/a-test-shards` from `490c195`. Closes `todo.md` "Learning cycle — left open" bullet 2.

**The problem.** The documented way to run the backend suite did not work at all. `telemetry`'s
middleware writes a `RequestLog` row for every request, into one of nine SQLite shards
(`telemetry/routers.py`), and Django's test runner forbids a test from touching a database alias
its class did not declare. Forty test classes carried
`databases = set(all_log_shards()) | {'default'}`; **138** did not — the brief counted 137 in 28
files, of which two (`booking/test_week_schedules.py`) turned out to need nothing and three more
(`taxonomy/tests.py`) only showed up once the checker was widened, leaving 135 for this branch and
3 for steps B and E. Serially,
`telemetry/middleware.py`'s `except Exception` swallowed the resulting `DatabaseOperationForbidden`
and logged a full traceback **per request** — the measurement: a run of the single class
`events.test_permission_matrix.PermissionMatrixTests`, **one test**, printed **704** copies of
`Failed to write a request log row` and **19 020 lines** of output. Multiply by the whole suite and
that is the "tens of thousands of lines" the board complained of. Under `--parallel` the same
refusal surfaced as a hard `setUpClass` error, and the runner then died shipping that error back to
the parent: `TypeError: cannot pickle 'traceback' object`.

**The fix is one line, repeated on purpose.** **113** copies of
`databases = set(all_log_shards()) | {'default'}` across **25** test files, resolving **135**
reported classes — the difference is inheritance: where a file already had a base class
(`shifts/tests.py: RotaTestCase`, `plans/tests.py: PlansTestCase`, `galleries/tests.py:
GalleryBase`, `accounts/test_avatar.py: AvatarTestCase`, `accounts/test_throttling.py:
ThrottleTestCase`, `needs/tests.py: NeedsBaseTestCase`) the line went on the base, once, and
twenty-two subclasses inherited it. **No cross-app shared base was extracted**, and that is a
decision rather than laziness: the forty classes that already had the line each kept their own copy
so that one app's fixtures cannot break another app's suite, and house rule 13 points the other way
only when the thing being shared is *behaviour*, not a constant.

`booking/test_week_schedules.py` was reported by the brief's own script and is the one file that
needed **nothing**: its classes inherit `booking.tests.ApiTestCase`, which has had the line all
along. A second copy there would have been a change that looked like a fix.

**`tblib` is what makes a parallel failure legible**, and is now in `backend/requirements.txt` (the
root file is a one-line include of it, which is what `setup.sh` installs, so one edit covers both).
Without it the first error in any worker kills the run with no test name attached.

**The checker is the deliverable, not the sweep.** `backend/testing/check_databases_declared.py`
parses every `test*.py` (no settings, no database needed), resolves a `databases` declaration
through inheritance **including a base imported from another module**, and names every class that
still needs the line. Zero is the bar.

**And the checker caught the sweep lying.** The brief's version of the script looked for
`self.client.`, reported 137 classes, and would have printed `0` with
`taxonomy.tests.TaxonomyModerationTests` — a class the board's own bullet names as broken — still
broken, because that file posts through an `APIClient()` a `_as(who)` helper builds. Widening the
test to "uses `self.client.` **or** constructs a client" found that class and two more beside it in
the same file. A checker narrower than the rule it checks is worse than no checker: it says "done".

### Verified

- `backend/testing/check_databases_declared.py` → **`3 classes still unresolved, in 2 files`**, and
  all three are the ones the ownership table gives to other branches:
  `events/test_permission_matrix.py: PermissionMatrixTests` (step B) and
  `community/test_discussions.py: DiscussionEndpointTests, DiscussionLocationAdminTests` (step E).
  After those two merge it is **0**, which is what `prompts/17-closing-integration.md` step 3 asks.
- `manage.py check` — no issues. `makemigrations --check --dry-run` — no changes.
- Serial `manage.py test shifts plans materials --keepdb` — **196 tests, OK**, 161 s of tests
  (11 min wall including the database build), and **0** occurrences of
  `Failed to write a request log row`. Against the 704 that one unfixed class produces on its own,
  that zero is the proof the declaration is the right fix and not a silenced guard.
- `time manage.py test --parallel 4 --keepdb` — **2 686 tests, OK**, exit 0.
  **24 min 27 s** wall-clock (22:58:38 → 23:23:05), of which 14 min 53 s is the tests themselves
  and ~9½ min is building ten databases before any test runs. **Four other agents were working the
  same six cores throughout** (closing steps B–E, three of them driving browsers), so that is an
  upper bound, not a clean-machine figure. The documented "~9 min" was never a measurement of this
  command — it is the database-build time quoted in every worktree recipe — and `test.md` now says
  the measured number instead.
- The 738 remaining `Failed to write a request log row` lines in that run are **all** from the
  three classes the ownership table gives to steps B and E: 704 of them are
  `PermissionMatrixTests` (measured on its own), the rest `community/test_discussions.py`. Nothing
  else in 2 686 tests prints the line.
- **The first `--parallel 4` run failed, and both causes were real but neither was the shards.**
  Six errors were `OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device` on `/tmp` — the machine's root
  filesystem filled up mid-run with five agents on it, and `galleries/tests.py` and
  `community/test_inline_images.py` both `mkdtemp` a per-class `MEDIA_ROOT`. The seventh was a
  genuine, pre-existing, **date-dependent** test, described below. The run *reported* all seven and
  exited cleanly, which is precisely what `tblib` is for: before this branch the first of them
  would have killed the runner with no test name attached.

### Left open

- **Three classes still need the line and are deliberately not mine**:
  `events/test_permission_matrix.py: PermissionMatrixTests` (step B's file) and
  `community/test_discussions.py: DiscussionEndpointTests, DiscussionLocationAdminTests` (step E's).
  `check_databases_declared.py` prints them by name until those branches merge; the integrator
  should expect **0** afterwards and treat any other name as the step that missed it.
- **`booking/test_week_schedules.py: PrecedenceTests` was fixed here, outside this step's brief.**
  `test_the_weeks_around_a_detached_one_are_untouched` asserts on the week *before* the anchor
  Tuesday, which with the default `weeks_ahead=1` is **today** whenever the suite runs on a
  Tuesday — and `slots_for_service` never offers an hour that has already passed, so the 14:00 and
  15:00 it expects are gone by mid-afternoon. It failed for the first time at 22:45 on Tuesday
  2026-10-06 and would have failed serially too; `--parallel` had nothing to do with it. The fix is
  `weeks_ahead=2` in that class's `setUp` with a comment saying why. I did not sweep the rest of
  the suite for other day-of-week-dependent tests; `booking/tests.py: next_weekday` and
  `events/tests.py` are where any others would live.
- **The ~9½-minute database build is paid on every run** and `--keepdb` cannot help, because the
  SQLite test databases are in-memory. Giving `default` a `TEST['NAME']` on disk would make
  `--keepdb` real and cut most of it; it would also mean a stale test database can now outlive a
  migration, which is a trade nobody has chosen. Named, not taken.
- **Nothing stops the next test class from forgetting the line.** The checker exists and `test.md`
  points at it, but no hook and no CI runs it — this project has no CI at all, so a reminder in a
  document is the whole mechanism.
- **Files that would genuinely benefit from an in-file base class** and did not get one, because
  extracting one is a bigger change than this step was given: `moderation/tests.py` and
  `materials/tests.py` (17 classes each, every one of them now carrying its own copy of the line),
  `services/tests.py` (9) and `exercises/test_solution_entries.py` (10). The repetition is
  deliberate *across* apps; inside one file it is just repetition.
- **The six `No space left on device` errors were environmental and are not fixed.** They say
  something true, though: a parallel run plus four other agents can fill this machine's root
  filesystem, and `mkdtemp`-based per-class `MEDIA_ROOT`s are where it shows up first.
- **`backend/CLAUDE.md`'s own "Testing" section still does not mention the rule.** It is not in the
  closing cycle's file-ownership table, so I left it alone rather than collide with another branch;
  it is a two-line addition for whoever integrates.

## 17BU — After the closing cycle: the publish replay, and four branches on the left-opens (2026-10-07)

The closing cycle (§17BT) ended with a board shorter than it found it and one thing it was not
allowed to do: publish. This section is that publish, and the four branches that took what §17BT
named and did not own. Nothing new was designed; every item below was a bullet on `todo.md` that
morning.

### The publish, and the drift it had to settle first

`origin/main` had been at `4668148` since 2026-09-25 — the owner's list, the learning cycle and the
closing cycle were all unpublished, 42 first-parent commits and 465 paths. Two things made the usual
cherry-pick replay the wrong tool. The 2026-09-25 replays had been **edited on the publish branch**
(deploy and webek4 references stripped; §17BL split into §17BL + §17BM) and never merged back, so
nine paths disagreed and `git cherry` could not be trusted; and a 42-commit cherry-pick across
that drift would have conflicted on every HISTORY append.

So the drift came home first — `d577d94`: origin's wording for HISTORY.md, test.md,
`backend/events/CLAUDE.md`, `testing/conference_demo.py` and `testing/personas.py`, with every
local section after §17BP kept; local kept for the three `school-management-demo/scripts/*.js` and
the snapshot, where local was ahead. Then the replay was done as a **tree build rather than a
patch series**: for each first-parent commit, its tree with `deploy/` swapped for origin's copy and
(for the commits before the reconcile) the five text files overlaid, written with `commit-tree`
under the original author, date and message. No conflict is possible that way, and the audit is one
command: `git diff --stat d577d94 publish/2026-10-07` lists the three held-back `deploy/` files and
nothing else. `publish/2026-10-07` = `9ec2086`, 41 commits (the reconcile itself is empty after the
overlays and is skipped). The script is kept beside the union resolver in the orchestrator's memory
directory, with a `BASE=` so the after-cycle commits stack on the same branch.

**Not pushed by the session.** The auto-mode classifier refuses `git push` as a production deploy,
and that refusal is not something an agent should route around; the owner pushes
`publish/2026-10-07:main` (a fast-forward). Until then `origin/main` is still `4668148`, and the
boards say so.

### The four branches

Cut from `d577d94`, worktrees `after-<x>`, ports 815x/525x, merged as they landed — D `a921e0c`,
B `86b2f9f`, A `efa1d01`, C `f1e5b00` — every conflict the "both appended" kind in HISTORY.md,
resolved by union; no migration anywhere. Each has its own subsection below, written on its branch.

| Step | Closed | Found on the way |
|---|---|---|
| **D** make-a-deck | `e2e/make-a-deck.mjs`, 45 checks against the real `POST /api/decks/` | the create path **refused** a generated name over 120 characters that the edit path truncated — "The deck could not be made" about a name nobody typed (`backend/flashcards/serializers.py`); the concept button's confirmation had no link to the deck |
| **B** matrix rows | 24 rows, 722 → 746: the verified contributor's four 201s, the issuing action's four refusal words and its success, `already_revoked` | the matrix count had drifted in three files (690 was true at the management layer); `POST /api/services/` and `POST /api/courses/` had **no founding rows at all**; "the two course founding paths" are one course path and one tutoring listing |
| **A** six small things | the footer's doubled name, the `/flashcards` sign-in door, three a11y findings, two `e2e/CLAUDE.md` traps, the orphaned PNG, the hint/solution reveal toggles | the heading-order finding was not the scratch row's — `/events` and `/tutoring` put cards' `h3` straight under an `h1`; the waiting badge was a **mismatched pair** (warning foreground on the info background) |
| **C** test hygiene | 55 copies of the `databases` line → 4 in-file bases; the checker run by the suite (`testing/test_databases_declared.py`); the day-of-week sweep | the checker had skipped **74 request-making classes** whose base name did not contain `TestCase`; one booking test could not fail after 22:00; nothing else in the backend computes a weekday |

### What integration did on top

  back only because A was in the events components. Driven by D's script on the merged tree: 45
