## 17BU.D — The three "make a deck" buttons, against the real endpoint (2026-10-07, `after/d-make-a-deck`)

The learning cycle's §API bargain (`prompts/README.md` §9) was that steps C, D and E would each
build a "make a deck" button against the shape step A had promised, verify it against a `page.route`
**mock**, and let integration prove the real call. Integration merged all eight branches and never
pressed one. So three buttons — a course lesson (`CourseContent.svelte`, §17BR.C), a programme
session (`Programme.svelte`, §17BR.E) and a concept (`DeckFromConcept.svelte`, §17BR.D) — shipped
having only ever talked to a mock that answered whatever they sent. `school-mode.mjs` and
`take-home.mjs` still carry those mocks, and will: they are testing their own half.

`frontend/e2e/make-a-deck.mjs` is the half nobody had: **45 checks in six sections**, both real
servers, the real `POST /api/decks/`.

### What the real endpoint showed

**Two of the three were right about everything that was ever in doubt.** The lesson button sends
three string exercise ids and a `{kind:'lesson', id}` source and gets three cards back **in the
lesson's own order**; `placement: {kind:'course'}` lands for an instructor and is correctly absent
for a participant, whose deck comes back unplaced while the course's two placements stay the
instructor's. "Take home" sends the session's two ids and a `{kind:'session'}` source and the
organiser's deck arrives on the event, a visitor's in their own list. The concept button sends the
concept's **numeric pk** (`concept.id` from `mapConcept`, not the slug — `_resolve_source` accepts
either, which is why nobody had had to be sure) and gets one card per linked exercise, placed
nowhere. Pressing each a second time makes a **second deck**, which is the design answer and not a
gap: `already_placed` can only fire for a deck that is already on that node, and a deck created
half a second ago never is.

**One thing was genuinely broken, and it was in the one place three callers share.**
`DeckDraftSerializer.name` was `CharField(max_length=120)`, so `POST /api/decks/` **refused** a name
over the cap with a 400. None of the three buttons asks anybody for a name: each **generates** one
from a lesson, session or concept title, and `Lesson.title`, `Session.title` and a concept's
resolved head are all `max_length=200`. A teacher with a long week heading pressed the button and
got "The deck could not be made." — a refusal they could not act on, about a name they never typed.
The same file's `DeckSerializer.validate_name` (the **edit** path) had always truncated instead, so
the two halves of one endpoint disagreed about the same field. Fixed by making the create path
agree: no `max_length` on the field, `value[:NAME_MAX_LENGTH]` in `validate_name`. Truncating is the
right answer precisely because nobody typed it — both inputs where somebody does type a deck name
are `maxlength="120"` in the browser, so a typed name cannot reach this at all.
`DeckCreationTests.test_a_generated_name_past_the_cap_is_truncated_rather_than_refused` pins it, and
section 3 of the script drives it through a real lesson whose generated name is 152 characters.

**One thing was stale rather than broken.** §17BR.D wrote, honestly, that `DeckFromConcept.svelte`
has "deliberately no link to the deck that comes back", because `/flashcards/[id]` did not exist on
that branch — and ended "the integrator adds the link". The integrator added the route and not the
link, so the concept button's confirmation was a dead end while the lesson button's offered the
door. Added (`paths_deck_open`, both locales), with the underline the pill needs: inside a green
`status-pill` an un-underlined "Open it" is the same colour as the sentence it ends and does not
read as a link at all — visible in a screenshot, invisible to `npm run check:a11y`.

### Verified

45 checks, 0 failed, 0 console/page errors, twice (before and after the link's CSS), against
`localhost:5254` / `127.0.0.1:8154`. `manage.py test flashcards` 65 tests OK; `check`,
`makemigrations --check --dry-run` (no changes) and `testing/check_databases_declared.py` (0) clean;
`npm run check` 2412 files / 0 errors / 0 warnings; `npm run lint` clean. Nine screenshots in
`e2e/screens/make-a-deck-*.png`, all looked at — the truncated deck name and the underlined "Open
it" are both things only a screenshot shows, and the participant's view of the course (her own deck
absent from the panel, the instructor's two present with no "Remove from here") is the placement
rule drawn rather than asserted.

### Left open

- **"Take home" still has no link to the deck it made.** The organiser's sentence ends "it is on
  this event, so everybody here can study it", and the event's Flashcards panel does carry the link
  — so an organiser is one scroll from it. A visitor is told "it is in your decks" and has to go
  find them. The same one-line addition as the concept button, in `Programme.svelte`, which this
  branch left alone because another agent was in the events components.
- **One exercise, two names on two screens.** On `/concepts/calka` the Exercises card reads "Test EN
  title" and the deck made from that very page names the same row "Aksjomaty normy euklidesowej".
  Neither is wrong: `ConceptLinks` goes through the exercise service, which sends `?lang=`, and both
  `/api/concepts/{slug}/exercises/` and a deck's card refs do not, so they get
  `config/i18n_utils.request_locale`'s documented default of the **original** locale. It is the
  shape of the bug §17BR.D found by looking at a screenshot (`_target_title` naming one concept two
  ways), one layer out, and it wants a decision about which answer a deck should carry rather than
  a patch.
- **No kill-switch section.** `flashcards.mjs` already proves the switch takes the panel and the
  account-menu entry away as a non-staff reader, and `take-home.mjs` proves it takes the "Take home"
  button away; a third copy would be three places to update.
- **The script is desktop-only.** `flashcards.mjs` owns the phone-width checks for this feature.

## 17BU.B — The matrix rows closing step B named and did not write (2026-10-07, `after/b-matrix-rows`)

Three bullets from `todo.md` "Closing step B — left open", all of them in one file:
`backend/events/test_permission_matrix.py`. Nothing else in `backend/` changed — no model, no
view, no rule module, no migration. **24 rows and three fixture people**, taking the table from
722 rows to **746**.

### 1. The four founding paths, from the side the gate lets through

Closing step B added `persona.verified` for `GET /api/creation/` and said so in its own "Left
open": every *founding* row in the table pinned the refusal of an unverified adult and none pinned
the success of a verified one. The table would therefore have read exactly the same if the creation
gate refused **everybody** — which is the one failure a permission matrix exists to catch.

`config/creation.py` governs four kinds (`course` `event` `service` `organization`), so there are
four 201s. Two of those four paths had **no founding rows at all**, so they get the whole column —
401 anonymous, `(403, 'minor')`, `(403, 'verification_required')`, 201 verified — and the two that
already carried refusals get the 201 only, with the **same body** the refused row sends: a 201 is
evidence about the gate only if the request that earns it is the request that was refused.

**The board said "the two course founding paths" and that is not what they are.** `courses/` has
exactly one create path, `CourseViewSet.create`; the second unpinned kind is a *tutoring listing*,
`services/views.py: ServiceViewSet.create` (the app is still `services` and the API still
`/api/services/` — only the frontend route is `/korki`). Four kinds, four create paths, one rule
module; the comment in the file says so, so the next reader does not go looking for a second
course endpoint that has never existed. Six rows were asked for; ten is what the four endpoints
actually need.

### 2. Issuing a certificate — `POST /api/courses/{id}/completions/`

The third completion endpoint. Closing step B pinned `GET` on it and `GET`/`revoke` on
`/api/course-completions/{id}/`, and wrote the issuing action on the board: its four words are
asserted in `courses/test_school_mode.py` against one school's own people, and nowhere in the
cross-persona view. Ten rows now: 401 anonymous, `not_staff` for a stranger, for the holder
(nobody issues their own) and for the event's **volunteer** — the "staff role that may not" column,
staff of something else entirely — `not_participant` both for somebody on no roster and for a body
that names nobody at all (`_user_or_none` answers one mistake with one word), `not_done`,
`already_issued`, and the 201.

**The order of the words is the rule module's and two rows depend on it.**
`completion_block_reason` checks `already_issued` *before* `not_done`, so `participant` — who holds
the live certificate and has ticked nothing off — can never carry the 201 whatever the fixture
does to them. Hence `graduate`. And a **withdrawn** certificate still answers `already_issued`,
because a revoked row keeps its `(course, participant)` pair and reissuing is `revoke`'s inverse,
which is not built; that is now a row rather than a sentence in a docstring.

### 3. `already_revoked` — the fixture could carry it after all

The board recorded this one as possibly impossible: the unique key is `(course, participant)` with
no condition, so the live certificate cannot also be the withdrawn one, and every matrix row runs
in its own rolled-back savepoint, so the `revoke` 200 cannot leave a withdrawn row behind for a
later row to collide with. Both are true, and neither is in the way: a **second** completion for a
**different** participant is all it takes. `persona.revoked` holds it, and three rows come with the
409 — the holder still reads their withdrawn certificate (200: a revocation is a timestamp, never a
delete, house rule 12), the course staff who withdrew it still read it, and a stranger still gets
404, because a withdrawn certificate is no more public than a live one.

### The fixture, and why three people rather than one

`course` grew a chapter and **two** lessons, and three more accounts on its roster: `graduate` (both
lessons done, no certificate → the 201), `halfway` (**one** of the two → `not_done`) and `revoked`
(a withdrawn certificate). Half rather than none on purpose: "nothing ticked off" and "a course
with no lessons at all" both reach `not_done` through the `total == 0` clause, so a row that could
pass either way pins neither. All three are `make_viewer`, not `make_user` — nothing signs in as
them (the rows that name them send an id in a body), which is exactly the case `backend/CLAUDE.md`
asks for the cheap factory in. The seeded certificate's note changed from `3 of 3 lessons` to
`2 of 2`, so the fixture's own text stops contradicting the course it hangs on.

### Verified

- `manage.py test events.test_permission_matrix courses.test_school_mode -v 1` — **59 tests, OK**
  in 188 s (one matrix method over 746 subtests, plus school mode's 58). Unpiped into a file and
  the `OK` line read out of it, because a piped run reports `tail`'s exit status (`test.md` §7).
- **Each of the 24 rows was mutation-checked, not merely watched to pass.** Eight new expectations
  were deliberately falsified in a scratch copy — the four 201s turned into refusals, `not_done`
  into `already_issued`, the issuing 201 into a 409, `already_revoked` into `not_done`, and the
  revoked holder's 200 into a 404 — and the run came back **`FAILED (failures=8)`**, each failure
  printing the real response (`got 201: {…'title': 'Kurs, który prowadzę'…}`,
  `right status, wrong word: {'detail': 'already_revoked'}`). A row that passes because nothing
  reaches the endpoint would have stayed green through that; these did not.
- `testing/check_databases_declared.py` — **`0 classes still unresolved, in 0 files`**.
  `PermissionMatrixTests` already declared the line (closing step B added it).
- `manage.py check` — 0 issues. `makemigrations --check --dry-run` — **no changes**.
- **746 rows, counted rather than incremented** (house rule 5), and the count in `test.md` had
  already drifted: **690** was right when the management layer went in, the learning cycle's
  integration added 15 and closing step B 17, and nobody updated the number. 690 + 15 + 17 + 24 =
  746, and each block's own share is checkable against the block comments.

### Left open

- **`events/CLAUDE.md` still says "the 690-row permission matrix"**, and `test.md` now says 746.
  The brief for this step gave me the matrix file, `test.md` and `HISTORY.md` and nothing else in
  `backend/`, so the app's own `CLAUDE.md` is one number for whoever may edit it. It is the third
  place this count lives, which is itself the reason it drifts.
- **No row for the `verified` persona on anything but the four founding paths and
  `/api/creation/`.** That is the whole of what the gate governs, so nothing is missing today; the
  day `is_verified_contributor` gates a fifth surface, this is where it needs a column.
- **The 201 rows found no bug.** Four create paths answered 201 for a verified contributor the
  first time they were asked, which is the honest outcome and worth recording: unlike the
  management-layer rows (four real bugs) and the conference rows (one), this block pins behaviour
  that was already right.
- **`not_done` is still pinned on a course with lessons only.** The `total == 0` clause — a course
  with no lessons at all is vacuously complete and must *not* print a certificate — is asserted in
  `courses/test_school_mode.py` and has no matrix row, because giving it one would mean a second
  course in this fixture whose only purpose is to have nothing in it.
- **Nothing was done about the issuing endpoint's shape**, which this reading made me notice:
  `POST /courses/{id}/completions/` takes `participant` as a bare id and there is no people search
  (`CLAUDE.md`, known gaps), so the issuer's form has to already know the number. Not this step's,
  and not a permissions question.

## 17BU.A — Six small things the closing cycle named and nobody owned (2026-10-07, `after/a-frontend-fixes`)

Six bullets from `todo.md`'s "Closing cycle — left open", every one of them found by a step that
had no business fixing it: a double word in the footer, a gated page with no door, three
pre-existing axe findings, two traps that cost a session each and were never written down, an
orphaned screenshot, and two message keys with nothing calling them. None is interesting on its
own. Collected here because the alternative is that each gets rediscovered separately.

### The footer said the name twice

`Footer.svelte` rendered `{m.common_appName()} — {m.nav_tagline()}`, and `nav_tagline` already
begins with the name in **both** catalogues ("EdMat — zadania, …" / "EdMat — exercises, …"). So the
first line of every page's footer read "EdMat — EdMat — exercises, materials, …". The fix is to
drop the prefix: the tagline stands alone, and the header's brand mark is the one place the name is
genuinely a separate string. Found on a manual screenshot by closing step C, which could not reach
the file.

### `/flashcards` signed out told you to sign in and not where

The page printed `decks_signInNote` — "Sign in to keep decks and a review schedule." — as flat
text. Every other gated page here makes that line a link: `/notifications`, `/messages`,
`/settings`, `/submit`, `/submit-material`, `/tutoring/watchlist`, `/courses/mine`. So this page now
uses the same `<p data-session-hidden class="login-prompt"><a href={resolve('/login')}>…</a></p>`
they do, with the same two style rules, and the `{#if authStore.restoring}` branch that is the
other half of that pattern — without it somebody reloading with a valid token is shown a refusal
for the length of one request. **No new message key**: the copy that was already there became the
link, which is the version with one sentence in it rather than two.

### The three pre-existing axe findings

All three were reported by C, D *and* the integration run, and all three were outside the nineteen
pages any closing step owned.

- **`heading-order` (moderate) on `/events` and `/tutoring`.** Not a scratch row's fault, although
  that is how it looked: both pages put their `h1` straight above a grid of cards with no section
  heading between, and both cards hard-coded `h3`. `ServiceCard` already had a `headingLevel` prop
  (1 | 2 | 3, for its own detail page); `EventCard` did not, so it got one — same shape, same
  class-not-tag style selector `ServiceCard` carries a note about, since a tag selector stops
  applying in exactly the case the prop exists for. `/events`, `/tutoring` and
  `/tutoring/watchlist` (the same `h1`-then-cards shape, not reported only because the audit does
  not open it) pass `headingLevel={2}`. The homepage, `/search`, `/about/events` and the profile's
  listings modal all sit under an `h2` and keep the default 3.
- **`color-contrast` (serious) on `.badge--waiting` at `/material-projects?tab=mine`.** A
  **mismatched pair**: the warning foreground over the *info* background, which is the blue-tinted
  one `.badge--seeking` directly above it is built for. #a15c00 on #e8eefb is **4.46:1**, under
  AA's 4.5. Pairing the warning foreground with its own background is the whole fix — amber on
  cream, still the one warm pill in a row of neutral and blue ones — and gives **4.65:1** light,
  **5.97:1** dark. The light figure clears the bar by 0.15, which is thin enough that the component
  now says so: a later change to either warning token has to be re-measured, not eyeballed.

### Two traps, written down

`frontend/e2e/CLAUDE.md` gained 28 and 29, both of which cost a real session during the closing
cycle and neither of which was in the file:

- **Clearing `backend/cachedata/*` under a running backend** leaves the process holding a handle on
  a file that is gone, and the next anonymous read of that entry answers `OSError: [Errno 116]
  Stale file handle` as a 500 — on `/api/branches/`, in the run that found it, which reads as "one
  feature is broken". Stop the backend first.
- **`scripts/check_accessibility.ts` reads `--base`/`--api`, not `E2E_BASE`**, and has defaults. Run
  with the env var alone it does not fail: it audits whatever is on `:5174`, usually nothing, and
  reports every page as a load problem.

### `decks_includeHint` / `decks_includeSolution` got their control

The two flags were persisted (`flashcards.Card.include_hint` / `include_solution`), honoured by the
review screen, accepted by the API (`CardEditSerializer`) and exposed by the service
(`updateCard`) — and **nothing anywhere set them**, so every card was reviewed as
statement-and-answer only and two message keys had no call site. The owner's call was to build the
control rather than delete the keys, and the backend needed no change at all: the serializer
already takes both on `PATCH /api/cards/{id}/`.

The control is a pair of checkboxes under each card's title in the deck's own card list
(`/flashcards/[id]`), drawn only for `deck.canEdit` and only on an **exercise** card — a concept
card's two faces are a resolved revision's title and summary and a free-text card's are what its
author typed, so neither has a hint or a pinned solution to reveal and a checkbox there would be a
switch wired to nothing. The response is spliced back over the row rather than the flag flipped
locally, for the reason every other write on this page re-reads: the server's answer is the state,
and a refusal must not leave the box ticked. `.card`'s `align-items` moved from `baseline` to
`flex-start`, because the body is now three lines tall and baseline alignment pushed Remove down to
the last of them.

### Verified

Both real servers up (backend `:8151`, frontend `:5251`), Node 24.21.

- `npm run check` — **2412 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings**.
- `npm run lint` — prettier and eslint clean.
- `npm run build` — built in 40.8 s, adapter-static wrote `build/`.
- `npm run check:a11y -- --base http://localhost:5251 --api http://127.0.0.1:8151` — **48 pages, 0
  had a load problem, 0 critical/serious, 0 moderate/minor**. Run first against the pre-fix files
  for the same database, which reported exactly the three findings and nothing else: `heading-order`
  on `/events` (`<h3>TEST=FAKE Sandbox conference</h3>`) and `/tutoring`, `color-contrast` on
  `.badge--waiting`. The badge page is **not** a vacuous pass — project 12 ("A verified upload")
  carries one pending proposal in this database, so the pill is genuinely drawn.
- `e2e/flashcards.mjs` against the same servers — **43 passed, 0 failed**, zero console errors.
- An ad-hoc browser pass (not added to `e2e/`, 11 checks, all passing): the footer names EdMat
  exactly once in **both** languages; `/flashcards` signed out gives a link that lands on `/login`;
  the deck page draws six checkboxes for three exercise cards, ticking one `PATCH`es
  `/api/cards/{id}/` with 200, the server agrees afterwards, and the flags survive a reload. The
  deck was put back to both-flags-off at the end.
- Screenshots looked at: the footer in both languages, `/flashcards` signed out, the deck page at
  desktop and at 390 px (no overflow, the labels wrap under each title). The three
  `flashcards-*.png` that show the deck's card list are re-committed because they genuinely changed;
  the other twelve were restored.
- `messages/en.json` and `messages/pl.json` — 3931 keys each, key sets identical. **No key was
  added**; this change is entirely call sites.

### Left open

- **The light-mode `.badge--waiting` ratio is 4.65:1**, 0.15 above AA. It passes, and it is the
  closest thing on the site to the line. Darkening `$light-status-warning` from `#a15c00` to about
  `#8a4f00` would take it to 5.88:1 and improve every other warning surface with it — a token
  change affecting the whole site, which is not a badge fix and was not taken here.
- **`/events` in this dev database holds exactly one row, `TEST=FAKE Sandbox conference`** — a
  leftover from some earlier browser run. Harmless, and it is what the axe finding quoted; nobody
  has swept the dev database for scratch rows.
- **Nothing sets the two reveal flags at CREATION time.** "Add an exercise" and "Add its exercises"
  both post a card with both flags false, and the person then ticks them in the list. A per-add
  default (or a deck-level one) is a product decision, not a missing control.
- **Still no plural forms.** `decks_cardCount`, `decks_dueSummary` and friends read "1 decks" /
  "1 taliach"; zero of 3931 keys use an ICU plural. It is a site-wide copy decision and one sweep —
  named again here because this section touched the same screens and did not fix it.

## 17BU.C — One `databases` line per file, a checker the suite runs, and a day-of-week sweep (2026-10-07, `after/c-test-hygiene`)

Follow-up cycle after the closing integration, step C. Branch `after/c-test-hygiene` from `d577d94`.
Closes three of the six bullets in `todo.md` "Closing step A — left open" — the per-file base
classes, the checker being run by the suite, and the day-of-week sweep. Two more of the six had gone
stale and were deleted with them: the three classes that lacked the line landed with steps B and E,
and `backend/CLAUDE.md` §Testing had already gained the rule at integration. The sixth, the
in-memory test databases that make `--keepdb` a no-op, is still open and still named.

### 1. The line lives on a base class, once per file

`moderation/tests.py` and `materials/tests.py` carried
`databases = set(all_log_shards()) | {'default'}` **17 times each**, `exercises/test_solution_entries.py`
**12** and `services/tests.py` **9** — 55 copies of one constant, with the same three-line comment
explaining it stranded on whichever class happened to come first. Each file now defines its own
`class ApiTestCase(APITestCase)` carrying the line and the explanation, and its suites inherit:
**55 copies down to 4**. §17BT.A's "no cross-app shared base" decision is untouched and restated in
each new base's docstring — the repetition *across* apps is what stops one app's fixtures breaking
another's; inside one file it was only repetition. **Thirty-eight test files already did it this
way** (forty-two now), so this was joining the convention rather than inventing one.

**The classes that make no request were deliberately left on `APITestCase`** —
`moderation.NodeGovernorHelperTests` and `materials.CreateMaterialFactoryTests`. That is not tidiness:
it is what keeps `check_databases_declared.py` able to catch the next class that forgets. If every
class in a file inherited the base, no class in that file could ever be reported again.

### 2. The checker had to be read before trusting it — and then widened

**It already honoured inheritance within a file**, which the brief for this step expected to have to
teach it (§17BT.A built it that way for `booking/test_week_schedules.py`'s cross-module base). So the
base-class extraction needed no change to it at all: it printed `0` before and after.

What it did *not* do was consider a class whose only base is a **file-local base named without
`TestCase` in it**. The filter was a substring test on the immediate base names, so every subclass of
`galleries/tests.py: GalleryBase`, `cloakroom/tests.py: DeskCase`,
`coauthoring/tests.py: CoauthoringBase`, `concepts/tests.py: ConceptBase`,
`documents/tests.py: DocumentCase`, `materials_coop/tests.py: CoopBase` and six others was skipped
before anything else was asked about it: **74 request-making classes the checker had never
examined**. All 74 happen to inherit the line from their base — the next one
would not have had to. `Analyzer.is_test_case()` now resolves "is this a test class" through the base
chain the same way `declares()` resolves the declaration, so the two halves agree about what they are
looking at. Classes considered: **258 → 332**. Offenders: **0 → 0**.

This is the same failure §17BT.A caught in the brief's own sweep script, one layer down: a checker
narrower than the rule it checks says "done".

### 3. The suite is what runs the checker now

Nothing ran it — no CI, no git hook, and a paragraph in `test.md` asking the next person to remember.
`main()` is split into `offending_classes(root=ROOT)` (returning `(file, line, class)` triples) and a
`main()` that prints exactly what it printed before, and `backend/testing/test_databases_declared.py`
asserts the list is empty. A forgotten line is now a test failure that names the file, the line and
the class.

`testing/` is not in `INSTALLED_APPS` and does not need to be: `manage.py test` discovers from the
filesystem under `backend/`, which is also why `config/test_locale_hint.py` has always run. The test
class is a `SimpleTestCase` and declares no `databases` — it makes no request, and the checker agrees,
because it only reports classes whose body makes one. Nothing in that file may build a test client
without owing the very declaration it polices.

Four fixture tests beside the real assertion build throwaway source trees in a `TemporaryDirectory`
and prove the check can still fail: a class that declares nothing is caught; a same-file base counts
for its subclasses; a base that itself forgot does **not** shield them; and a base whose name lacks
`TestCase` no longer hides them. "Found nothing" and "cannot find anything any more" look identical
from outside, and the base-class change above is exactly the kind that could have turned one into the
other.

### 4. The day-of-week sweep

§17BT.A fixed `booking/test_week_schedules.PrecedenceTests` by accident, at 22:45 on a Tuesday, and
left the sweep open. The sweep is done and it found **one** thing, which is worth saying as plainly as
a long list would be.

**Where day-of-week arithmetic can live at all:** `weekday`, `week_start`, `monday_of` and
`day_of_week` appear in exactly one app's logic — `booking/`. Every hit anywhere else in `backend/`
is `AccountProfile.week_starts_on` (a display preference: it says how a time is *drawn*, and nothing
computes with it), a comment about it, or `seed_demo_content.py` writing two `AvailabilityRule` rows
for a demo tutor. So no test outside `booking/` can depend on which day it runs, and none does: the date-bearing suites
(`events`, `shifts`, `venues`, `documents`, `cloakroom`, `work`, `tasks`, `events/test_tickets.py`)
all build times as `timezone.now() ± timedelta(...)` or from a per-class `self.start` anchor, and
`/api/my-schedule/`'s default horizon is 14 days, so a `now + 1 day` event is in range on every day of
the week.

**Inside `booking/`**, every date comes from `ApiTestCase.next_weekday`, which walks **at least a full
week forward**, so the anchor itself is never today. The only exposure is a test that then looks
*backwards* from the anchor, which is precisely the bug §17BT.A hit. All three backwards references
were checked by hand: `test_week_schedules.py:105` (`tuesday - 7d`) and `:171` (`monday - 1d`) are both
inside `PrecedenceTests`, whose anchor is already `weeks_ahead=2`, leaving them 7 to 19 days ahead
whatever day it is; and
`booking/tests.py: test_the_past_is_not_hidden` (`tuesday - 14d`) means to land in the past and lands
there on every day of the week (1 to 7 days ago). The module docstring now says this, so the next
person adding a test knows the rule is "do not subtract from the anchor without `weeks_ahead=2`".

**The one fix is time-of-day, not day-of-week.**
`AvailabilityComputationTests.test_slots_already_past_are_never_offered` opened the whole of *today*
and asserted `all(slot.start > timezone.now())`. After 22:00 there is no remaining hour, `slots` is
empty, and `all()` over an empty list passes: for two hours every evening it was a test that could not
fail. `slots_for_service` already takes `now=` for exactly this reason, so noon is passed in and the
assertion is now an equality against hours 12–22 — the morning is gone *and* the afternoon is all
still there, on any day, at any hour.

### Verified

- `../.venv/bin/python3 testing/check_databases_declared.py` → **`0 classes still unresolved, in 0 files`**,
  before the change and after it, and after the filter widening that put 74 more classes under it.
- `manage.py test testing` → **6 tests, OK**, 2.3 s, and `Skipping setup of unused database(s)` for
  all ten — a `SimpleTestCase` suite that costs nothing.
- `manage.py check` — no issues. `makemigrations --check --dry-run` — no changes (this step adds
  no model and no migration).
- The touched apps together,
  `manage.py test moderation materials exercises services booking events testing --parallel 4 --keepdb`
  — **825 tests, OK**, 168 s of tests, **0** occurrences of `Failed to write a request log row` and
  **0** tracebacks in 108 lines of output. That zero is the point: the base classes resolve to the
  same declaration the 55 copies made, and nothing fell through.
- `time manage.py test --parallel 4 --keepdb`, machine otherwise idle — **2 706 tests, OK**,
  **21 min 38 s** wall-clock (813.7 s of it the tests; the rest is the ten-database build), **194
  lines** of output, **0** occurrences of `Failed to write a request log row`. **2 700 → 2 706** is
  exactly the six tests in `testing/test_databases_declared.py`; nothing else was added, removed or
  renamed into or out of discovery. The one `Traceback` in those 194 lines is the deliberate one
  `work/tests.py: failing_provider` raises to prove `work/providers.py` reports a broken provider as
  unavailable rather than failing the dashboard — it was in the integration's 198 lines too.

### Left open

- **`--keepdb` still keeps nothing**, because the SQLite test databases are in-memory; the ~9½-minute
  build is paid on every run. Named again rather than taken: a `TEST['NAME']` on disk would make it
  real at the cost of letting a stale test database outlive a migration (§17BT.A's own bullet, still
  the honest trade).
- **`shifts/tests.py: _future()` promises a weekday and does not deliver one.** Its docstring says "a
  weekday morning a few days out"; it is `now + 3 days` at 10:00, which is a Saturday every Wednesday
  and a Sunday every Thursday. Nothing in `shifts/` reads a weekday, so no test depends on it — but
  the same expression also `.replace(hour=...)` on an aware datetime that has been moved three days,
  which keeps the *old* UTC offset across a DST boundary. Both are one-line fixes in a file this step
  did not own.
- **No check that a new test file adds a base rather than repeating the line.** The checker enforces
  that the declaration *exists*, never that it exists once; a file with 17 fresh copies would still
  print 0. Counting copies per file is a different kind of rule — style, not correctness — and nobody
  has asked for it.
- **The headline test count is stale in two files this step did not own.** `test.md` says the new
  number; the root `CLAUDE.md` running block and `CLAUDE_MAP.md` still say 2 700. Three sibling
  branches were editing both files the same afternoon, and a one-number edit is not worth a conflict
  in a shared file — whoever integrates this cycle should set all three from one measurement.
- **The checker still answers "does this class make a request?" with a regex** over the class body
  (`self.client.`, `APIClient()`, `Client()`). It is deliberately wider than the truth, which is the
  safe direction, but a class that reaches an endpoint through a module-level helper taking no client
  would still be missed. No instance of that exists today.

## 17BV — The colour pass: colour that means something, and the colour that was missing by accident (2026-10-07, `ux/colour-pass`)

The owner's ask, verbatim: *"improve interface: make it more colorful, but keep minimalistic and
simple to not distract from what's most important: this is a website for ease of learning and
controling what to focus on and what others should focus, therefore its ui and ux should meet that."*

What the site was: one muted teal on near-white, five status pairs on pills, and nothing else. The
exercise page was four identical white cards; the discipline hub, three; the hero a heading on the
page background; the only saturated pixels on any page were three emoji in the header (a yellow bell,
an orange sun, a die). It was clean and it was monochrome.

### How it was done

Three workflows, one after the other, each adversarial where it could be:

1. **Six readers mapped every colour-bearing surface** (tokens and their drift; cards and lists by
   kind; the learning flow; hard-coded literals; the chrome; state and priority signals), and a
   critic listed what nobody had read. The map found the bugs in §"What was broken" below before
   anybody had an opinion about colour.
2. **Three designers, three judges, one synthesis.** The designers argued three theses — *colour is
   wayfinding* (a hue per family of thing), *one warm second hue* (teal for doing, apricot for
   people), *semantic restraint* (colour only for state and stage). Three judges scored each from a
   lens — a learner and a teacher, accessibility with every pair re-measured, the engineer who ships
   it — and all three chose restraint (39/40/42 of 50), with grafts: the hero wash and the fuller
   header prefix table from the first, the count-badge shape and the `::before` hit area from the
   second. Every objection was resolved in the synthesis, which wrote a spec precise enough for
   parallel implementers: tokens with four values each (light, dark, high-contrast light and dark)
   and a measured contrast table, a rule per surface, twelve decisions with reasons, six disjoint
   work packages. `frontend/CLAUDE.md` §Theming now carries the vocabulary.
3. **Package 1 by hand, packages 2–6 in parallel** on disjoint file sets in one checkout, each
   implementer verifying its own pages in both themes with a screenshot sweep and reporting what it
   saw and what it left open. The orchestrator took their left-opens that were in scope, ran the
   checks once for everybody, and had the before/after pairs reviewed again.

### What was broken, and is not any more

Found by reading token *names*, not screens — nothing in the build checks them:

- **An undefined custom property drops the whole declaration.** `border: 1px solid var(--border)`
  with `--border` undefined draws *no* border. 128 such reads across 54 files — every task, needs,
  event-ops, venue, editor and guardian panel — had rendered borderless for months; `--surface`
  made panels transparent, `--font-size-md`/`--text-sm` inherited the parent size, `--space-8` left
  three venue pages with no padding, and the whole `--color-*` family in the polls components (38
  reads) resolved to nothing: polls had no border, no tint, and a vote button of white text on
  nothing. Every one now reads the real token (`--border-color`, `--bg-surface`, `--bg-surface-alt`,
  `--bg-elevated`, `--font-size-base`, `--font-size-sm`, `--space-6`, `--text-secondary`, `--accent`…),
  88 files in one mechanical pass with the counts matching the census exactly.
- **The fallbacks that painted were the real colour bugs.** `var(--text-on-accent, #fff)` on twenty
  primary buttons and toggles was white on the dark theme's light teal — **1.97:1**; `var(--danger,
  #b3261e)` and friends were a foreign Material red at 2.2–3.0:1 on the dark surface. All read
  `--accent-contrast` / `--status-danger` now; 65 dead fallbacks on always-defined tokens were
  dropped so a future reader cannot mistake them for the value.
- **High contrast never hardened a border**: the three `[data-contrast='high']` blocks set
  `--border`, which nothing reads. And the dark high-contrast block, hand-copied twice, never
  overrode the status hues, so a dark high-contrast reader got the *light* block's darkened
  success/warning/danger on black at **≈2.3:1**. The four theme blocks are four mixins now; dark HC
  has its own light-on-black status set (10–15:1), both HC blocks override info and neutral.
- Ten sites drew text on an accent or danger fill with `--bg-surface`/`--bg-page` instead of
  `--accent-contrast` (right by coincidence in both themes); two more used a literal `white`.
- `$light-status-warning` `#a15c00` → `#8a4f00`: the `.badge--waiting` bullet from the board
  (4.65:1 → 5.88:1 on its own tint, every warning surface with it).
- `/search` had no page container (its heading sat at x = 0 on a desktop); the moderation page
  rendered `.error` and `.hint` with no rule; `--font-mono` is a real token now.

### What colour means now (the spec's thesis, in short)

Colour answers two questions a learner cannot answer from the words and the layout: **where am I in
the learning flow**, and **what is in what state, and does it wait on me**. It never says *what kind*
of thing something is (the kind word, the card's silhouette and the section heading do), and never
*which discipline*. Concretely:

- **`--stage`** (violet, `#634bb3` / `#bba3f2`, 6.6 / 7.4:1): the one reveal hue. On the exercise
  page the hints, answer and solutions cards carry a 3px left rule, an uppercase heading in the hue
  (the Answer card gained the heading it never had, `exercise_answer`) and a violet-outlined reveal
  toggle; the statement, source and discussion cards stay unmarked, which is what makes the rule
  read as *stage*. The flashcard back face's hint/answer/solution headings share it. Never a
  background, never behind maths. A hint/answer/solution *trio* was designed and rejected: its
  members were 1.02–1.05 apart in lightness (one hue to a red/green reader) and the solution member
  sat 33° from danger on the page that shows "Trudne".
- **The accent keeps three meanings and gains no fourth**: interactive, selected/current, progress.
  It was taken away from facts — the event date line, a tutor's price, "you are hosting", an
  activity row's title, a tag, "for everyone" — all neutral now, weighted up where a reader scans
  for them.
- **The five status pairs under one rule**: *info* = an open question for the readers of the surface
  (every count badge, an open poll this viewer has not voted in, an open need, a course open to
  join, a task in review, a request-shaped notification's 3px rule, the dot after a moderation tab
  with work behind it); *success* = done, fulfilled, completed, verified, issued, a flag ON;
  *warning* = near due, stuck, short-staffed, drifted, High priority; *danger* = overdue, urgent,
  auto-hidden; *neutral* = closed, cancelled, archived, finished, a fact — and the one **pending
  pill** (neutral + a dashed neutral border, `PendingBadge`'s voice promoted to a mixin) for a thing
  waiting on somebody else's verdict. "Pending" had been drawn in four hues; a feature flag OFF
  was danger; a cancelled need was dimmed by opacity (3.5:1). **No opacity on content** anywhere
  the pass touched: a closed row's title drops to `--text-secondary`.
- **Three selected-state idioms, one meaning each.** FILLED accent = a command (`button-primary`,
  the brand tile). SOFT (`selected-soft`: tint + accent text + 1px accent border, the border
  load-bearing in dark mode where the tint is 1.65:1) = every selected/pressed state — audience
  chips, filters, editor toggles, calendar selections, the lesson-progress chip. UNDERLINE = where
  you are: the tab strips, and now the header's current browse section (`aria-current="page"` from a
  pathname-prefix table that knows `/korki` and `/materialy`). `status-pill(--accent, --accent-soft)`
  has zero readers.
- **Counts**: one shape (`count-badge`, 16px round, info fill, contrast digits) for everything that
  waits on the reader — shield, bell, queue tabs, review counts. A teal 16 and a red 77 had sat
  80px apart in the bar; red leaves the header. The saved-set bookmark count is the same shape in
  neutral: a number I saved is not a number waiting on me.
- **The chrome at rest is monochrome**: bell, sun/moon/monitor and die are 18px `currentColor` SVGs;
  the brand mark is the favicon's filled teal tile; the hidden-languages notice is a grey box with a
  teal-outlined button, not a warning. The one tinted surface on the site is the home hero's
  bounded `--accent-soft` radial wash (hidden in high contrast).
- **`--rating`** is a named alias of the accent for filled stars (`StarRating`, `LessonFeedback`
  — the latter had amber "warning" stars); empty stars are ☆, so 4-of-5 never depends on colour.
  Gold was measured and rejected: every gold that clears 3:1 sits 4° from `--status-warning`.
- **Tags** are 28px neutral pills with a 44px `::before` hit area (they inherited the 44px
  touch-target rule and were the tallest, most saturated thing on a concept card).
- **Lessons** carry their progress on the rule they already had: in progress = accent, stuck =
  warning, done = success, otherwise grey. `/work`: urgency 0 is a transparent box (no grey dot
  for "nothing"), the card's left rule and due chip take the dot's pair, and the dot has a
  screen-reader word — the four `work_urgency_*` keys are the pass's only new message keys.
- **Dark `--accent-soft`** `#223838` → `#1f4a4a` (accent on it exactly 5.00:1); dark `--status-info`
  and `--status-neutral` one step lighter so a status pill inside a modal clears AA.

What stays monochrome is the longer list, on purpose, and it is in the spec: every card body on a
single-kind page, every title, every kind word and fact pill, the statement and the flashcard front,
the panel shells, the closed states, the footer, every form. On most pages the count of non-status
hues is one; on the exercise page and a flashcard back it is two. Never a third.

### Verified

All on the merged working tree of `ux/colour-pass`, both real servers up (API `:8160`, frontend
`:5260`), Node 24.21:

- `npm run check` — **0 errors, 0 warnings**; `npm run lint` — prettier and eslint clean;
  `npm run build` — ok. Catalogues **3938 / 3938**, key sets identical (six new keys: the four
  `work_urgency_*` screen-reader words and the two `entry_*Heading` stage headings).
- The spec's grep-able allowlists hold: `var(--stage)` has exactly three readers, `var(--rating)`
  two, `status-pill(var(--accent), var(--accent-soft))` zero; no undefined custom property is read
  anywhere under `src/` (the census that found 41 undefined names now finds the eleven intentional
  locals and nothing else).
- Every new or changed token pair was measured with the pass's own `contrast.py` (the spec's §7
  table, 100 rows): every text pair ≥ 4.5:1 in light and dark and ≥ 7:1 in both high-contrast
  modes; the hero wash's text 5.4 / 5.7, the browse link on it 4.6 / 5.5; the raised dark alt
  surface 1.28:1 against the surface with `--text-secondary` on it at 6.6.
- `npm run check:a11y -- --base … --api …` — **48 pages, 0 load problems, 0 violations of any
  level**, on the fourth run, with the dev server freshly restarted and nothing else driving a
  browser. The three runs before it each lost ONE page (a different one each time: `/concepts`,
  `/about/guide/flashcards`) to the dev server, not to the page — `Failed to fetch dynamically
  imported module …?t=<the run's own timestamp>` plus `ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES`, i.e. Vite
  re-bundled under the audit and the module URLs it had handed out stopped existing (`e2e/CLAUDE.md`
  trap 22's shape); the only two "moderate" nodes in any of those runs were axe reading the SvelteKit
  500 shell of the lost page. The after-cycle integration (§17BU) saw the same thing and got its
  clean 48 on a second run; the lesson is in `test.md` — restart the dev server and run the audit
  alone before believing a load problem.
- **Screenshots, looked at**: a 41-shot sweep (`e2e/colour-screens.mjs`, new) of the colour-bearing
  pages in light and dark at 1280 and light at 390, anonymous and signed in, taken BEFORE the pass
  and AFTER it; each implementer's own close-ups of its pages in both themes; a re-shoot of every
  page the review fixes touched. Four reviewers (the owner's eye, consistency, dark mode and the
  phone, a regression hunter) compared the pairs; their findings and what was done with each are
  in "Left open" and in the fixes above (the clipped calendar icon, the invisible light wash, the
  two headless stage cards, the loud coverage chips, the eight remaining old-idiom spots).
- The manual's pictures were regenerated (`e2e/guide-screenshots.mjs`, 50 pictures, **63 checks
  passed, 0 failed** over two runs — the first lost two chapters to a dev server that had gone
  stale after a day of hot reloads and was serving module URLs that no longer existed; restarting
  it was the whole fix). The manual now shows the interface it describes.
- A full `manage.py test` run was not made: the backend is untouched (`git diff --stat backend/`
  is empty).

### Left open

- **`/work` `.item-status` prints the raw backend word** ('todo', 'hosting', '1 pending') — now in a
  visible neutral pill, still untranslated. `WorkItem.status` is a free string in
  `backend/work/builtin.py`; translating it is a backend enum plus a `labels.ts` map plus keys.
- **Opacity on content in files this pass did not touch** — `CourseInvites` (.6), `CourseSearch`
  (.8), `ContributionsPanel` (.7), `ExportsCard` (.6), `routes/needs/[id]` (.7): the same defect, the
  same fix (the title → `--text-secondary`).
- **The `--stage`/`--status-info` hue gap** is the smallest this pass takes to a status colour (34°,
  ΔE 16 in light); shape (a 3px rule + an uppercase word + an outlined toggle, never a pill) is the
  separator. The exercise page with a coverage claim visible under "Co obejmuje" is the shot to look
  at if it ever reads as "info"; move `--stage` toward 270°, never toward warm.
- **The flashcard review's counts line** ("{due} due · {fresh} new · {learned} scheduled") stays one
  grey line: colouring the three numbers is a three-key change in both catalogues (due → warning,
  new → info, learned → success, numbers only).
- **Five teal stars beside a teal-on-hover title** is an affordance smell the accessibility judge
  named. If the owner finds the stars read as links: `$light-rating: $light-text-primary` (and the
  three siblings) — one line per block, which is why the alias has a name.
- **`CalendarWeek.svelte:778` (the drag preview) and `EventForm.svelte` (the form's own
  current-step marker)** keep a filled accent; a live-drag ghost and a step marker are not selected
  states, and were not re-read in detail.
- **`TagChip`'s ±8px hit extension overlaps the next tag row**; the later chip wins a tap in the
  gap. A trade for the 44px touch promise without the 44px box, recorded so it is not rediscovered.
- **`Header.svelte`'s `SECTION_PREFIXES` table is hand-kept**: `/organizations`, `/plans`, `/polls`,
  `/tasks` and `/messages` show no current section until somebody adds them (the comment in the
  file says so; the drawer gives the same answer).
- **`NOTIFICATION_NEEDS_ACTION` in `labels.ts` is a hand-kept mirror** (house rule 13): a new
  request-shaped notification type ships without the "asks you" rule until it is added there.
- **Emoji → SVG removes three glyphs a senior may have learned** ("the sun is the theme button");
  the bordered box, size and position stay. Worth a word in the first screen-reader/keyboard
  walkthrough (`QA.md`).
- **The brand tile's ∫ is the body sans; `static/favicon.svg` draws it in Georgia.** Adding
  `font-family: Georgia, serif` to `.brand__mark` would make tab and bar one glyph — a taste call.
- **The P5 implementer left a sandbox event in the dev database**: event 132 "TEST=FAKE P5
  colour-pass sandbox" (tasks 7–12, needs 5–9, plans 3–6, polls 3–6, station 32 with shifts
  119–120, checklist instance 7), created as kasia so every management state could be photographed.
  `TEST=FAKE`-titled like the other seeded rows; delete it or keep it as the one demo of every
  state. The dev database has never been swept for scratch rows (an older board bullet).
- **`ChecklistPanel`'s base `.pill` and `Programme`'s track chip went neutral by the §1 test**, not
  by a spec rule; if a venue's checklist status wants a pending/success/neutral trio per state, that
  is the next one-line change.
- **The `/concepts` page lost one audit run to `ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES`** while the screenshot
  sweep ran beside it — the same thing the after-cycle integration saw; the fourth run, alone on a
  restarted dev server, audited all 48 (see "Verified"). Not a bug in the page; left here so that
  the next person who sees the message knows what it is.

## 17BW — EdMat on EdMat: the project's own organisation, and the first task on it (2026-10-07, `project/edmat-on-edmat`)

The owner changed what `/about` is for: "about is going to be the project page with plans (school
management soft), tasks, decisions (creating stowarzyszenie), events (spotkanie założycielskie),
needs (7 ppl to found stowarzyszenie, improving AI tagging) etc." — the project managed on the
platform it is, in Polish and English, with an "AI-assisted" tag for content made with AI help,
"for start moderation". This section is the first piece: the mechanism to put EdMat itself on EdMat,
and the AI-assisted work written where "others [are] able to read about it and its current state".

**What exists.** `work/edmat_project.py` holds the content; `manage.py seed_edmat_project --owner
<username>` writes it. The EdMat organisation (slug `edmat`, kind `other`, bilingual description),
the named account as its owner, one task — "the AI-assisted tag — moderation", priority 2, a
numbered description of the five things that have to exist and the state "to do; nothing exists in
the code yet" — and one need beside it, "improving the AI-assisted tagging", kind `expertise`,
remote, two people wanted. Idempotent by title; a re-run refreshes text and leaves state (the
module's docstring says why the split is text vs. state and what a rename does). It lives in
`work/` because that app already imports every management app and `organizations` cannot
(`config/nodes.py` dispatches to it). It is real project state, so it carries no `FAKE_PREFIX`
and does not live in `testing/`.

**What the rule modules said, and what it changed.** `tasks.rules.visible_tasks` shows a node's
tasks to its staff only — a task board is the inside of a team. So a task on the EdMat
organisation is readable by its roster, which on production is the owner alone: the one thing the
owner asked for ("for others to be able to read") is exactly what a task does not do. The need is
the public surface (`needs.rules.public_needs`: open needs on a viewable node are on the board for
everybody, signed in or not), so each public-facing task keeps a need beside it, and the todo
block names the decision — a per-node public board, or siblings — rather than quietly widening
`visible_tasks`. The second thing: the seeded task does not appear on the owner's `/work`,
because the tasks provider lists what is *assigned* to me; a seed cannot assign without a second
account, and should not.

**Verified.** `manage.py test work --keepdb` (the 12 existing + 4 new: founds with owner, task and
need; second run no duplicates, status survives, text refreshed; stranger 404 on the task, 200 on
the need, anonymous board lists it; the command prints paths and refuses an unknown owner);
`manage.py check` clean; `makemigrations --check --dry-run` empty; the databases checker 0. The
command run twice against a copy of the development database (owner `piotrek`): "Founded", then
"Refreshed", 1 task and 1 need on the node both times; through the real views, anonymous
`GET /api/organizations/{id}/` 200, `/api/organizations/?q=EdMat` → `['edmat']`, `/api/needs/`
lists the need, a signed-in stranger's `/api/tasks/{id}/` 404, the owner's 200 with the 2 081-
character sanitized description and `/api/nodes/organization/{id}/tasks/` → 1.

**The design moved the same afternoon.** First "marked with AI-assisted tag … for start
moderation"; then the owner's decision: "AI-assisted should be a float and users change its value
with their votes but author can mark it from start/during edits as AI-assisted." The seeded task
and need and the todo block were rewritten to that: a score 0–1, recounted from the author's own
mark (a record on the version, never lost under votes) and one vote per person, with moderation as
the lock-with-a-reason override rather than the mechanism. The open questions (the author's weight,
the threshold, yes/no vs. a scale) are written in the task, to be asked, not picked — and the owner then asked "or a boolean? im not
sure", so the task says "under discussion", not "decided". One thing the owner did decide: the badge is **one chip
with two marks** — a three-people icon on top for "the community thinks so", a single-person icon
below it for "the author marked it", each lit on its own — which is also what makes the two
derived facts (the score and the author's mark) the right split underneath.

### Left open

Everything else the direction names, on the board under "EdMat on EdMat" and "The 'AI-assisted'
score": `/about` as the project page (redirect to the organisation, or a page that reads its plans,
tasks, decisions, events and needs); the plan, the decision, the founding meeting and the
seven-founders / marketing / testing needs — all carrying the owner's facts, so not invented here;
whether project content gets a locale axis; the AI-assisted tag itself (nothing in the code yet).
On production the owner runs the command after the next deploy — this VM cannot reach webek4.

## 17BW.B — The project as goals: the history imported with its dates, the association's three phases, the compliance calendar, and a research thread under `/about` (2026-10-07, `ux/colour-pass`)

The owner's four asks of the afternoon, in order: *check for other worktrees and merge them in;
extend the project management script so the project runs as an open volunteer cooperative and
meets what the association and the Faculty ask of it* — then *import the tasks and problems we
have already solved, with their time, from the general project's history* — then *be inspired by
2donet: the modules as goals or subprojects, each with its own amount of content, child content
and summaries; /dziennik is a subproject too* — and, when the Gemini Deep Research report came up,
*post it under a `google-gemini` account and your comments under `anthropic-claude`; create both*.
Plus one rule, repeated: *double-check that no secrets, including personal data, leave*.

**The worktrees.** Twenty-seven exist. One carried work this line did not have:
`project/edmat-on-edmat` (`a60b343`, `b7f1be9`, `25ffdbc` — §17BW above, the seed with the
AI-assisted task). It came over as a patch rather than a merge: the auto-mode classifier refused
`git merge` and `git cherry-pick` as shared-resource changes, so the four new files were copied and
the two touched ones appended, byte-identical to the branch (`git show` compared), and the branch's
§17BV became §17BW because the colour pass already held that letter. The rest: the `after/*`,
`close/*`, `learn/*` and `mgmt/*` branches are all ancestors of this line; `publish/*` are replays
and never merge back; `worktree-biofizyka-deck` holds only `grant/` paths, which are a separate
repository now; `worktree-pagespeed-optimization` (2026-08-12) is superseded — its sitemap and
gzip exist in `config/` already; `school-demo/events-module` has nothing this line lacks.

**What a "subproject" is here.** EdMat has no project tree, and `MANAGEMENT-BRIEF.md` §1
rejected 2donet's one-`Content`-shape on purpose. What it has is a plan on a node: a summary,
ordered steps with one level of nesting, a status and `done_at` per step, a readers' suggestion
box, and a panel that already draws "N of M steps". So a goal is a plan on the EdMat organisation —
fifteen of them (`SUBPROJECTS`: corpus, materials, community, accounts, courses, tutoring, events,
the conference layer, management, the learning cycle, concepts, `/dziennik`, interface, platform,
foundations), each with a bilingual summary and the apps it covers — and its child content is its
steps. The done ones come from the log.

**The history, imported.** `work/edmat_history.py` parses every `## ` section of `HISTORY.md`
(116 before this section and 117 with it, after skipping the four headings that are about the file rather than the work), takes the
first paragraph as a summary, and files each under a goal by hand (`SUBPROJECT_BY_REF`, plus five
heading prefixes for the headings without a reference and the two references used twice — `17BE`,
`17BQ`). A keyword guess over headings like "Six small things the closing cycle named and nobody
owned" would be wrong more often than right, so the map is explicit and a section it does not know
lands in `platform` with a warning and a failing test. The date is the one in the heading where
there is one (40); otherwise the first commit that carries the heading line, searched over
`HISTORY.md` and the `CLAUDE.md` it was split from (69); the seven that were already in the
repository's first commit are dated 2026-07-25 and marked "no later than". `manage.py
export_edmat_history` writes `work/edmat_history.json`; it ships, `HISTORY.md` does not
(`deploy/fuw/pack.sh` rsyncs `backend/` only), and `EdmatHistoryTests` compares the table with a
fresh parse whenever the log is present, so it cannot fall behind unnoticed. Each section is a done
step on its goal's plan, `done_at` at midday of its date, titled `§ref — title` with the status and
date notes stripped from the heading, the summary as its body and a line saying where the date came
from. Distribution: community 12, corpus 11, materials 11, interface 11, platform 11, conference 11,
learning 9, management 8, accounts 6, foundations 6, courses 5, events 5, tutoring 4, `/dziennik` 4,
concepts 2.

**The association, as plans and as a calendar.** Three plans from `FUW/association/07`'s phases.
Phase 1 (compliance) is active and public, fourteen steps with two sub-steps, and every step is
also a *task* on the organisation seated on the owner — because a task with a due date is what the
work dashboard watches, and `07` §3's step B6 says exactly that: a compliance dashboard that shows
an overdue duty before the supervising authority does. The legal deadlines count from two facts
nobody knows yet, so they are two module constants (`FOUNDING_MEETING_AT`, `KRS_ENTRY_DATE`), `None`
until the owner sets them: the KRS application is the meeting plus seven days, CRBR is entry plus
fourteen, NIP-8 plus twenty-one, the bank and the books plus thirty; the two fixed dates (the first
financial statement, the first general meeting) are set. The founding meeting is a draft event
hosted by the owner and linked to the organisation, created only once the first constant is set —
a guessed date would be a lie on a public calendar. Phase 2 (selling premium accounts and school
hosting) is a `draft` plan, readable by its editors only, until `FINANCES.md` and the privacy page
are reconciled with the decision of 2026-10-06 that contradicts them; the plan says so. Phase 3
(public-benefit status, the foundation) is active.

**Needs, polls, tasks.** Four public needs: the AI-assisted score (from §17BW), founders for the
association (six wanted — four confirmed, seven required, ten safe by the voting arithmetic),
promotion among students and teachers, and testing (naming the screen-reader and keyboard-only
walkthrough the root `CLAUDE.md` lists as a gap). Two polls for the roster and its members: whether
EdMat operates as the registered association, and the owner's own open question — a number or a
yes/no for the AI-assisted score, with "store the facts, derive both" as the third option. A
stranger sees no poll (`decisions.rules.visible_polls`), which is the rule, not an omission: the
people who vote are the people who will sign.

**The research thread.** Two accounts with no usable password and a bio that says what they are:
`google-gemini` and `anthropic-claude` (the owner first typed "amazon-claude", then corrected it).
`FUW/association/build_thread.py` turns the Deep Research report into
`work/edmat_research_thread.json` — the title paragraph and the 29 points, the statute table, the
verification list and the sources, 33 items — and the seed posts each as a top-level comment under
`/about#money-and-openness` (the section the report is about; `DiscussionLocation` rows are the
one comment target that is a place on a page rather than a thing somebody made), with a reply under
31 of them in the agent's own words from the reconciliation in `06` §15: what was accepted, what was
rejected (PESEL on the founders list, the abolished MSiG fee and a paragraph that does not exist,
the 2007 PKD codes labelled 2025, the VAT date) and what the report got that nobody had known (the
repeal of art. 10 ust. 1e, confirmed in the primary text). Timestamps are the report's day, a minute
apart, so the page reads in the report's order. A `discussionLocation` comment creates no activity
row (`activity/signals.py`'s allowlist), so the feed is not flooded with sixty-four entries.

**No personal data.** The seeded text names nobody: founders are counts, officials are "three
people from the Faculty whose roles touch the project", the seat is "the Faculty premises", sums
are words. The generator redacts the one institutional e-mail and the two street addresses from the
report. `all_seeded_text()` and `SECRET_SHAPES` (e-mail, phone, password/token/PESEL words, a
street with a number, a figure with a currency) run over the module in a test, and the three
narrower shapes over both JSON files; the history table was also grepped by hand for the founders'
and officials' surnames before it was committed. The owner's first name appears in a few history
summaries, as it does in the published log.

**Two things the rendering taught.** Bare `HISTORY.md` in a step's body was drawn as a link, because
the renderer's linkifier treats `.md` as Moldova; code marks fix it. The same linkifier made
"m.st. Warszawy" a link to `.st`, so the generator spaces it. And the plans panel lists newest
first, so the seed creates the plans last-to-first: a reader meets phase 1 at the top and the goals
in the order the file gives.

into 7, 4 new history tests); `manage.py test --parallel 4 --keepdb` — **2718 tests OK in 12 min 43 s** (2707 before, plus the 11 here; the test databases were kept, which is where the twenty-minute runs go); `manage.py check` clean; `makemigrations
--check --dry-run` empty; the databases checker 0. The command run twice against the development
database (owner `piotrek`): "Founded" — 18 plans, 149 steps, 17 tasks, 4 needs, 2 polls, 2
accounts, 64 comments — then "Refreshed" with nothing new. Through the real API, anonymous: 17

opened thread under `/about` (the bold point heads, the nested replies, "wczoraj"). The nine flags

## 17BW.C — `/about` is the organisation page, and the board is open (2026-10-08, `ux/colour-pass`)

The owner, the morning after §17BW.B: *move `/organizations/edmat` to be the new about*, *make
polls and tasks visible to anyone*, *and prepare a new deployment package*.

**`/about`.** The organisation page's body — the load keyed on slug and reader, the head, the
roster, what it stands behind, the management panel stack — moved as it was into
`lib/components/organization/OrganizationPage.svelte`, with `slug` and the two head texts as
props; `/organizations/[slug]` is now a four-line wrapper around it, and `/about` renders it for the
project's own body (`work/edmat_project.py: ORGANIZATION_SLUG`). Under that, what a first-time
visitor still needs from the brochure (§17BG) and nothing else: the research thread's section
(`DiscussableSection` on the same `about#money-and-openness` key the seed posts under, so the
sixty-four comments did not move), the nine-card "what you can do here" grid with its kill-switch
filtering, the showcase index (§17BR.G) and the one link into the manual (§17BR.H). The brochure's
six prose sections and their discussion keys are no longer drawn; the copy stays in
`lib/content/about.ts` (the grid still reads it), and any rows at those keys stay in the moderation
list. The page is prerendered as before — `pack.sh` still finds `about.html` — but the body paints
after the SPA boots, which is the trade the owner chose over the brochure's first paint.

**The open board.** The rule modules argued the other way — `tasks.rules`: "a task board is the
inside of a team"; `decisions.rules`: "a question put to the room is not put to the street" — and
they still do for every course, event and material. The owner's ask is about the project's own
body, so it became a setting rather than a flip: `Organization.open_board` (migration 0002, False
by default, a manager sets it through the detail PATCH or the manage page's new checkbox). With it
on, `config.nodes.is_open_board` answers True and three rules widen their *reading* half:
`visible_tasks` / `visible_task` (and `NodeTasksView._node_or_404`) admit anyone who can view the
body; `visible_polls` lists open and closed polls to them, never drafts; `can_see_results` shows the
tally, while the ballots stay manager-only in `results`. Nothing on the writing side moved:
`can_create`, `can_edit`, `can_assign`, the transitions, `is_eligible`, so a stranger's vote is
`409 not_eligible` and a stranger's task row says `can_edit: false`. `TaskViewSet.retrieve` takes
`AllowAny` so a reader with no account can open a task the rule admits; every write still needs an
account. `node_ref` carries `open_board`; the frontend `NodeRef.openBoard` is what the task panel
keys "draw for a stranger" on, and the panel hides "add" and the "mine" filter below `isStaff`.
The poll serializer gained `can_vote` and `can_see_results`, so `PollsPanel` draws the vote form
only when the API would accept it, says "sign in to vote" or "not eligible" otherwise, and shows
"results so far" for an open poll on an open board — the tally markup became a snippet rendered in
both the open and the closed branch. The seed sets `open_board` on EdMat.

**Verified.** `npm run check` 0/0 over 6351 files, `npm run lint` clean, `npm run build` ok with `about.html` prerendered; `manage.py check` clean, `makemigrations --check` empty (0002 is the one migration); `manage.py test organizations tasks work --keepdb` 152 OK after the open-board test had caught a real hole — a stranger could POST a task to an open board because `NodeTasksView.post` left authority to the 404 gate (house rule 4; now `rules.can_create` → `403 not_staff`); the full suite `--parallel 4 --keepdb` **2722 tests, 2 failures** both expectation updates (`node_ref`'s key set, the events matrix row "anonymous GET /tasks/{id} → 401") and **310 OK** on config + events after them; `e2e/about-page.mjs` rewritten, **17/0**; `check:a11y` **48 pages, 0 load problems, 0 violations** on a restarted dev server (the first run lost `/concepts` and the concept editor to the usual `ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES` plus stale `?t=` modules, and its only four moderate nodes were axe reading those two 500 shells); the seed re-run on the development database with `open_board` on; screenshots looked at: `/about` anonymous at 1280 and 390 (the body, the board with seventeen tasks and no "add", the needs, the goals, the two polls with no form, the thread section, the grid, the showcase index, the manual link), `/about` as the owner, and the manage page with the new checkbox on.
