## 17BV.A — The hero wash stops being a rectangle (2026-10-08, `ux/colour-pass`)

The one wash §17BV added was painted by `.hero::before` with `inset: 0`, so its box was the hero,
and the hero sits inside `.page` — `max-width: 1100px; margin: 0 auto; padding: var(--space-4)`.
The gradient is an ellipse centred at 28% of that box's height reaching 36% of it, which puts its
top edge 8% ABOVE the box: clipped. On the home page that drew a straight horizontal line across
the full width of the content column, 24px below the header, where the tint began all at once.
Measured on a 1920×430 capture at the page centre, the background went 247,247,251 at y=82 to
239,243,246 at y=86 — a step, not a gradient. Nobody had looked at the top strip on its own.

**The fix is two properties and one line in the layout.** `.hero::before` keeps its stops and gets
a box that is not the content column: `inset-block: calc(-1 * var(--space-4)) 0` carries it up over
`.page`'s own top padding so the clip lands exactly on the header's bottom edge, where it is not an
edge at all, and `inset-inline: calc(50% - 50vw)` takes it out to both window edges. `vw` counts the
scrollbar, so the box overhangs the visible width by a scrollbar; `.app-main` gets `overflow-x:
clip` to absorb it. **`clip`, not `hidden`** — `hidden` would make `.app-main` a scroll container and
every `position: sticky` inside a page (the branch page's filters sidebar, the booking week's day
header) would then stick to a box that never scrolls, which looks exactly like sticky having been
deleted; `overflow-x: hidden` also coerces `overflow-y` to `auto` and takes the same sticky away,
where `overflow-x: clip` leaves `overflow-y: visible` alone.

The horizontal radius became a length (`40rem`) rather than `60%`. Measured against a 100vw box a
percentage grows with the window — 1536px of radius on a 2560px monitor — and flattens the glow into
a band across the top of the page. 40rem is what 60% of the 1100px column already came to, so the
shape over the column is the one the colour pass judged; it simply no longer stops at the column's
edge. The vertical radius stays a percentage, because it should follow the height of the thing it
is lighting.

**Verified** (house rule 2, with both servers up): `npm run check` 6355 files 0/0, `npm run lint`
clean, `npm run build` exit 0. A browser pass at 1280×900 light and dark, 1920×1000 and 390×844:
20/20 checks — no horizontal page scroll at any of the four (`scrollWidth == clientWidth`), the
wash's box reaching x=0 and the right edge exactly, `inset-block-start` resolving to -24px, no page
errors — plus the screenshots looked at, including the top strip at 3× where the old edge was. The
before/after pair was captured by re-imposing the old rule in the page itself, so the two shots
differ in nothing else. Sticky: on `/branches/analiza-matematyczna` the real `.filters` sidebar sits
at `top: 80` after a 1000px scroll (its own offset), `.app-main` computes `overflow-x: clip` with
`overflow-y: visible`, and an injected sticky probe pins at 0. A `position: fixed` overlay appended
inside `.app-main` still measures 0,0,1280,800 — the Lightbox/modal shape is not clipped.

**Contrast is unmoved**, which is the point worth recording: the bleed changes where the wash ends,
not the tint at its centre, and the centre samples the same rgb(214,233,233) light / rgb(27,67,67)
dark before and after. At the elements themselves the worst ratio is 5.46 (the browse link, which
sits on the transparent tail and did not change at all); the h1 reads 13.54 light / 10.29 dark and
the subtitle 5.76 / 7.00.

**Left open.** The wash still ends in a straight line *at the header's bottom edge* rather than
continuing behind it — invisible today because the header's background is opaque, and a real edge
again the day it becomes translucent. On a phone the ellipse is now wider than the screen, so the
tint reaches both side edges instead of fading inside them; that is what "bleed" was asked for and
it looks right in the 390px capture, but it is a taste call somebody may want back. Only the home
page has a wash (`--hero-wash` has exactly one call site), so nothing else needed the same fix.


## 17BX — The "AI-assisted" mark, and the management layer stops being glued together (2026-10-08, `ux/colour-pass`)

Three things the owner asked for in three messages on the same morning, built together because they
land on the same two pages and because the second and third are one feature once you look at them.

### A — The "AI-assisted" mark (`provenance/`)

The owner, 2026-10-08:

> *"cant mark/vote on AI-assisted exercises and its contents (the exercise itelsf, tip, solution,
> and even comments and reviews: make sure each has a meatballs menu where mark as AI-assisted and
> how % sure are you about that, also report, reply, etc (reply higher than AI-assisted, also some
> quick mod actions)"*

**This had a spec already, written by the owner and seeded into the platform itself.**
`work/edmat_project.py: TASKS[0]` is a task on the EdMat organisation, dated 2026-10-07, titled
*"Wskaźnik „z pomocą AI" — autor oznacza, społeczność głosuje"*, and its first line was **"to do;
nothing exists in the code yet"**. It names six deliverables and leaves three questions to the
organisation's own poll (`POLLS[1]`, still open). The message above settles one of them: a vote is
**how sure you are, 0–100%**, not a yes/no — which also picks the third of the three options the
poll offers ("store the facts, derive both readings"), because a confidence is a fact and both the
badge and a filter can be derived from it.

**Three tables, not one**, because three different people are speaking and conflating them is how a
badge starts lying about who claimed what:

- `AuthorMark` — the author's own disclosure. One row per target; `assisted=False` is a real stored
  answer and deliberately not the same as having no row ("the author says no" and "nobody has asked
  the author" read identically to a boolean and completely differently to a person).
- `AssistanceVote` — one reader's confidence, 0–100, one row per person per target, changeable.
  Zero means "I am not at all convinced", which is a vote against on the same scale rather than a
  second field.
- `ScoreLock` — a moderator ending the argument at a value, with a reason that is not blank-able
  (house rule 6). It replaces the community reading and never the author's mark: that is a record
  of something a person said about their own work.

**The reading is two marks and one number** — the owner's decision of 2026-10-07, kept as the shape
of `rules.summaries_for`'s return value: a three-people icon (the community), a single-person icon
(the author), each lighting on its own, and one percent for a filter to use. **The chip draws only
once one of the two marks is lit** (or a moderator has fixed the reading, which is also a person
standing behind it). An earlier cut drew it as soon as anybody had voted, and the screenshot is what
settled it: a chip reading "80%" off ONE vote looks exactly like a figure the community arrived at,
which is the thing `MIN_VOTES_FOR_COMMUNITY_MARK` exists to prevent. Below the threshold there is no
claim to show — the dialog says "not enough people have looked" to whoever opens it, and the person
who voted still sees their own vote there. The author's mark is
final (votes can only add the badge, never remove it) and an author's *denial* does not pull the
community reading down — it is recorded, it is shown, and the reader weighs both. A denial that
silently erased every reader's reading would make the signal worthless on exactly the content it
matters most on.

`MIN_VOTES_FOR_COMMUNITY_MARK = 3` is the same safety rail, for the same reason, as
`moderation/services.py: MIN_REPORTS_FOR_AUTO_HIDE`: a mean over one vote is one person's opinion
wearing the word "community". It and `COMMUNITY_MARK_THRESHOLD` are named constants in one module
because the owner's task lists "the vote weight and threshold" as undecided and the poll is where
they get decided.

**One batched read, not a field on four serializers.** `GET /api/ai-assistance/?targets=exercise:12,
comment:9,…` answers for every chip a page has just drawn, in four queries per kind. A
`SerializerMethodField` on `Exercise`, `SolutionEntry`, `Comment` and `Review` would have been a
GenericForeignKey aggregate per row — the N+1 — and would have put this app's import into three
others. `provideAiAssistance()` is the page-level holder the chips read from, the
`providePageDiscussions` shape, and it coalesces registrations in waves because the chips do not all
mount at once (the statement is there on first paint, the reviews land with their own fetch, the
thread after that).

**`ContentActionsMenu` is where the order lives.** Reply → mark as AI-assisted → whatever this
surface adds → report → a moderator's quick remove/restore, fixed once rather than at five call
sites, and asserted as an ORDER in the browser script rather than as a set. `CommentNode`'s own
bespoke menu was folded into it (it keeps save / link to course / copy link as its `items`), which
is what gave a comment the AI item and the quick moderator action it did not have.

`provideAiAssistance()` is called by all eight routes that render a comment thread, not just the
exercise page — a comment is a target wherever it is written, even where the material or the concept
article it hangs under is not one yet. `ContentActionsMenu` hides the AI item on a page that provided
no holder rather than opening a dialog nothing would answer, which is what makes adding a route one
line and what keeps a half-wired page from looking broken.

**The registry is deliberately shorter than `REPORT_KIND_MODELS`** — four kinds, because everything
here is a judgement about who wrote a piece of **prose**, and a tag or a venue has none. A hint and
a solution are one kind (`SolutionEntry` differs by its own `kind` field), so the four cover the
five surfaces the owner named.

**One trap worth the paragraph.** `ReviewList.svelte` renders three different review models and its
`kind` prop defaults to `'review'`, so a *material* review already falls through to that default.
Deriving the provenance target from it would have written an "AI-assisted" mark against whichever
`community.Review` happened to share the pk. The chip is gated on a separate explicit `assistKind`
prop that only the exercise page passes; both files say so.

### B — Editing a need or a poll without Django admin (`translations/`, the frontend half)

> *"cant edit task etc from aboutsubpage from frontend (has to be done using django admin - add
> meatball menu here as well)"*

Checked before building, and the answer was narrower and sharper than the complaint: the backend was
**complete** (`PlanViewSet` partial_update/destroy/transition/steps/reorder, `PollViewSet`
partial_update/destroy/options, `NeedViewSet` update) and so were the frontend services
(`updateNeed`, `updatePoll`, `deletePoll`, …) — **with no call site anywhere in the app**. A task had
its Edit on `TaskCard`, a plan had a whole edit page at `/plans/[id]`; a **need's words and a poll's
question genuinely could only be changed in Django admin**, and a draft poll could only be deleted
there. That is the "tasks etc" in the complaint.

### C — Bilingual management text, and the editor that keeps the two in step

> *"all of the tasks and other project management stuff should be bilingual: User sees the version
> in their UI language by default, if there's a newer version in a different language it says how
> much newer. mods/admins can edit and submit edit/new stuff also using translate interface you need
> to make now: side by side original and the translation (up and bottom for mobiles), so that if a
> user translates and edit/update/new content, there's no sth like "newer in PL by 4 minutes""*

B and C are one feature: the thing the meatballs "Edit" should open **is** the translate interface,
so writing a change and translating it is one submission.

What was wrong: each model had ONE `title` and ONE `description`, so being bilingual was something
you did by hand, in the field. `work/edmat_project.py: _pl_en()` is what that looked like — Polish
and English glued with a `/` and a `---` rule, and every reader of `/about` got both at once
whichever language they had chosen.

**`translations.TextVersion`**: one row per (target, locale), `is_original` marking the language it
was written in, `heading`/`body` named for their shape rather than for any one model's field
(the seven targets call them four different things). A `GenericForeignKey` plus a registry, not seven
near-identical tables in five apps — and **not** `ExerciseTranslation`'s shape, which carries a review
workflow this does not need: the people writing management text are the people who already run the
thing, and `tasks.rules.can_edit` and its siblings are already the right answer to "may you write
this". `authority.py` asks each app rather than answering, which is why a task's **assignee** may
translate the thing they are carrying.

**Five decisions worth keeping:**

1. **The model's own column survives, holding the original**, mirrored on every write. That is what
   keeps every existing reader of `Task.title` correct and untouched — the work dashboard, a
   notification body, the activity feed, an export, a `__str__`, Django admin. A target with no rows
   here behaves exactly as it did before, which is why **nothing had to be migrated and nothing had
   to guess what language a task written in 2026-09 was in**.
2. **`updated_at` is not `auto_now`.** `write_versions` stamps one timestamp across every language it
   writes, so two written together are exactly equal and there is nothing to report. Under `auto_now`
   they would save microseconds apart and the page would say "newer by 0 minutes" about content
   somebody had just written in one go — the precise thing the owner asked to be rid of.
3. **One endpoint, writing every language at once.** There is deliberately no per-language write: an
   editor that saved one language at a time would *manufacture* the staleness it exists to avoid.
4. **No read endpoint.** Every version arrives embedded in the row it belongs to, through a queryset
   that has already applied that row's own visibility — five visibility answers that would otherwise
   have needed a second copy here.
5. **No kill switch of its own.** A flag guards a feature *surface*; this is a property of five
   surfaces that each already have one.

**Two mirror-image kinds.** A poll option has a heading and no body; an organisation has a body and
no heading (its `name` is a registered name and the same in every language). The "say something in
the language you wrote it in" rule therefore falls on the body for an organisation
(`original_body_empty`), and `TranslateFields` draws one pane or two accordingly.

**The seed splits; it does not store split.** `work/edmat_project.py` still writes `_pl_en(...)` and
`'PL / EN'` — a good way to keep a bilingual source readable in one file — and now splits it on the
way in. Checked first: 58 of the 59 titles in that file contain exactly one ` / ` and the 59th is the
founding meeting's, which is an `events.Event` and not a translatable kind; `tak/nie` and `yes/no`
carry no spaces round their slash. `_find_by_title` recognises **both** the glued title an earlier
run left and the Polish one this run writes — without that, a second run against a database seeded
before the change would have duplicated every task, plan, need and poll. A test asserts the "at most
one separator" claim rather than trusting it. One real wart it uncovered: a goal's
`*Aplikacje / apps: …*` line was concatenated **after** `_pl_en`'s own rule, so splitting filed it
under English alone; it goes through `body_suffix` and is appended to both.

### D — "Which language is this written in?" becomes a picker

> *"change the way adding new exercises work: rn adding it has en language text_input by default
> even for pl interface (that's default for now btw), lets have a pick choose one from for now"*

Two forms asked for the content language as a **free text box**, and one of them pre-filled it
wrongly. Adding a hint or a solution (`SolutionEntrySection`) seeded the box from `contentLocale` —
the language the EXERCISE was being read in — so a reader with a Polish interface looking at the
English rendering got `en` pre-filled for the Polish solution they were about to type, and a typo
there is a row filed under a language nobody reads. Submitting a translation (`TranslateForm`) had
the same box with no default at all.

`ContentLocaleSelect` is now the one control, and it also replaced three hand-written
`<option value="pl">PL</option>` pairs (`/submit`, `/submit-material`, `CatalogueForm`). Five call
sites is well past house rule 13's three strikes, and the thing they duplicated — *which languages
may content be in* — is exactly the kind of list that drifts. The options are
`SUPPORTED_CONTENT_LOCALES` plus the reader's own opted-in extras plus whatever the row is already
in, which is the shape `ArticleEditor` had worked out first and this now owns.

**One rule for the default everywhere: the language you are reading the site in.** What somebody is
about to write is far better guessed by their interface than by whichever rendering of somebody
else's exercise they happen to be looking at — and it is a picker now, so a wrong guess costs one
click. `/submit` and `/submit-material` moved from a hard-coded `'pl'` to the same rule; for a
Polish reader (the default interface) that changes nothing, and for an English one it stops being
quietly wrong.

`TranslateForm` additionally takes `existingLocales` and leaves out what the exercise already has —
offering to translate something into the language it is already in is not an offer. **`exclude` may
never empty the list**, though, and the first wiring did exactly that: the test exercise was
published in both languages, every option was filtered out, and the select rendered with nothing in
it. A re-translation of an existing language is a legitimate pending row anyway (the backend's
partial unique constraint only ever allows one PUBLISHED row per locale), so the component falls
back to the whole list rather than to none.

**"For now" is the owner's own word and is the honest limit**, recorded in the component: a content
locale is a free string server-side and the root CLAUDE.md says that axis is unbounded on purpose.
A bounded picker is better than an unbounded text box today; it is not a schema decision.

A browser probe confirmed all three (and caught e2e trap 6 doing it — the first `select` on
`/submit` is the HEADER's interface-language picker, which has the same EN/PL options and whose
value *is* the interface locale, so an unscoped locator reported the header as if it were the form
field): `/submit` opens on the interface language, the hint composer opens on `pl` for a Polish
interface even while the exercise is being read in English, and the translate form offers only the
language the exercise is missing.

### The one the owner caught before it shipped

The runbook for this bundle has to say "re-run `seed_edmat_project` after applying", because that is
what splits the already-seeded production rows. The owner read that and asked the right question:

> *"wdym? each time we apply on server we will rerun the seed script?! its going to overwrite my
> edits i do on production on the desc of edmat"*

It would have. The seed is idempotent in the sense of "creates nothing twice", and it refreshes its
text on every run — which was harmless while nobody could edit that text, and this is the very
bundle that makes it editable. Every deployment would have thrown the owner's own words away.

**`write_versions(keep_edited=True)`** is the fix, and `seed_edmat_project` is its only caller.
`TextVersion.written_by` is null for a row the seed wrote and set for one a person saved through the
editor, so the two are told apart by the data rather than by a flag somebody has to remember to set.
With it on, every language with a person's name on it is skipped entirely — not updated, not
deleted, not even re-stamped, so its `updated_at` keeps saying when the PERSON wrote it and the
staleness reading stays honest. It is per LANGUAGE and not per row: rewrite the Polish of a task and
the seed keeps your Polish and goes on maintaining the English.

Two things fell out of testing it rather than reasoning about it:

- **The column drifted from the version.** A protected original is skipped by the write loop, so the
  first cut simply did not mirror anything — and a column an earlier run had already clobbered would
  have stayed wrong for ever. It now reads the person's row back and mirrors from *that*, which also
  self-healed the dev VM's stale description.
- **The organisation's `description` was being refreshed behind `keep_edited`'s back**, by the
  `Organization.objects.update_or_create(defaults={**ORGANIZATION})` that founds the body. The two
  `TextVersion` rows survived a seed run and the column did not. `description` is out of those
  defaults now; name, kind, city, website and `open_board` are still seed-owned.

Proven on the dev VM the way the owner would experience it: edit the description through the
editor, run the seed, read it back — the edit is there, in both languages and in the column — then
delete the rows and run the seed again to get the seeded wording back, which is the documented and
only route. Four tests cover it (`translations.tests.KeepEditedTests`), including three consecutive
seed runs over an edit.

**And two bugs the same exercise found**, both of which would have reached production:

- **A heading was being entity-escaped.** `TextVersion.save()` ran `config.sanitize` over both
  halves, and `bleach` escapes rather than strips: `i18n & content` became `i18n &amp; content`,
  which a reader sees literally. Worse, the seed looks its rows up by title and the mirrored title
  no longer matched the file's, so a second run created a **duplicate of every plan step whose
  heading contained an `&`** — ten of them on the dev VM, found by running the seed twice. The body
  is still sanitized; a heading is plain text everywhere it is read and mirrors onto `Task.title`
  and friends, none of which has ever been sanitized in this codebase.
- **History step titles were being split on ` / `.** Two `HISTORY.md` headings contain a real one
  ("Follow / Notify / Save for Later", "Report issue / Zgłoś błąd"), so the title was truncated and
  the remainder filed as English. The split is opt-in now and the log's own headings are excluded;
  a test asserts that every title in the seed file still splits into at most two halves.

### What the tests found

- **`tasks/views.py` passed `user` in the serializer context and not `request`** — deliberate there
  (its serializer's docstring says why), but `TranslatedTextMixin` reads `?lang=` off the request, so
  the locale fell back to `pl` and an English reader silently got the Polish. Fixed at all eight call
  sites; the serializer now records why `request` is there and that `user` is still the explicit key.
- **The partial unique index is immediate, not deferred.** `write_versions` cleared the previous
  original *after* writing the new one and failed inside its own transaction. Cleanup moved first.
- **The mirror copied the payload rather than the saved row**, so the model's own column would have
  held the one unsanitized copy on the platform — a real gap on `Task`, which sanitizes in its
  serializer rather than in `save()` (house rule 8).
- **A test had the author of a review voting on their own review** and quietly counted 2 instead
  of 3, which is `rules.can_vote` working. The fixture was wrong, not the rule.
- **`services/translations.ts` already existed** — the exercise-translation workflow — and was
  silently replaced for about an hour. `svelte-check` is what said so; the new seam is
  `services/textVersions.ts`, named for its endpoint, and both files now say why.

**Verified** (house rule 2, with both servers up on :8100/:5183). Backend: `manage.py check` clean,
`makemigrations --check` clean, the full suite **PENDING**. Frontend: `npm run check` 6368
files 0 errors 0 warnings, `npm run lint` clean, key sets identical at 4007 each.
`e2e/ai-assist-and-bilingual.mjs` — **31/31**, as a non-staff reader for the kill switch (trap 10),
and the screenshots looked at — which is what produced the chip change above: the menu order, the
confidence dialog, the chip after three readers agree (amber, the three-people icon lit and the
author's faint, reading 80%), `/about` in English and in Polish with no glue anywhere, and the
two-pane editor with the Polish on the left and the English on the right.

**Left open, not built** (each app's `CLAUDE.md` has the full list):

- **No list filter on the "AI-assisted" score.** The owner's task asks for "hide above X" / "only
  above X" with an `X-EdMat-Hidden-Languages`-shaped count. The threshold it would filter on is the
  number the organisation's poll has not decided, and a filter with a guessed threshold is worse than
  none. The endpoint already answers `score`.
- **No author mark at write time.** The task asks for the choice in `/submit`, `/submit-material` and
  the editors; today the author marks content *after* it exists, from its own menu — one component
  reaching all five surfaces instead of five forms. The write-time question is the better moment and
  is its own change.
- **`material`, `concept_article` and `post` are not provenance targets**, and plan steps and poll
  options have no `⋯` of their own yet (both translate correctly through the endpoint).
- **116 of the 151 plan steps are Polish-only**, because they come from the project log, which is.
  They are the one place a reader will meet the fallback note in quantity, and no step row draws one
  today.

## 17BY — The project board is commentable: a task, a plan, a need or a poll is a discussion location (2026-10-08, `ux/colour-pass`)

The owner, once the "AI-assisted" mark and the bilingual board had shipped: "all the edmat
about/project info section with tasks, plans, needs etc should be commentable, reviable, etc: lets
allow users as we wanted to do that with the previous version of about meaning replies and
moderation/flags different settings". The previous version of `/about` (§17BS) had `DiscussionLocation`
rows under its sections: an audience and a `moderated` switch per location, replies, an anonymous
comment always held, the hold going through the report queue a moderator already reads, and a
moderation tab listing every location with its held count. The ask was that mechanism, under every
row of the board.

### The decision: a row IS a page

The obvious build was a comment endpoint on each of four apps — `tasks`, `plans`, `needs`,
`decisions` added to `community/targets.py` and a `comments` action on each viewset. That gives
threads and gives none of the rest: the two settings live on `DiscussionLocation`, the hold lives in
`discussions.held_for`, the moderation tab reads `/api/discussion-locations/`. Four apps would each
have had to grow a settings row and a hold rule, or the owner would have got threads without the
"different settings" he named.

So a management row is a **page** to `community/discussions.py`: a key of `tasks/17`, `plans/3`,
`needs/2` or `polls/1` (`MANAGEMENT_PAGE_RE`, plural because those are the frontend's route
segments) is the `page` of a `DiscussionLocation`, with no section — one thread per row, one row
of settings per row. **No new endpoint, no new table, no new queue.** The moderation tab lists
`tasks/17` beside `about#money-and-openness` without having learned anything, and "Held: 3" next to
it links to the same filtered report queue.

Two things ARE different about such a page, and both are answered in the rule module so the views
stayed thin:

- **It can be private.** A standing page is prose anybody can open; a task hangs off a node with a
  roster. `discussions.can_read_location` asks the row's own app — `tasks.rules.visible_task`,
  `plans.rules.can_view_plan`, `decisions.rules.can_view_poll`, and a new `needs.rules.can_view_need`
  (the needs app only had the list-shaped `public_needs`; the new function restates its three
  conditions per row and a test keeps the two agreeing) — and both reading endpoints turn a refusal
  into **404**, the answer `/api/tasks/17/` gives the same reader (house rule 4). A row that is gone
  is the same 404. The write path goes through the same check, so a stranger learns nothing from a
  403 either.
- **It answers to two kill switches.** `about_discussions` for the thread and the row's own
  (`tasks`, `plans`, `needs`, `decisions`): `effective_policy` folds the second in for management
  pages only, so a killed board does not keep a live thread under rows nobody can reach (house
  rule 3).

### One request per panel

`/about` draws forty-odd rows across four panels, and each is its own page to the policy endpoint.
`DiscussionPolicyView` grew a second form, `?keys=tasks/1,tasks/2,plans/3,…` (capped at 200), that
answers one policy per key in the order asked, from one query for the location rows, one for the
counts and one per KIND for the management rows — 12 queries for five keys in the test, however many
rows a panel has. A key the reader may not open is simply absent, the queryset-filter shape of house
rule 4; the single-key forms keep their 404. The frontend half is `rowDiscussions.svelte.ts`: a
panel owns ONE `RowDiscussions`, loads it from an `$effect` keyed on its rows and the reader, and
hands each row its policy. The browser script asserts the count of policy requests on the network.

### Where it is drawn

`RowDiscussion.svelte` wraps `SectionDiscussion` (§17BS's collapsed line and lazy thread, unchanged)
in a child that takes a full line of its own — a grid row spans every column, a wrapping flex row
wraps — because the five hosts are laid out five ways. It sits at the foot of a `TaskCard` (a new
optional `discussion` prop; subtasks and `/tasks` draw none), under every plan, need and poll row on
the panels, and on the four detail pages — `/tasks/[id]` through the card, `/plans/[id]`,
`/needs/[id]` and `/polls/[id]` through `PageDiscussion`, which already fetched a policy by page key
and needed no change. The moderation tab makes a management key a link to the row's page and says
what kind of row it is ("a task", "zadanie") where a standing page's row says "the whole page";
`utils/discussionKeys.ts` is the frontend's half of `MANAGEMENT_PAGE_RE` and says so.

"Reviable" was read as **reportable and reviewed by a moderator** — the hold queue, the `⋯` on each
comment with reply / the "AI-assisted" mark / report / a moderator's remove — not star ratings. A
task is not something you rate, and the exercise `Review` model is exercise-only by FK.

### What the tests found

- **A held comment is listed with a placeholder body, not hidden.** The first browser run asserted
  the held comment's WORDS in the staff thread and in the author's view, and both failed: the row is
  there, its body is blanked behind "hidden until a moderator reviews it", because a held comment is
  an auto-hidden one and `CommentSerializer` has always done that. The script now asserts the id for
  staff and the placeholder for the author; `e2e/CLAUDE.md` trap 31.
- **`{@const}` must be the immediate child of the block**, not of an element inside it —
  `svelte-check` refused the first placement in the moderation panel.
- **An exact query count hides the N+1 it was meant to catch.** `assertNumQueries(12)` held in
  one run and read 21 in another, and I first blamed cache warmth. Replacing it with the property —
  three rows must cost what one row costs — showed the batch paying **three queries per key**:
  `is_feature_enabled` reads its row on every call (a kill switch must take effect at once), so the
  thread flag and the kind's flag were read once per key, and each row loaded its node through the
  `GenericForeignKey`. Now `discussions.memoised_flags()` remembers each flag for the life of one
  request and `management_rows` prefetches the node per kind: 6 queries for three tasks, 7 for one.
  A signed-in reader still pays one roster query per row inside each app's own rule
  (`is_node_staff`), which is the honest remainder and is named under "Left open".

**Verified** (house rule 2, both servers up on :8100/:5183). Backend: `manage.py check` and
`makemigrations --check` clean (no model changed), `check_databases_declared` 0;
`community.test_management_discussions` **30 OK**; `community needs moderation` together **323
tests, 1 failure** — my own exact-query-count assertion, replaced by the property it stood in for
(three rows cost what one row costs), which then found a real N+1 — see below — and is green since.
Frontend: `npm run check` 0 errors 0 warnings, `eslint` clean on every touched file, key sets
identical at **4011** each, `check:a11y` **48 pages, 0 violations**.
`e2e/management-discussions.mjs` — **30/30**, screenshots looked at: the line under the task on
`/about` with the exact count and the thread open in place, the plan page's one line at its foot,
the moderation tab's new lead and placeholder.

### Folded by default: a task opens in a modal, a step opens in a modal, and the URL survives a refresh

The owner, while the above was being verified: "both steps and tasks should be folded by default
e.g. by hiding behind a modal and then full page if refreshed with modal opened with returning to
previous page/parent content easily". The board on `/about` had been drawing every task as a full
card — description, assignees, subtasks, actions, and now a discussion line — so a reader scrolled
past a page of prose to find the next task.

- **A task on a board is one line** (`TaskRow.svelte`: priority, title, due date, step count,
  status), the whole line a button. Clicking it opens the full `TaskCard` — subtasks and thread
  included — in a `ModalShell` over the board. The modal is a **shallow route**: `pushState` from
  `$app/navigation` makes the address bar say `/tasks/<id>` while the board stays mounted and draws
  the dialog from `page.state.taskModal`. A refresh therefore lands on the real `/tasks/[id]` page
  (the same card, full size), which now carries a **link back to the node** the task hangs on;
  Escape, the × and the browser's back button are all `history.back()`. `App.PageState` in
  `app.d.ts` names the two keys.
- **A plan's steps are one line each**; a step with a description is a button that opens it in a
  modal keyed by `?step=<id>`, so a refresh re-opens the same dialog over the plan and a pasted
  link does the same. Closing is `back()` when the page pushed the state and a `replaceState`
  navigation to the bare plan URL after a reload, where there is no entry to go back to.
- **`utils/nodeHref.ts`** is the one answer to "where is this node's page" — the plan page and the
  work dashboard each had their own, and the dashboard's sent an organisation to
  `/organizations/<id>`, which is not a route. An organisation's page is its **slug**, so
  `config/nodes.py: node_ref` now carries `slug` for that kind (and `None` for the three addressed
  by id), the four frontend node mappers copy it, and the project's own organisation resolves to
  `/about`.

**What the browser run found.** SvelteKit keeps `page.url` at the page's own URL across a shallow
push (the history entry records it as `sveltekit:pageurl`), so a step modal derived from the query
alone changed the address bar and drew nothing. The id is read from `page.state` first and the
query second — one covers the click, the other the refresh. And the task card draws its subtasks as
nested `article.task`s, so a locator for "the card in the modal" matched three.

**Verified**: `e2e/management-discussions.mjs` grew to **43/43** — the row carries no description
and no card is on the board; the click opens the card in a modal with the URL at `/tasks/<id>`;
Escape returns to `/about`; the task page links back to `/about`; a step's description is absent
from the list, present in the modal, `?step=` in the URL, still open after a reload, and "Back to
the plan" leaves a clean URL. Screenshots looked at. `npm run check` 0 errors 0 warnings, `lint`
clean (Prettier reflowed three files), production build OK, `check:a11y` **48 pages, 0
violations** (one run that overlapped the build reported a load problem and two minor nodes; the
run after it, alone, reported none). Backend: `config.test_nodes` **10 OK** with the shape test
taught `slug`; `config tasks plans needs decisions organizations` 306 tests green bar that one
pre-fix shape assertion.

### Left open

- **`/tasks` (my tasks) still draws full cards**, by choice: a personal list a person reads top to
  bottom is not a board, and it already links each card to its page. Fold it if it grows.
- **A need and a poll are already one line on the panels**; their full content is their page.
  A poll's ballot stays inline on the panel because that is where people vote.
- **No ceiling over a board.** A standing page's own row narrows every section on it; a management
  row has no page above it, because the node is not a page and no row of this table stands for it.
  "Close every thread on this organisation's board" is N switches today. The shape that would do it
  is a `organizations/edmat`-style page row consulted by `effective_policy` for every row whose
  node it is — one more branch there, and a line in the serializer's allowlist.
- **Plan steps and poll options have no thread of their own.** The plan's and the poll's thread is
  where that talk goes; a step would be the next key kind if anybody asks.
- **Subtasks draw no line**, by choice: a subtask's card is drawn by its parent and a thread per
  subtask under a thread per task is noise. `tasks/<subtask id>` is a legal key all the same.
- **A signed-in reader pays one roster query per row** in the batched read, inside each app's
  own rule (`nodes.is_node_staff` → the organisation's member table), because the rule is asked
  per row and the module does not re-implement it. An anonymous reader pays nothing per row.
  Bounded by the panel; a node with hundreds of tasks would want the roster answered once per node.
- **Comment notifications** do not fire for a thread under a management row, exactly as they do
  not for a standing page (§17BT.E's left-open). The task's assignee is the obvious recipient.

## 17BZ — Goals and their definitions of done; the description is commentable; the plan step editor exists (2026-10-08, `ux/colour-pass`)

Three asks from the owner in one afternoon, in the order they arrived.

### A. "after the header, the description should be commentable as well"

The header and the description in question are `/about`'s, which since §17BX is the EdMat
organisation's page (`OrganizationPage.svelte`) — so the thing to make commentable was not a block
of prerendered prose but a row of `organizations.Organization`. §17BY had just built the mechanism
for exactly that, so the answer was one more kind rather than anything new: **`organizations/edmat`
is the `page` of a `DiscussionLocation`**, with no section — one thread per organisation, drawn
under its description, on every organisation page rather than on `/about` alone, because a student
circle's "what we are" is the same kind of text and wants the same thread.

It is addressed by **slug** where the four management kinds are addressed by pk, and that is not an
inconsistency: the slug is this one model's stable public address (`organizations/serializers.py` —
read-only, "allocated once from the name and never moves under a link somebody already sent"), it is
what `/organizations/[slug]` resolves, and a key is also an href (`utils/discussionKeys.ts`). A task
has no such address. `SLUG_KINDS` is the one-line split in `management_rows`, and
`organizations.access.can_view_organization` is what the thread 404s on — so a dissolved
organisation's thread is members-only exactly as its page is.

What it deliberately is NOT is the board ceiling §17BY's "Left open" asks for. This row is the
organisation's own thread, not a switch over the threads of its tasks and plans. Making it both is a
defensible future move and is one branch in `effective_policy`; it stays in `todo.md`.

### B. "we also need goal class which is going to be used as a definition of done and also commentable"

The word was already in use as a **convention**: `/about` has always called the twelve module plans
the project's goals (`work/edmat_project.py`, "a goal is a plan on the EdMat organisation"). That
convention is what the new `goals/` app replaces. The owner chose the shape from four put to them:
a node-level goal whose ordered criteria are the definition of done, with tasks and plans pointing
at the goal they serve — and, separately, that **the twelve module plans do not move**. Goals are a
new, shorter list above them; nothing seeded was rewritten and there is no data migration.

**The one decision everything else follows from: `met` is derived.** Nothing writes
`Goal.status = 'met'`; `goals.rules.recount` does, from the criteria, and it is the only writer —
the `needs.rules.recount` shape and the same argument (house rule 5). Every criterion met and at
least one → `met`; one re-opened → `open`; **no criteria at all → open forever, by construction**,
which is the refusal the ask needs and needs no refusal word, because there is nothing to have met.
`met -> open` is not a hand transition (409 `illegal_transition`: un-tick the line that is not
actually true), and a hand-written `met` is 400 carrying *"tick the criteria"* rather than being
silently dropped (house rule 10). A criterion's own state is **one nullable `met_at`**, not a boolean
and not a `status`: two states, and `met_at IS NULL` is already the honest spelling of one of them.

**The bug the test suite found, and why it is worth reading twice.** `criteria_counts()` was
`self.criteria.count()`. A related manager whose relation has been **prefetched answers from the
prefetch cache**, so a goal loaded by a view that prefetched its criteria and then had one ADDED
counted the old list and stayed `met` — a recount that reads a cache is not a recount. It is now two
methods: `criteria_counts()` queries and is what `recount` decides from; `criteria_counts_cached()`
reads the prefetched list and is what the serializer prints, which is the same list the response is
about to contain. Pinned by `test_adding_an_open_criterion_reopens_a_met_goal`.

**Two authority tiers, because they are two acts.** `can_edit` (the node's manager, or the goal's
own author — the `plans` pair) writes the words, the criteria and the order and abandons the goal;
`can_tick` (the node's **staff**) records a line as met. Widened on purpose: somebody doing the work
is who knows a criterion is now true, and making them ask a manager to record it is how a definition
of done goes stale. `translations/authority.py` asks `can_edit` for both new kinds — translating is
editing, never ticking.

**Visibility is the node's and nothing narrower.** A goal is a public statement of what a body is
trying to achieve, which is the whole point of the list on `/about`; `abandoned` ones stay visible
(house rule 12). It deliberately does not follow `tasks`, which is staff-only unless the board is
open — a task board is the inside of a team and a goal is the outside.

**`destroy` is bounded rather than absent**, and that was a late change driven by writing the
browser script: with no delete at all, a goal typed by mistake could only ever be abandoned, and a
board accumulating "Abandoned: Untitlde" forever is a board people stop reading. `delete_block_reason`
is the `sweep_discussion_locations` test applied to a goal — no task or plan serving it and no
comment of **any** kind under it (tombstones and held rows included: a thread that exists has to
resolve), else 409 `has_work` / `has_comments`, and abandoning is what to do with those.

**The "serves" link** is `tasks.Task.goal` and `plans.Plan.goal`, nullable `SET_NULL`. The rule that
a row may only serve a goal on its **own node** cannot be a database constraint — two generic targets,
no shared column — so it is `goals.rules.goal_for_node`, asked by `ServesGoalMixin` on
`TaskWriteSerializer` and by `PlanViewSet.partial_update`'s own hand-rolled field list. A cross-node
goal is 400 `{"goal": ["other_node"]}`.

And it is commentable the same way everything else on that board is: `goals/5` is a
`DiscussionLocation` page, one more line in `MANAGEMENT_KINDS` and one more branch in
`_row_visible`. No new endpoint, table or queue.

### C. "in plans edit steps doesnt launch any input"

A real bug, and **not** a regression from §17BY: `openEditForm` has set `formOpenFor = 'edit:<id>'`
since the plans app landed (`8ddfeef`, management step D), and the only render conditions on that
page were `formOpenFor === 'top'`, `=== step.id` and `=== sub.id`. Nothing ever matched `edit:<id>`,
so clicking **Edit** on a step set some state and drew nothing — a button that did nothing, which
every check in the suite passed over because the form's *handlers* were all correct.

Fixed by drawing it, and then by answering the question the bug makes obvious: one form reused for
three different jobs with no heading cannot say which job it is doing. `stepForm` now takes a
caption — *New step* / *New sub-step under "X"* / *Editing "X"* — and its two fields got real
labels, the title's having been a placeholder and the description's nothing at all. The dead
`formOpenFor === sub.id` branch (one level of nesting, so a sub-step has no "add a sub-step" of its
own) is gone.

### Verified

`manage.py test goals` 31, `community.test_management_discussions` 41 (11 new, for the organisation
page as a location), `moderation.tests.FeatureFlagTests` 9 — and the full suite. `npm run check`
0/0, `npm run lint` clean, `npm run build` OK, `npm run check:a11y` 48 pages 0 violations, the two
catalogues identical at 4064 keys. `e2e/goals.mjs` 30/30 against both real servers, **and the three
screenshots were looked at**: the collapsed "Comment on EdMat" line sits under the description where
the ask put it; the goal card reads "1 of 2 met" with the met line struck through and "recorded by
piotrek" beside it; the plan step's Edit opens a form captioned *Editing "The EdMat Foundation
founded by the association"* with both fields filled.

### Left open

- **No draft state for a goal.** A goal is short and you write it when you mean it, so there is no
  `draft` the way a plan has one — but there is also no way to prepare one out of sight.
- **A goal is not in the `?keys=` batch on its own page.** `/goals/[id]` uses `PageDiscussion`,
  which fetches its one policy itself; that is the right trade for one thread, but it means the
  page pays a request the panel would have had anyway.
- **`order` is writable but nothing drags.** A goal's position is a PATCH; there is no up/down pair
  on the panel the way `/plans/[id]` has one for steps.
- **A goal cannot be set at creation time from the UI.** `TaskWriteSerializer` accepts `goal` on a
  create (the view passes the node in context), but neither the task form nor the plan form offers
  it — you file the work under a goal afterwards, with the picker on the card.
- **Nothing notifies anybody** when a goal is met, when a criterion they wrote is ticked, or when
  somebody comments under a goal — the same gap §17BT.E and §17BY both name.
- **`e2e/goals.mjs` needs `E2E_OWNER_TOKEN`** and cannot log in for it: writing a goal is a node
  manager's act and `can_manage_node` has no `is_staff` bypass, so platform staff are not owners of
  the `edmat` organisation. That is the rule working, not a gap, but it does mean the script is not
  runnable from the seeded accounts alone.

## 17CA — Withdrawing a room booking: the operator who could see it could not do it (2026-10-08, `ux/colour-pass`)

The owner, mid-session: *"i dont seem to be able to withdraw reservation for a room in
https://edmat.net/events/6"*. Reproduced locally against both real servers in two probes, which is
what turned one report into two separate findings.

**The bug.** `RoomBookingViewSet.get_queryset` has had an `is_staff` bypass since the conference
layer landed — platform staff see every booking, because somebody has to be able to answer "what is
this building holding" without being on the event's staff list. `cancel` asked
`booking.event.can_organise(request.user)` and nothing else. So the two halves disagreed: an
operator was *shown* every booking on an event they do not organise and told `not_allowed` the
moment they acted on one — and the button was not drawn either, because `VenuePanel` gated it on
the same `canOrganise`, so the refusal was invisible until somebody POSTed by hand. Measured:

```
LIST  as superuser  200  12 rows        ← you see them
EVENT can_organise= false               ← no button
CANCEL as superuser 403 {"detail":"not_allowed"}
```

Seeing a row and being able to act on it are now the same permission. `is_staff` is this project's
one operator bypass (the same one `feature_gate` uses) so it is the one used here rather than a new
rule; `Event.can_organise` is **untouched**, because running an event and operating the platform are
different jobs and only this one withdrawal needs the second. The frontend mirrors it in
`canWithdraw`, exactly as `venuesOn` already mirrors the feature gate.

**The second finding, which nobody reported.** `cancel` set `status` and `decided_at` but never
`decided_by`, while `_decide` (approve/reject) sets all three. That was survivable while an
organiser was the only person who could withdraw; the moment two different people can, the record
stops answering *who took the room back*. It is set now — house rule 12: the record of a decision is
part of the trust model.

### Left open — and it needs the owner's decision, not a patch

**A building cannot revoke a booking it has already approved.** `_decide`'s update is WHERE-anchored
on `status='requested'`, and `/venues/[slug]/manage` draws a decided row as a pill with no control.
So once a room is granted, only the organiser (or now an operator) can hand it back — the building
itself cannot. That is defensible (the organiser holds the room; the building said yes) and it is
also how a venue administrator would describe exactly the owner's complaint. Fixing it is not a
bypass but a new status: `cancelled` reads *"Withdrawn by the organiser"*, and "the building took it
back" is a different fact that a reader of the row needs told apart from it — so it is a choices
change, a migration and a control on the manage page. `todo.md` carries it.

### Verified

`manage.py test venues.tests.RoomBookingTests --keepdb` 15 OK (5 new: the operator's withdrawal,
the record of who made it, the stranger still getting 404 rather than 403, the operator still not
being an organiser, and the building's own refusal, which is the left-open written down as a test so
that changing it is a deliberate act).

## 17CB — A node page folds: every panel is one line until you open it (2026-10-08, `ux/colour-pass`)

The owner: *"simplify and clean as rn its overwehalming: most things should be hidden under some
kind of expandable sth"* — and, asked which surface and what should be open to start with: **an
event or a course page**, **everything shut but the first**, remembered.

It was not an exaggeration. `/events/[id]` mounts sixteen panels below the hero — programme,
contributions, registration fields, registrations, staff, venue, checklist, documents, tickets,
rota, cloakroom, the seven management panels, deck placements, related courses, updates, roster —
and every one of them drew at full height. On the demo conference the attendee list was four
screens below the date. Measured on that event: **1646px shut against 6064px with two sections
opened**, and the whole page now fits on one screen as eight labelled lines.

### `FoldSection`, and the one rule about where it goes

One component (`lib/components/shared/FoldSection.svelte`) plus one rune store
(`lib/state/foldedSections.svelte.ts`). The rule that shaped it:

**It is used INSIDE a panel, never wrapped around one from the page.** A panel decides for itself
whether it has anything to draw — its own kill switch, and whether this reader may see what it
holds — and house rule 3 says a killed feature takes its own surface away rather than leaving a sign
where it used to be. A fold wrapped around a panel from the outside cannot know that, and would
leave a header with nothing behind it. A panel that loads first and then renders the fold can also
put its own **count** on the line, which is the entire value of a shut section: the reader decides
whether to open it from what the line says (*Program 20*, *Kto się wybiera 130*, *Dokumenty 3 · 2
still to read*). The one deliberate exception is `CourseClaims` on the course page, wrapped from
outside because `ClaimGroups` always draws its two groups and is shared with `/exercises/[id]` and
`/materials/[id]`, which the owner did not ask to change.

Three smaller decisions, each with a reason:

- **The body is destroyed while shut**, not hidden with `hidden`. The data is already loaded by the
  panel above, so what is saved is DOM, KaTeX typesetting and layout — the cost the owner was
  actually complaining about. A panel that only fetches what it shows gets `onopen`, because it can
  no longer see the click itself (`CourseReports` is the one).
- **Keyed by SECTION, not by object.** `fold:documents`, not `fold:event:6:documents`: a reader who
  opens Documents on one event is telling us something about themselves, not about that event, and
  a per-object key would make them say it again on the next one and grow one localStorage entry per
  row they ever looked at.
- **Nothing here is `<details>`.** The native element cannot carry a count and an action menu on its
  summary line without nesting interactive content inside `<summary>` — a real a11y problem, not a
  style one — and its open state does not survive a reload. A button with `aria-expanded` and
  `aria-controls` is the same promise, kept.

An "open by default" section needs a stored **no** rather than the absence of a yes, or shutting it
would be forgotten on the next load; that is the `-key` prefix in the store.

### What folded

The six management panels (`goals` `organizations` `tasks` `needs` `plans` `polls`), which are
shared — so `/about`, `/organizations/[slug]` and every material page got the same treatment for
free. Eleven event panels, the event page's own sub-events and attendee sections, and on the course
page: coverage, reports, completions and the two always-open "add" forms. `CourseReports` had
**written its own disclosure** — a button, a `▾`/`▸` and a count — before there was a shared one; it
is now the shared one, and the reader's choice is remembered, which the local one never did.

The course page carries a warning from the last time something like this was tried: *"it used to be
four collapsed drawers here… an instructor found the thing they came to do always shut."* The
answer to it is that a fold now **remembers**: an instructor who opens the contribute form once
finds it open on every course after that.

### Verified

`npm run check` 0/0, `npm run lint` clean, `npm run build` OK, both catalogues identical at 4068
keys (four new: `fold_expand`, `fold_collapse`, `polls_panelHeading`, `course_coverageHeading`).
`e2e/folded-sections.mjs` 12/12 against both real servers — every panel shut with its count, the
page height before and after, `aria-expanded` moving, and the choice surviving a reload in both
directions — **and the screenshots were looked at**: the whole conference page is one screen of
eight labelled lines.

### Left open

- **Nothing folds on `/exercises/[id]` or `/materials/[id]`.** They have the same management panels
  (so those fold) but their own sections do not, because the owner named two surfaces and those are
  not them.
- **No "collapse all" / "expand all".** The store has `reset()` and nothing calls it.
- **The tabs on the course page are untouched.** Five tabs are already a disclosure; folding inside
  one would be hiding the same thing twice.
- **A count is not always the right line.** `Zaświadczenia o ukończeniu` and `Co obejmuje i czego
  wymaga` have no number, so their lines say less than the others'.

## 17CC — The admin registers what it was missing; the EdMat description is the owner's words; the conference demo is twelve people (2026-10-08, `ux/colour-pass`)

Three of the owner's asks from the same evening, each small on its own.

### "django admin lacks funcionalities"

Counted rather than guessed: **72 of this project's 174 models had an admin page. Eleven apps had
no `admin.py` at all** — `flashcards` `goals` `needs` `organizations` `provenance` `translations`
`decisions` `telemetry` and three with nothing to register — and `services` had one with zero
registrations, so a tutoring listing could not be looked at either. `courses` had 3 pages against
19 models, `events` 3 against 15.

**161 of 174 now.** The thirteen that are not registered are each edited as an inline on the row
they belong to (the five taxonomy translations, a set's items, a profile's CV rows, the two
availability windows, a post's links) — an inline answers the only question those tables are asked.

Three rules shaped the pages rather than a template:

- **A derived status is `readonly_fields`.** `goals.Goal.status` and `needs.Need.fulfilled` are
  recounted from other rows and the API answers 400 if you try to set them by hand (house rule 5,
  root CLAUDE.md shape 4). The admin must not become the one surface that can make `met` mean
  nothing — so it shows `met_by`/`met_at` beside the status, which is the evidence, not the
  decision. The same for `MaterialView` (the input a view count is recounted from) and for the
  door log and the export log, which are evidence and are add/change-disabled outright.
- **A ballot and a vote stay apart.** `decisions` registers both, and `BallotAdmin` shows who voted
  and never what they chose while `VoteAdmin` shows what was chosen and never by whom. Joining them
  helpfully in one changelist would undo in a list view exactly what the schema separates for an
  anonymous poll.
- **Every FK to a person is `raw_id_fields`.** A select holding every account is slow and is a way
  to pick the wrong person.

**And one page was deliberately un-registered again.** `RequestLog` and `AuditEvent` live on the log
shards, not on `default`, so the `ModelAdmin` written for them opened to
`OperationalError: no such table: telemetry_requestlog` — registered, `manage.py check` clean, and
broken on the first click. `telemetry/admin.py` is now a module that explains why there is no page
and what the three real options would cost (house rule 10: flag it, don't fake it). Found by a
throwaway script that opened all 164 changelists as a superuser; after the fix, **162 open, 0
fail**, which is the check worth keeping in mind next time somebody adds a model on a shard.

### The organisation's description is the owner's sentence

The owner, the same evening: *"prepare the desc of edmat org on about to be Edukacja potrzebuje
usprawnień. EdMat.net to otwarte miejsce współpracy nad materiałami edukacyjnymi i oprogramowaniem:
buduje je społeczność, każda zmiana jest widoczna, a każde rozwiązanie ma osobę, która za nie
odpowiada"*. It replaces the two paragraphs the seed wrote the day before, in both languages; a full
stop was added and nothing else changed.

**`seed_edmat_project --retake-description` is new, and it exists because the protection written
yesterday is also a trap.** `_write_bilingual` passes `keep_edited=True` so that a deployment never
silently undoes an edit the owner made on production — correct, and it also means the seed can never
again change that field once anybody has touched it. The flag is how a NEW description from the file
is allowed to win, said out loud on the command line rather than by quietly weakening the rule.
**This matters for tomorrow's deploy:** if the description on production has ever been saved through
the editor, `seed_edmat_project --owner <name>` alone will leave it exactly as it is.

### Twelve people at the conference, not a hundred and fifty

The owner: *"lets also have only 6 test users"* — and, asked which of the three things that could
mean, **shrink the demo seeds**. The dev database held **217 accounts and 157 of them were the
conference demo**. `N_ATTENDEE_ACCOUNTS` 144 → 12, with every other number re-derived around it so
the SHAPES survive: full with a waiting list (capacity 10 = 6 going + 2 promoted + the two
personas), open seat offers, people who said no, a door log that is not everybody, a cloakroom with
returns. **217 → 85 accounts.**

Two things the shrink broke, both found by running it:

- **The door log quietly lost a result class.** The lunch exits were a slice of the first hour's
  batch (`first[5:8]`), which at twelve accounts is empty — so nobody went out for lunch, `exited`
  never appeared, and "fewer inside than have been let in" stopped being demonstrated. Rebuilt from
  `arrivals` instead, which also fixes the subtler half: that batch carries the collision duplicate
  and the two tokens nobody issued, so an exit scan built from one of those is refused and "three
  out" could silently be two.
- **The tests restated the numbers.** `waitlisted == 6`, `checked_in == 100`, `coats_returned == 9`
  are now `N_WAITLISTED`, `DAY_ONE_CHECKED_IN`, `N_LUNCH_RETURNS`, and `inside_count == 99` is now
  the relationship it was standing for (`inside < checked_in`, `> 0`) — a test that hard-codes a
  demo's size fails for the size being changed on purpose rather than for the shape being wrong.

### Verified

`manage.py check` clean, `events.test_conference_demo` 17 OK, `work` + `translations` 61 OK,
`venues.tests.RoomBookingTests` 15 OK, the full suite green, and the 162-changelist smoke above.
`/about` was loaded in a browser and **looked at**: the new sentence, one paragraph, with the folded
panels under it.

### The one thing that was *not* reproduced, and the one fix it produced anyway

The owner, the same evening: *"troubleshoot why have i killed the about by changing the description
of the orgazniation by deleting what have you seeded today/yest … plain regular input with polish
letters"*. It could not be reproduced:

- production `/about` renders correctly for an anonymous reader **right now**, with 10,260
  characters of content and no console error;
- every endpoint that page calls answers 200 — the organisation, its members and links, the node
  ref, goals, decks, tasks, needs, plans, polls, the flags, the discussions;
- the description on production is **still the seeded text**, so the edit never persisted;
- driving the real editor locally — open ⋯, *Edit in both languages*, clear the box, type a plain
  Polish sentence, Save — works, and the page redraws with the new text.

**What was found instead is a dead end that looks exactly like a broken page.** `TranslateFields`
disables Save when the ORIGINAL pane's body is empty, and said nothing about why: clear the box to
retype the description and the button goes grey with no sentence beside it. That is house rule 6
unanswered — and it is worse than a plain missing message, because the OTHER pane carries the hint
*"leave both boxes empty to take this translation down"*, so emptying a box reads like a delete
everywhere except the one pane where it is not one. There is now a line under the form saying which
language needs something written in it and that clearing the field is not how to delete the text.

To settle the original report somebody still needs two facts that only the owner can give: **what
`/about` shows them while signed in**, and any error in the browser console.

### Left open

- **The ~44 accounts left behind by browser scripts** (`ehost-…`, `owner-…`, `e2e-…`, `gatekid…`,
  `bugtest`) are still there. They are safe to delete and nothing shows them; a
  `purge_test_accounts --dry-run` command is the honest shape and was not written, because the owner
  picked the seed shrink and not this.
- **The eleven named volunteers were not shrunk.** The rota is the thing they exist for and a rota
  with one volunteer on it demonstrates nothing; the shift `needed` counts still carry the report's
  ratios for a 150-person event.
- **No admin page can reach a log shard**, as above.

## 17CD — Attachments on anything: one table that supersedes three (2026-10-09, `ux/colour-pass`)

The owner, 2026-10-08 evening: *".md files, docs, etc, sketches etc for files when creating an event
for attachements (in multiple places we lack this funcionality)"* — and, asked where: events at
creation, courses, tasks, plans, needs, goals, materials, organisations **and comments**,
"EVERYWHERE". Two decisions were put to them before anything was written, because both were theirs
to make and neither could be guessed:

1. **What to do about the three tables that already answered a piece of it** — `documents.EventDocument`
   (an event's tiered briefing pack with a read ledger), `courses.Attachment` (a course's files with
   ratings) and `community.CommentAttachment` (a picture on a comment). They chose **one table,
   supersede the others**, over the cheaper "new table, leave the two alone".
2. **Whether an office document may be stored at all**, given house rule 7 — *never store the bytes
   that were uploaded*. They chose **yes, the same path as a PDF**, which is the carve-out the rule's
   own text already makes: *"What cannot be re-encoded (a PDF) gets the sniff, the size cap and a
   ClamAV scan."* Modern OOXML only; `.doc`/`.xls`/`.ppt` and the macro formats refused **by name**.

### The shape

One `Attachment` with a `GenericForeignKey` and a registry of nine legal targets
(`attachments/targets.py`), which is this project's standing shape for a polymorphic target. The
registry has three halves that behave differently, and that is why it is written out rather than
derived:

- a **node** (course, event, material, organisation) answers the whole ladder through `config/nodes.py`;
- a **board row** (task, plan, need, goal) has no standing of its own and resolves to the node it
  hangs off — exactly as its own discussion thread does, so four more apps did not have to learn a
  permission model;
- a **comment** has no node at all, so only `public` is legal and `tier_block_reason` refuses the
  rest rather than quietly treating them as public.

**The ladder is `EventDocument`'s, generalised**: `public ⊂ members ⊂ staff ⊂ managers`, plus `venue`
which is deliberately NOT on it — a building's administrators are neither above nor below an
organiser. The old event tiers map onto it exactly (`attendees → members`, `organisers → managers`),
which is what makes the absorption a rename and not a reinterpretation.

**Four file paths, and which one a file takes is decided by what it IS, never by what it was
called.** An image is re-encoded from pixels, so nothing of the upload survives and a polyglot is not
a question this path has to answer. **`.md`/`.txt` become characters in a TEXT column** — house rule
7 answered by not having the question — and render through `renderContent.ts` like every other body,
maths included. A PDF is stored as-is behind the sniff, the cap and the honest `scanned=False`. An
office document takes the PDF's path plus the zip-container member check, because libmagic can only
ever answer "it is a zip" for all four OOXML kinds, so an arbitrary archive renamed `.docx` would
otherwise pass.

### The two warnings, which say two different things

The owner also asked for *"two popups with warning before downloading a file"*. Two dialogs with the
same words would be a click to dismiss twice, so they carry different facts: the first is about
**provenance** — who put this here, that EdMat did not make it and cannot see inside it, and whether
a scanner was even running — and the second is about **this file**: its name, its type, its size, and
the one sentence that changes behaviour (*open it only if you trust whoever put it here*). The
download fires only after the second, and cancelling either one downloads nothing.

### The absorption is a command, not a migration

`manage.py absorb_legacy_attachments`, dry by default, `--apply` to write, `--verify` to check. A
data migration runs itself on the next deploy, in whatever order the deploy reaches it, with no dry
run and nobody looking — the wrong shape for a step whose whole risk is in the data rather than in
the schema. It is idempotent by the legacy row's id, carries the acknowledgements and the ratings
across, fixes the supersession chain in a second pass, and **shares the file path rather than copying
bytes**, which has a consequence worth stating rather than discovering: while both rows exist,
deleting either takes the shared file with it. That is why `--apply` does not delete the legacy rows.

On this dev database it absorbed **11 event documents and 30 acknowledgements**; a second run
reported 11 already done.

### Two bugs found by running it

- **`is_reencodable_image` takes the UPLOAD, not the sniffed string.** It does its own sniff, which
  is what keeps "is this an image we re-encode" in `imaging.py` rather than in five callers. Passing
  it the string is an `AttributeError` on `.seek` — five tests, one cause.
- **A test asserted `len(response.data) == 0` for a stranger** and passed against the wrong thing: a
  404's body is a dict and `len()` of it is 1. It asserts the status now.

### Verified

`attachments` 31 tests OK — the tiers in both directions, the file endpoint refusing a tier you do
not have, the legacy Office refusal, a zip renamed `.docx`, a real `.docx` served as a download, a
replacement keeping the old row's acknowledgements, a withdrawal that is not a delete, a 409 on an
acknowledgement of superseded text, the kill switch, and a board row inheriting its node.
`manage.py check` clean. Frontend `npm run check` 0/0, both catalogues identical at 4110 keys.
`e2e/attachments.mjs` **14/14** against both real servers, and the screenshots were looked at: the
`.md` renders with its maths typeset, and the two dialogs say different things.

### Left open

- **Nothing is mounted on a course or an event page yet**, and the condition that holds it back is
  one line in `ManagementPanels`. Both still have their older surfaces, and two attachment UIs on one
  page is worse than one in the wrong place; the line goes on the day `--apply` runs on production.
- **The legacy tables are still there** and still serve their own endpoints. That is the second half
  of "supersede", and it is deliberately not in the same change as the first.
- **Sketch and chem attachments have no picker.** The kinds exist, the API takes them, the panel
  renders them; nothing offers to choose an existing drawing.
- **No replacement from the UI.** The endpoint exists and is tested; the panel offers withdraw.
- **A course attachment's discussion thread is not moved** by the absorb command — a thread is
  addressed by `(content_type, object_id)` and moving one is a `community` change. The command counts
  them and says so rather than leaving it to be discovered.
- **`MATERIAL_SCAN_REQUIRED` is still off.** With office documents now accepted, that is the setting
  the owner should turn on before this is open to anybody but the people running the thing — without
  it, an unscannable upload is stored with an honest `scanned=False` rather than refused.

## 17CE. Contests (*konkursy*) — the preamble, the prep, and the integration (2026-10-09)

**What this section is.** The owner's ask of the afternoon of 2026-10-09 — *"add contests.
personalize all current modules to this use case. each subagent can have 1 haiku. research law for
konkursy in poland and add presets with making it possible by prefilling with current users"* —
built as a research agent, a prep commit, two Opus branches at once and an integration, all in one
day. The research is `CONTESTS-LAW.md`; the design is `CONTESTS-BRIEF.md`; the two steps' own
records are §17CE.A (the app, its rules and every page of it) and §17CE.B (every other module made
contest-aware), appended by the agents that built them; the prep and the integration are below,
written by the orchestrating session. **The short version:** a contest is a new node kind with a
jury and a ranking; ten presets carry what Polish law asks of each kind of *konkurs* (no prize by
default; a prize unlocks the claim deadline, the no-draw rule and the tax block; kurator and
olympiad presets staff-only); founding one through the wizard prefills the jury from the people the
founder already works with and creates, through the other apps' own paths, a plan with the
timeline, a goal whose criteria are the definition of done, the legal checklist as tasks, the
"jury member wanted" needs and the jury's poll.

### The integration (the orchestrating session, after A and B landed)

Merge B (`e3c79d3`, a fast-forward of the prep branch) then A (`f2c2ba9`) onto `contests/prep`.
Five "both appended" conflicts (`HISTORY.md`, both catalogues, `labels.ts`, `test.md`), resolved
with the union resolver; the one blind spot it has — identical trailing lines folded into shared
context — bit once, on the closing brace of step B's `contestLabel()` helper, and Prettier found it.
Then the §5 wiring:

- **One label file, not two.** Step A had written its six enum maps typed against
  `lib/types/contest` in a temporary `utils/contestLabels.ts` because B's `Record<string>` copies
  did not exist on its branch; B's six, with different message keys, had landed in `labels.ts`.
  A's typed block was folded into `labels.ts` whole (with its extra maps — stage status,
  advancement, result title, compliance state — and `complianceHint`), B's six duplicates were
  dropped along with the 24 `contestLabel_*` catalogue keys nothing referenced any more, and
  thirteen importers were re-pointed. `contestLabels.ts` is gone.
- **The bilingual title and description on the contest page.** `ContestSerializer` now carries
  `TranslatedTextMixin` (`title`/`description` answer in the reader's `?lang=`, plus `language` and
  `text_versions`), `Contest` gained the `text_versions` `GenericRelation` B had asked for (no
  column, no migration), `TranslatableKind` gained `contest`, and `ManagementTextMenu` is mounted
  at A's `contests: translations` marker for a manager.
- **The contest's own thread**, `contests/<id>` in `community/discussions.py` (B), mounted at A's

### The prep (what the orchestrating session landed before the two steps started)

The owner, the afternoon of 2026-10-09: *"add contests. personalize all current modules to this use
case. each subagent can have 1 haiku. research law for konkursy in poland and add presets with
making it possible by prefilling with current users"* — the interface to be built by an Opus agent
from a detailed brief, with the interface tasks spelled out. `CONTESTS-BRIEF.md` is that brief's
design half; `prompts/18-contests-a-core.md` and `prompts/19-contests-b-personalise.md` are the two
agents' halves; `CONTESTS-LAW.md` is the research. This section records the prep; §17CE.A and
§17CE.B are the two steps' own records, appended by them; the preamble tying them together is the
integrator's, after the merges.

### Why a new app, in one paragraph

A course has no jury and an event has no ranking. A contest's one property neither has — the
participants are judged and the judging produces a ranking that outlives it — is exactly the
property Polish law attaches consequences to the moment a prize is promised: a *przyrzeczenie
publiczne* (KC art. 919–921) that is *bezskuteczne* without a claim deadline, a lottery if chance
decides any stage, 10% tax with somebody as *płatnik*, a guardian's consent for a minor, a separate
consent to publish a name. So `contests` is its own app and gets everything else — a venue and a
rota for its final, tasks, a plan, a goal, needs, polls, attachments, a practice deck, a discussion,
a bilingual description — by being a **node**.

### The research, and what it corrected

An Opus research agent with web access wrote `CONTESTS-LAW.md` (14 sections, every claim with its
act, article and URL, and one of four markers). Two premises in the brief it was given were wrong
and it said so: there is **no article of the Polish data-protection act transposing GDPR art. 8**
(Poland dropped the lowering to 13, so 16 applies directly — cite GDPR art. 8 only), and the
**2002 MENiS regulation does not fix szkolny → rejonowy → wojewódzki for a konkurs** (that ladder is
kuratoria practice; only olympiads have three fixed stages). Both are in the presets as the research
left them: the kurator ladder is editable, the olympiad's is locked. The thing worth recording for
`LEGAL.md` beyond contests: **Poland's DSA implementing act was signed 25 September 2026 and applies
from 6 November 2026**, with the Prezes UKE as the Digital Services Coordinator.

  answers; `_registered` is the one body step A replaces), **`presets.py`** (ten presets —
  `challenge` the prize-free default, `school`, `staged`, `university`, `student_circle`,
  `organization`, `open_online`, `team`, and the staff-only `kuratorium` and `olympiad`; the
  12-section regulamin skeleton; the 24-item legal checklist; the `LAW` table where every citation
  carries its marker so the frontend never presents an unverified article as settled), three stubs
  with fixed signatures (`personalize.apply_preset`, `work.work_items`, `record.placements_for`),
  `GET /api/contest-presets/` answering `{law, presets}` filtered by who asks, seven prep tests.
- **The seam**: kind `contest` in `config/nodes.py`; `contest` as the fifth `CREATION_KINDS` entry
  (three files + `gate_hub_contest` in both catalogues); `contest` as an attachment target on both

- **Decisions baked into the presets** (§1 of the brief; each the owner's to overturn): no prize
