## 17CE.B. Every other module made contest-aware — the preset as rows, nine registries, `/about/contests`, the manual chapter (2026-10-09)

Step B of the contests cycle (`prompts/19-contests-b-personalise.md`, `CONTESTS-BRIEF.md` §3.B),
built on `contest/b-personalise` from the prep `75a6fea` while step A built the app and its pages on
`contest/a-core`. The owner's ask of that afternoon was two sentences and this is the second of
them: *"personalize all current modules to this use case"*.

A contest owns almost nothing of what it takes to run one. Its timeline is a `plans.Plan`, its
definition of done is a `goals.Goal` and its criteria, its legal checklist is one `tasks.Task` per
item, "jury member wanted" is a `needs.Need`, and the jury confirming the ranking is a
`decisions.Poll` — all five hung off the contest **as a node** (`config/nodes.py`), which is the
whole reason `contests` could be a small app. This step wrote the thing that puts them there, and
then taught nine other registries that a contest exists.

### Presets and personalisation

`contests/presets.py` gained the words and `contests/personalize.py` gained the mechanism, and the
split is deliberate: a preset is DATA, so both languages of a sentence sit on one line where a
reviewer can see that the Polish still says what the English does (`content/about.ts`'s reasoning,
applied to a seed). What `presets.py` grew: `PLAN_TITLE`/`PLAN_DESCRIPTION` and eight `PlanPhase`
rows (the timeline, one per phase, each with the anchor its due date comes from), `STAGE_STEP_OPENS`
/`STAGE_STEP_CLOSES` (a stage becomes **two** steps, because that is where the jury's work starts and
stops and a single step for a stage cannot be half done), `GOAL_TITLE`/`GOAL_DESCRIPTION`,
`POLL_QUESTION`/`POLL_DESCRIPTION`/`POLL_OPTIONS`, `TASK_PHASE_ANCHORS`, `MARKER_WORDS`,
`NOT_LEGAL_ADVICE`, and `citation_block()` — the Markdown a task's description carries, one bullet
per citation with its verification marker as a WORD rather than a bracketed tag from the research
note, and the sentence saying none of it is advice.

**`LAW_PL`, 32 rows, is the one addition nobody asked for and the file needed.** `LAW`'s citations
were English glosses of Polish statutes, and a Polish reader being shown "no claim deadline ⇒ the
promise is bezskuteczne" next to *Kodeks cywilny art. 921 §1* is exactly the drift house rule 1
exists to stop. A separate table rather than a third element on every tuple, because step A reads
`LAW` and `law_as_api()` and a changed tuple shape would have broken it mid-build; `law_as_api()`
now answers `citation_pl` beside `citation`, which is additive.

`checklist_for` and the new `goal_criteria_for` both take an optional `has_prize` override, because
the one fact a preset cannot know is whether THIS contest promises a prize — `has_prize` is a field
on the row (step A's) and a founder may turn it off on a preset that normally promises one. Turning
it OFF drops the prize-only items; turning it ON does not invent rows the preset never named, and
the docstring says why.

`apply_preset(contest, actor)` returns the stub's own shape and is built to three rules:

1. **Through each app's own path.** Every row goes through that app's write serializer, so its
   validation and its `sanitize_content` run (house rule 8), after that app's rule module has said
   the actor may create it — `tasks.rules.can_create` for the tasks (any node staff), and
   `config.nodes.can_manage_node` for the other four. A second copy of "may this person" here is how
   two surfaces start disagreeing. `work/edmat_project.py` is the precedent for everything else
   about the shape, including the bilingual text.
2. **A module that is off is a word in `skipped`, never an exception** (house rule 10). The function
   is called from `ContestViewSet.create`, so a `tasks` kill switch must not be a 500 on founding a
   contest. `_enabled` asks whether the app is INSTALLED first, so a bare clone that dropped one
   reads as "not here" rather than crashing.
3. **Idempotent row by row, keyed by title on the node**, with `already_personalised` in `skipped`
   when nothing new was created. No marker table — a title on a node is what every other seed here
   keys on, and step B is forbidden a migration in `contests/` anyway. The useful consequence is
   that switching `needs` back on and re-running fills in the rows the kill switch cost, which a
   single "already done" flag could never do.

Everything it writes is bilingual in ONE submission through `translations.services.write_versions`,
Polish the original — which is what keeps a row this created from ever telling a reader that the
Polish is four minutes newer than the English.

Dates come from the contest's four datetimes and the preset's stage offsets, and **a step or task
whose anchor is empty gets no due date at all**: an invented deadline on a legal checklist is worse
than an open one. `complaint_window_days` and `has_prize` are read with `getattr` and fall back to
the preset, because step A adds those fields — which is not defensiveness for its own sake but what
let the two branches be built at once, and stays correct afterwards.

### The nine registries, and the two that needed more than a line

| Registry | What it took |
|---|---|
| `community/targets.py` | `('contests','contest'): 'contest'`, and NOT in `PRIVATE_TARGET_TYPES` — a contest's visibility is a per-ROW answer in the same shape a draft exercise's is |
| `community/discussions.py` | `contests` in `MANAGEMENT_PAGE_RE` + `MANAGEMENT_KINDS` + `_row_visible` → `contests.access.can_view`; page key `contests/5`, by pk |
| `moderation/services.py` | `REPORT_KIND_MODELS['contest']`, the Event posture — remove HIDES (`visibility='private'`) and never sets `cancelled` |
| `galleries/` | `GALLERY_TARGETS` + both halves of `visibility.py`: readable as the contest is, curated by its organisers only |
| `translations/` | `TRANSLATABLE_KIND_MODELS['contest']` = title + description, `authority.py` → `contests.access.can_manage` |
| `flashcards/models.py` | `PLACEABLE_NODE_KINDS` gains `contest` — a practice deck for a cohort getting ready for a date, which is why an organisation still does not qualify |
| `activity/` | two kinds, a typed `contest` FK, migration `0008`, two `post_save` receivers and the forgetting half |
| `work/` | four sections registered under the `contests` flag, and the four keys in `_SECTION_ORDER` |
| `identity/record.py` | a THIRD block, `placements`, with its own provider registry |

**`community/discussions.py` needed a third set, `NODE_KINDS_HERE`.** `management_rows` prefetches
`'node'` on every id-addressed kind, and a `Contest` has no such relation — asking for one raises. An
organisation escaped it only because it is slug-addressed, which conflated two different facts; the
new set says the real one ("this row IS a node") and `SLUG_KINDS` goes back to meaning only how the
key is spelled.

**`translations/resolve.py: _versions` had a silent wrong answer in it.** Its docstring promised a
query fallback for a model without the `GenericRelation`; the code returned `[]`. `Contest` is the
first registered kind that has no relation — it needs no migration but it is a line in
`contests/models.py`, which step B does not own — so a contest somebody HAD translated would have
read back as untranslated. The fallback is now real: one query per object, named as the cost, and it
disappears the moment the relation is added.

**The report serializer is the one place a visibility rule had to be added rather than joined.**
`ReportCreateSerializer.validate` checked existence as "the row is in the table", which is right for
every other kind — an exercise, a comment, a listing is public the moment it is written. A draft
contest is not, so a reporting form that confirmed one exists would be a way to enumerate drafts by
id (house rule 4). `_target_exists` asks `contests.access.visible_contests` for that one kind and
answers the endpoint's existing 400 "No matching content found", which is the honest meaning.

**The activity rows are public by construction, strictly.** Two kinds — `contest` on the transition
INTO `Contest.is_public`, `contest_results` when that public row reaches `results_published` — both
on a status transition rather than on creation, because `is_public` is `status` AND `visibility` and
announcing a PRIVATE contest must write nothing. Cancelling or pulling it back to private calls
`remove_activity_for`, which takes both rows. `_remember_contest` is the `pre_save` twin of the
course's and the event's.

### The pages

**`/about/contests`** is the eighth showcase page and the only one whose subject is mostly law,
which changed how it is written: the other seven describe a design, and a reader who misreads one
loses a feature; a reader who misreads this one runs a contest that is *bezskuteczne*. So every
article number on it carries its verification marker from `LAW_MARKER_LABELS` — the same map step A's
compliance panel reads — and "this is not legal advice" is said twice, once under the law table and
once in the closing paragraph, so that a reader who stops at the five rules has read it and so has
one who reads only the end. Six sections, all discussable; ten preset cards through a new
`ContestPresetCard` (its own component because a preset has one thing to say that no `SampleRows`
row does: whether it promises a prize, which decides whether the whole public-promise regime
applies).

**`/about/guide/contests`** is the manual's twelfth chapter, twelve steps, written against step A's
pages as `CONTESTS-BRIEF.md` §3.A describes them — and with **no screenshots**, which its own
closing note says plainly. The manual's standing promise is that every picture in it is a photograph
of the running site; a chapter with drawings would break that, and the integrator re-shoots them
after the merge. It is NOT marked `pending`, because the text is finished and `pending` tells a
reader there is nothing there to read.

`labels.ts` gained six maps and two key lists under a comment naming `presets.py` and `models.py`;
`presets.py` names them back. `Record<string, …>` rather than string-literal unions, deliberately: a
type declared in both halves of a two-branch build is a merge conflict for no benefit, and the
integrator can tighten it.

### Three bugs the browser found, none of them this branch's own idea

House rule 2 again, and all three were invisible to `svelte-check`, `eslint` and the build.

1. **`/work` rendered nothing at all** — "Loading your work…" for ever, with
   `param_value.startsWith is not a function` thrown during render. `services/work.ts` handed the
   raw JSON back under the `WorkDashboard` type without mapping it, and `node.id` is a NUMBER on the
   wire (`config/nodes.py: node_ref` sends `node.pk`) where `NodeRef.id` is a string; `/work` draws
   `nodeHref(item.node)`, which calls `resolve()`, which calls `.startsWith` on every param. It has
   been true of EVERY work item with a node since `nodeHref` landed on 2026-10-08 — `services/
   tasks.ts` and `services/plans.ts` have had the identical `String(raw.id)` all along — and it took
   a preset that puts seventeen tasks on one dashboard to make somebody look. Fixed here, with the
   mapper those two already have.
2. **`each_key_duplicate` on `/work`**, which is what the page showed next. The item list was keyed
   by `item.url`, and a work item has no id of its own (the §3.F shape is seven keys and none of
   them is one), so every due step of one plan is a row keyed `/plans/28`. Possible from the start;
   certain with a plan of eleven dated steps. Keyed by url plus title here, and a real id in the
   item shape is named in `todo.md`.
3. **`OrganizationsPanel.load()` reads `node.canManage` after an `await`**, and `ManagementPanels`
   sets `node = null` whenever its key changes — which it does once on every node page, when
   `authStore.user` resolves after the anonymous first pass. About one load in three throws. It is
   three characters of guard (`loadedFor === key` before the read, which the same function already
   does for every assignment) in a file this step does not own, so it is in `todo.md` and the
   browser script counts and PRINTS it rather than failing on it.

Two more came off the screenshots rather than off an error: the sentence under each law citation
was as bold as the citation (everything in a `<th>` inherits it) and the "no prize" chip was a
`neutral-pill` on a card whose background was the alt surface the pill itself uses, so the one chip
that says the whole public-promise regime does not apply was invisible.

### Left open

- **No notifications.** Rule 12 of the brief forbids a new type, and four were wanted: **a
  registration decided**, **a stage opened**, **results published**, **a complaint answered**. Each
  is a row in `_PREFERENCE_FIELD_FOR_TYPE` and a label in `labels.ts`, and all four want the same
  recipient logic the event app already has.
- **A DPA (umowa powierzenia) between EdMat and an organiser** does not exist. `LEGAL.md` §9 says
  the processor relationship requires one under GDPR art. 28(3), and §10 now names it.
- **A contest has no `language` column**, so a reader who narrows the activity feed with
  `?content_locales=` does not see contest rows — the same as concept rows today
  (`activity/services.py: _content_locale_feed_filter`). Fixing it means a column on `Contest`,
  which is step A's migration, not B's.
- **The regulamin is not in `translations/`.** `ContestRulesSection` is versioned legal text whose
  translation is a decision somebody signs off, not a field in a side-by-side editor;
  `translations/targets.py` says so at the contest entry.
- **No `GenericRelation` on `Contest`** for `text_versions`, so every contest's text resolution is
  one extra query (above). It is one line in step A's file and adds no column.
- **The manual hub still promises a screenshot in every chapter** and the contests chapter has none
  until the integrator re-shoots them.
- **The work dashboard's four sections are empty on this branch** — `contests/work.py` is step A's
  and answers `[]` — so what B's tests pin is that the sections are registered under the right flag
  and that registering them broke nothing. The same is true of the profile's `placements` block,

## 17CE.A — Contests, step A: the app, its rules, and every page of it (2026-10-09)

`prompts/18-contests-a-core.md` against `CONTESTS-BRIEF.md` §3.A, on `contest/a-core` from the prep
`092f80d`. Fourteen interface tasks, all fourteen shipped. The sibling step B (`contest/b-personalise`)
was building `presets.py`, `personalize.py`, the registries in every other app, `/about/contests`,
the manual chapter and `LEGAL.md` at the same time; this section is only what A did.

### What the law actually made us build

The brief's §1 turns `CONTESTS-LAW.md` into decisions, and almost every structural choice below is
one of those decisions rather than an engineering preference. Five are worth restating because they
are the reason the code is shaped the way it is:

1. **`has_prize` is a toggle that unlocks obligations, and it is off by default.** With no promised
   prize there is no *przyrzeczenie publiczne* (KC art. 919 §1 needs one), so no claim deadline is
   required, the gambling act does not apply and no PIT arises. The `challenge` preset is therefore
   the simplest contest to run AND the safest, and `ContestSerializer.validate` silently clears
   `prize_regime` and `prize_claim_deadline` when the toggle goes off rather than making a founder
   clear three fields they can no longer see.
2. **The claim deadline is the single hard field.** KC art. 921 §1 makes a prize promise with no
   deadline *bezskuteczne* — the whole promise. It is nullable in the schema, because a draft is
   allowed to be incomplete, and refused by `announce_block_reason` with its own word, so the
   organiser learns which field and why instead of getting a validation error on a date.
3. **A draw is structurally impossible rather than discouraged.** No `draw` advancement exists; ties
   SHARE a rank (and the next rank skips) so there is nothing to break by lot; `top_n` takes
   everybody tied at the cut-off for the same reason. `rules._looks_like_a_draw` refuses
   `chance_element` on an announce, on a stage description as it is typed, and on the merit criteria
   — matched on eight stems after Polish diacritics are stripped, deliberately a short list somebody
   can read and argue with, because a false positive here blocks a real announce. Chance deciding
   *any* stage makes the whole thing a *gra losowa*, and u.g.h. art. 89's penalty stacks with KKS
   art. 108's 240 *stawki dzienne*.
4. **Publishing a winner's name is its own, revocable consent.** `publish_name` defaults False, has
   its own PATCH, and **only the participant may change it** — not the organiser, who is the party
   it is given to. `ContestResultSerializer` then shows a full name only when the consent AND the
   contest's `publication_default` both allow it: two separate conditions, both server-side, so no
   page can re-assemble the rule. That separation is UODO's own lesson from its own pupil-contest
   regulamin, and the demo seed deliberately has one entrant opted in on a contest whose default is
   `initials`, so the page shows both halves of it at once.
5. **A minor's consent is a NAME and a timestamp, never a boolean.** `guardian_consent: true` in the
   request becomes `guardian_consent_at`, because a boolean cannot be shown to anybody afterwards.
   `minor` and `guardian_consent_required` are two different words with two different sentences:
   "this contest takes nobody your age" and "we need your guardian". And by the owner's standing
   default a minor does not lodge a complaint themself — free text to a stranger — so
   `complain_block_reason` answers `minor` and the page prints the sentence that says the guardian
   writes to the organiser instead of greying a button.

### The models (migration `0002_stages_registrations_scores_results`)

Nineteen new fields on `Contest` and nine new models. Two shapes are worth knowing:

- **Nothing stores a score.** `ContestScore` is one juror's marks for one problem of one submission;
  a submission's points are the MEAN over the jurors who scored each problem, summed over problems,
  recounted on every read (house rule 5). A stored total drifts the moment a juror edits a cell, and
  a contest whose ranking disagrees with its own scoring matrix is worse than one that takes two
  `COUNT`s longer to draw. The honest limit is stated in `submission_points` itself: a problem no
  juror has scored contributes zero, so a half-scored submission reads low rather than unknown, and
  `scored_problem_count` beside it is how the matrix and the ranking preview say which is which.
- **`ContestResult` rows exist only between `publish_results` and `unpublish_results`.** There is no
  `is_published` flag: the row's existence IS the publication, so a published result cannot secretly
  be unpublished and a draft ranking cannot leak. Unpublishing deletes them and is allowed only
  while the complaints window is open — after it the ranking is the record and the answer to a
  mistake is a new version (house rule 12).

`ContestSubmission.advanced` is the one derived-looking field that is deliberately a DECISION:
`rules.advance` is its only writer, and a participant who was told they went through must not stop
having gone through because a juror later changed a mark. It is idempotent, so re-scoring and
advancing again is safe.

There is **no `number` field on a registration.** The anonymised label the jury scores against is
the row's position among the contest's registrations ordered by arrival, computed at serialization —
registrations are never deleted (every terminal status keeps its row, house rule 12) so the position
is stable, and a stored sequence allocated under SQLite's single writer would be a retry loop for
something two queries answer.

### `access._registered`, replaced

The prep left it returning `False`. It is now "has a place-holding registration" —
`requested` + `accepted`, defined once in `models.PLACE_HOLDING_STATUSES`. `requested` counting is
the deliberate half: a request is a place held pending a decision, exactly as `events` counts a
`pending` row, and somebody waiting on a decision must already be able to read the regulamin they
will be judged against. `can_view` gained a third arm for it, so **a participant of a private
contest sees it because they are a member** — without that line somebody the organiser had just
accepted would be 404ed off the page they had been let into. `visible_contests` gained the matching
`Q()`, and `test_rules.MembershipTests` pins the two against each other for all five registration
statuses: a filter and an object check that disagree is exactly the shape house rule 4 warns about.

### The API, and the two refusal codes

Seven viewsets and two plain views, all behind `feature_gate('contests')`. 403 for "you may not",
**409 for "the world moved"** (already announced, already published, already entered, the last
organiser, a stage with submissions), 400 for a malformed request — and `announce_block_reason`'s
words come back as 409 because every one of them means "the world is not ready", not "your request
was wrong". `ContestViewSet.create` asks `creation_block_reason(user, 'contest')` like the other
four founding paths, validates `preset_key` against `presets.visible_to(user)` (a non-staff founder
cannot pick `kuratorium` — a false "kuratoryjny" claim harms pupils who believe they are earning an
exam exemption), lays out the preset's own answers, the regulamin's twelve empty sections and the
stage ladder from the preset's offsets, then calls `personalize.apply_preset` and returns its report
under `personalisation` — which on this branch honestly says `skipped: ['not_built']`, and the
wizard shows that rather than a promise.

**A stage's problems are 404 before it opens**, to everybody but its staff. An exercise's statement
is public content already; WHICH exercises a stage uses is the contest. 404 rather than 403, because
for an entrant they genuinely do not exist yet. And the stage payload carries the **statement only**
— `ContestProblemSerializer` sends no `answer`, no hint and no solution pool, enforced in the
serializer that builds the payload rather than in a frontend that chooses not to draw them.

### "Prefilling with current users"

`contests/people.py: suggested_people` unions the four rosters the founder is already on — course
staff (both arms: the instructor is denormalised onto the course row and is not necessarily a
`CourseStaff` row), event staff (one arm: `Event.save()` creates a real `organiser` row for the
host, and the difference between the two apps is exactly why this is four reads and not one clever
join), organisation members, material-project members — each candidate carrying `via` entries of the
form `'<kind>:<title>'`. **The sentence is the frontend's**, in both languages: a server that sent
"staff with you on Analiza I" would be a third i18n axis nobody asked for. It is the honest
substitute for the people-search gap the root `CLAUDE.md` has named for months, and the account-id
box stays underneath, because the person a founder most wants on a jury may be somebody they have
never shared a roster with.

### The compliance panel

`compliance.report(contest)` evaluates `presets.checklist_for` against the rows. **Three states, not
two**: `ok`, `missing` (the organiser can see which field) and `warning` — something no database can
check (has the prize actually been handed over? is the contest on the minister's wykaz? is there a
photo consent?) — which says so rather than showing a tick it has not earned. An item this module
has no evaluation for comes back `warning`, never a silent `ok` (house rule 10), so step B can add a
checklist item to `presets.py` without touching this file and it shows as something to look at.
`not_legal_advice: True` is a FIELD rather than a sentence in the copy, because the copy is the one
thing a second surface can forget, and `CompliancePanel.svelte` refuses to draw without it. Every
item carries its `LAW` keys and the panel draws each citation's marker — `verified`, `secondary`,
`unverified`, `disputed` — and a test asserts that every key the panel can cite exists in
`presets.LAW` with a marker the frontend has a label for. The tax block shows the "science" limb and
the 2 000 zł line and the gross-up (÷ 0.9, practice not statute), and **never the mass-media limb**,
which is disputed for an internet announcement.

### The interface — nine routes, nine components

`/contests` (four tabs, filters, the creation-gate note), `/contests/new` (the four-screen wizard,
nothing saved until the last screen), `/contests/[id]`, `/contests/[id]/rules` (reader + editor +
print), `/contests/[id]/stages/[stageId]` (the entrant's answer boxes and the organiser's problem
picker, on one address), `/contests/[id]/judge`, `/contests/[id]/results`, `/contests/[id]/manage`,
`/contests/[id]/certificate/[resultId]`. Components: `ContestCard`, `StatusStrip`, `StageLadder`,
`RolePicker`, `GuardianConsentBlock`, `CompliancePanel`, `ScoringMatrix`, `RankingTable`,
`RulesSectionEditor`.

**The organiser is the first thing on the contest page, above the title.** Not a layout preference:
EdMat is never the *przyrzekający*, and a page that showed a prize and a deadline without saying
whose promise they were would be this site appearing to make the promise. The same sentence is on
every hub card and on the printed certificate, which names the organiser as the issuer, says EdMat
is only the medium, says the copy is unsigned, and says that whatever rights a laureate's title
carries depend on that contest's own rules and the minister's list — not on this document.

Three markers on `/contests/[id]` for the integrator: `contests: compliance (A)` (A's own panel,
mounted), `contests: translations (integration)`, `contests: discussion (integration)`.

### Verified — what was actually run, with the numbers

- `manage.py test contests config --keepdb` — **165 tests, OK**, 239 s of tests on top of about
  eleven minutes of setup. **That setup cost is per invocation and `--keepdb` cannot remove it**:
  nine of the ten databases are the in-memory log shards (`file:memorydb_logs_*?mode=memory`),
  which exist only while a connection holds them, so every run rebuilds them — the root
  `CLAUDE.md` already says so and it is worth repeating, because a run that sits for ten minutes
  printing "Using existing test database for alias 'logs_4'…" looks hung and is not. An earlier
  `--parallel 4` run of the same two apps was **164 OK** in 69 s when the shards happened to still
  be alive from a concurrent process; the serial number above is the honest one to plan around.
  A `contests` migration also invalidates the on-disk `default` clone, so the first run after
  `0002` additionally pays the full migrate.
  The first run of `test_api.py` found one real bug of exactly the kind `backend/CLAUDE.md` warns
  about: catching an `IntegrityError` on a unique-constraint collision **without its own
  savepoint** leaves the transaction broken, so the next query answers
  `TransactionManagementError` — a 500 on a request whose honest answer is 409. Both such inserts
  now sit in `with transaction.atomic():`. A later run (102 in `contests` after one more test was
  added) found a second one, in the test rather than the app: `coauthoring` creates the owner's
  `ProjectMember` row with the project and `one_owner_per_project` is a partial unique index, so
  writing that row by hand is an `IntegrityError`.
- **`people.py` had a real bug that only the dev database could show**, and it is the reason that
  test exists: the four rosters are four other apps' models and they do NOT share a field name.
  `MaterialProject` has no `title` at all — it is a `OneToOne` on a material whose name lives in
  that material's translations — so `suggested_people` raised `AttributeError` for anybody who
  co-writes a material. Found by calling it against the real dev accounts rather than by any
  assertion; the test now exercises every arm.
- `manage.py check` clean; `makemigrations --check --dry-run` "No changes detected";
  `testing/check_databases_declared.py` prints **0 classes still unresolved, in 0 files**.
- `manage.py seed_contest_demo` **run twice**: the second run reports "Refreshed" for both contests
  and creates nothing — 2 contests, 4 registrations, 4 submissions, 32 scores, 4 results
  (laureate / finalist / distinction / participant), 1 answered complaint.
- `npm run check` **0 errors, 0 warnings** over 7017 files (after recompiling Paraglide — a stale
  catalogue throws `m.x is not a function` at runtime and `svelte-check` reports every key as
  missing, which is what the first run did).
- `npx eslint src e2e` — clean for everything this step wrote. One pre-existing error remains in
  `e2e/attachments.mjs` (`'API' is assigned a value but never used`), present at the branch point
  `092f80d` and left alone. `npm run build` OK.
- Both catalogues **identical at 4547 keys**, verified programmatically; 434 new `contests_*` keys,
  every placeholder set checked to match between `en` and `pl` before the files were written (a
  mismatch there gives Paraglide two different signatures and breaks the call site in exactly one
  language — the sort of thing `npm run check` cannot see).
- `node e2e/contests.mjs` against real servers on ports 5271 / 8171 — **58 checks, 58 passed, 0
  failed, zero page errors**, screenshots looked at. The first run reported six failures and
  **every one of them was the script's fault, not the product's**, which is worth recording
  because four of the six are the shapes `e2e/CLAUDE.md` already names:
  * three were counting rows before the fetch that fills them came back (traps 25 and 27). The
    hub reported "0 cards" while the API had three; the matrix reported "0 rows" and then went on
    to type into those very rows, because Playwright's own locators auto-wait and a `.count()`
    does not. All three now wait for the response or for the row, never for a timeout.
  * one was a **vacuous pass** (trap 8): "it is anonymised — a number, not a name" passed on an
    EMPTY heading, because "contains no name" is true of nothing at all. It now requires the
    number to be there as well.
  * one asserted the wrong rule: it refused the jury's view expecting `stage_open` while the
    token holder was not yet on the jury, so the real answer was `not_juror`.
  * one asserted **404 where the backend's own convention says 403**: an entrant CAN see the
    contest, so the contest is not hidden from them — only the organiser's obligations are, and
    `backend/CLAUDE.md` is explicit that a non-owner gets 404 via queryset scoping and a
    real-but-wrong party gets 403. The script was wrong; the view was right.
  The second run found the white-on-teal chip described below, in a screenshot, with every
  assertion green. The third run is the 58/58.

### Found outside this step's scope

**`presets.LAW`'s citations are English-only, and they are drawn inside a Polish page.** The
compliance panel, the regulamin editor and the wizard's law preview all render
`"PIT art. 21 ust. 1 pkt 68 — prizes ≤ 2 000 zł in contests 'w dziedzinie nauki' exempt…"` under
Polish headings — visible in `e2e/screens/contests-detail-draft.png` and impossible to miss once
looked at. Everything else on those surfaces IS bilingual (`title_en`/`title_pl` on the checklist,
`summary_*` and `info` on the preset, the markers and the state words from the catalogue); only the
citation strings are single-language, because `presets.LAW` is a flat `key -> (citation, marker)`
table. **`presets.py` is step B's file** (`CONTESTS-BRIEF.md` §3.B), so A did not widen it: the fix
is `LAW` carrying `citation_pl` beside `citation`, one line per row, and `law_as_api()` sending
both. Named here and in `todo.md` rather than worked around — a frontend map of thirty-two
citations would be a second copy of the research, drifting from the one in `presets.py`.

`frontend/CLAUDE.md`'s list of real theme tokens says `--text-on-accent` is NOT one of them, and it
is right: the first draft of `ScoringMatrix` used `var(--text-on-accent, #fff)` and would have drawn
a white-on-accent button only because of the fallback. The real token is `--accent-contrast`, and
the `button-primary` mixin already uses it — so the fix was to use the mixin. Worth repeating here
because the file's own warning ("an undefined custom property drops the whole declaration") is what
made it findable in one grep.

And the same file's colour vocabulary caught a second one, this time only in a screenshot:
`RolePicker`'s "chosen person" chip wrote `--accent-contrast` on `--accent-soft` by hand and drew
**white text on a pale teal tint** — the chosen juror's name was invisible on the wizard's third
screen. `svelte-check`, `eslint` and the build all passed; `e2e/screens/contests-wizard-3-people.png`
showed it immediately. The mixin that exists for exactly this is `selected-soft` (tint + accent text
+ a 1px accent border), and the chip now uses it. "A filled accent box is a command, never a
selection" is the sentence that explains both halves of the mistake.

### Left open, by design — all named rather than quietly omitted (house rule 14)

- **Notifications.** No new types, per the brief's rule 12. The four that are wanted:
  **registration decided** (accepted / declined / disqualified — the participant currently learns it
  by looking), **stage opened** (the one with a deadline attached), **results published**, and
  **complaint answered** (the organiser owes an answer within a window and the participant has no
  way to know it arrived). All four are `notifications/services.notify()` calls plus a preference
  field; none is built.
- **Teams beyond a `team_name`.** A real roster with a captain, and `kc_920_3`'s "who receives which
  share" as structured rows rather than a paragraph in §7. `team_size_max` exists on the model and
  nothing enforces it.
- **Community voting** (preset (k) in the research) — not built until a lawyer answers
  `CONTESTS-LAW.md` §14 item 1, because community voting that decides a prize is the shape that gets
  read as a lottery.
- **A DPA (umowa powierzenia) template** between EdMat and an organiser. `LEGAL.md` is step B's and
  names it; nothing generates one.
- **Proctoring beyond a role name.** `proctor` is a role and nothing else — no camera, no lockdown,
  and not wanted.
- **People search** is still the known gap; `suggested_people` is the honest substitute, not a fix.
- **An on-site stage does not create its event for you.** `ContestStage.event` is a real FK and the
  wizard asks whether the founder will want one, but the event itself is still created from
  `/events/new` and attached afterwards. The wizard says exactly that rather than implying a flow.
- **`lib/utils/contestLabels.ts` is a temporary home.** `CONTESTS-BRIEF.md` §4 rule 6 gives the six
  enum label maps to step B in `labels.ts` and says "A reads them" — but A's nine pages cannot be
  built or run on A's own branch without them. They live in that one file, with the keys and message
  keys the brief specifies, and **integration deletes it and re-points its eight importers at
  `labels.ts`**. The file's own header says so. A's own `CONTEST_BLOCK_LABELS` IS in `labels.ts`,
  under A's comment, as the brief requires.
- **One line in `Header.svelte` outside A's three markers**: `/contests` added to
  `SECTION_PREFIXES`, without which the `aria-current` on the nav link A appends is dead and never
  marks itself as the current page for a screen-reader user. Step B does not touch the nav, so
  nothing collides with it.
- **`contests_placeholder` is now an unused catalogue key** — the prep's placeholder copy, left in
  both catalogues because removing a key is a bigger edit than leaving one. The integrator can drop
  it.
- **No upload control on an answer, and the brief's suggested shape does not work.** §3.A's
  context table proposed "attach to the contest node with tier `staff` and reference the row from
  the answer", but `attachments/access.py: can_attach` allows attaching to a NODE only to that
  node's STAFF — deliberately, and in a file step A does not own — while a contest participant is
  a member. So `ContestAnswer.attachment` is a real FK the API accepts (an organiser or proctor
  can attach a scan on somebody's behalf, which is the on-site case) and the participant-facing
  control is not drawn, because it would be refused. **The clean fix is a `contest_answer` target
  kind in `attachments/targets.py`**, added to `ROW_TARGET_KINDS` with the answer's own author as
  its owner — the shape `needs` already uses for "whoever filed it may attach the photo that
  explains it". One entry in a registry plus a two-line `node_behind`; it belongs to whoever owns
  `attachments/` next, and `todo.md` has it.
- **The law citations are English-only** — see "Found outside this step's scope" above. It is a
  house-rule-1 gap on a surface A built, with the fix in a file A does not own.
- **No permission-matrix rows** for the new endpoints (`events/test_permission_matrix.py`'s shape).
  §5 of the brief already assigns them to the integrator; `test_api.py` covers the same ground for
  the paths that matter, but not the systematic `/api/<thing>/undefined/` sweep.

## 17CE.C — The state of contests on `/about`, in the seed, and the deploy kit (2026-10-10)

**The ask.** Two in a row the morning after §17CE: first *"you will be publishing in edmat's about
info about current state of contests: issues, what's lacking, what's ready, etc with possibly your
comments there signed as user claude-anthropic"* — with the code read-only for that part — and then
*"prepare deploy kit that is also going to import data on contests to about"*. The first was done
as data on the dev database through the seed's own helpers (`work/edmat_project.py: _upsert_plan`,
`_write_bilingual`, the thread writer's rule for a comment's identity); the second is what makes
that data arrive on production the same way everything else on `/about` does: through
`seed_edmat_project`, not by hand.

**The account is `anthropic-claude`**, the research account the seed created on 2026-10-07
(display name "Claude (Anthropic)", a bio that says it comments on what it read and checked, no
usable password). The owner wrote "claude-anthropic"; that account is the one that exists, and a
near-duplicate would have been worse than a transposition. Nothing was escalated for it: the
auto-mode classifier refused making the account an organisation admin and issuing it an API token,
so the rows were written the way `_upsert_thread` writes the Gemini thread — under the account, by
the seed path, never by signing in.

**What the seed now writes (the code change of this section):**

- **A `contests` subproject** in `SUBPROJECTS` — the plan "Konkursy / Contests", bilingual like the
  others, with the module's own "left open" list as **nine pending steps** (the four notifications,
  the DPA, teams, community judging, the answer attachment, the language column, the regulamin
  outside `translations/`, the manual's screenshots, the trunk fast-forward). Its done steps are the
  §17CE rows: `edmat_history.py: SUBPROJECT_BY_REF` now files `17CE`, `17CE.A`, `17CE.B` and this
  section under `contests` instead of `events`/`management`, which closes the "no `contests`
  subproject on `/about`" left-open of §17CE. The table was re-exported.
- **A second thread file, `work/edmat_project_threads.json`** — a LIST of threads located not by a
  standing page but by **a plan's title** (`"plan": "Konkursy / Contests"` → `plans/<pk>`, whatever
  pk that plan has on the database at hand) or by **the organisation** (`"organization": true` →
  `organizations/edmat`). `_thread_location()` resolves the three shapes and refuses anything
  `community.discussions` would not accept; `_upsert_thread` took `node=`/`organization=` and a
  `replier` became optional. Four comments under the plan (ready / lacking / issues and risks /
  notes on the code, each Polish then English) and one pointer at the top of `/about`, all dated
  2026-10-10, identified by their bold first line, so a second run refreshes and never duplicates.
  `build_edmat_project` returns them as `project_threads`; the command prints one `thread /plans/<pk>`
  line per file entry.
- Tests: the command's printed paths include the two new threads; a new test loads the file, builds,
  finds the four and the one under the right locations by `anthropic-claude`, and builds again for
  zero new rows; the secret-shape sweep covers the new file.

**The deploy kit** is `deploy/UPDATE-2026-10-10.md` and `FUW/UPDATE-20261010.tar.gz`, built by
`deploy/fuw/pack.sh` from this branch with `EDMAT_REPO` pointed at the worktree (the packer and
`apply-on-server.sh` are gitignored, so the worktree carries a copy of `deploy/fuw/` for the build).
The note lists the cycle's five migrations (all additive), the one flag (`contests`, seeded ON), and
the one seed command the data needs; the note is the place that says what to check afterwards.

**Verified, by running:** `manage.py test work` green after the export, `manage.py check` clean,
`seed_edmat_project --owner piotrek` on the dev database refreshing the hand-written plan 34 in
place (0 plans, 0 steps, 0 comments created on the second run — the titles and first lines match),
`pack.sh` completing with every prerendered page present, and `/about` in a real browser showing

**Left open:** the publish branch (`publish/2026-10-10`) is not built here — the replay script of
the previous kits is not in this worktree and publishing is the owner's step anyway (root

## 17CF — Every composer is behind a button: no page carries an input nobody asked for (2026-10-09, `ux/colour-pass`)

Owner: *"i want inputs of comments to be disappearing unless clicking comment or reply buttons (add
them if dont have them everywhere where a comment or sth discussable)"*.

Before this, a reader who opened an exercise, a material, a tutoring listing, an issue, a concept, a
course lesson, a conference session or a post met an empty text box between the content and the
comments, and the activity feed opened with the whole post composer — anchor pickers, audience,
language, reference search, image — above the first row anybody came to read. Every one of those
boxes belongs to somebody who has decided to write; none of them belongs to the reader who has not.

**The collapse lives in `CommentForm`, not in its hosts.** One prop — `collapsedLabel` — turns the
box into a single quiet button ("Write a comment" / *„Napisz komentarz"*), and the box comes back to
being a button after a post, so a thread that has just taken a comment looks the way it did before.
Eighteen pages render a thread through `DiscussionThread` and not one of them had to change: the
component that owns the input owns its reveal. Two further props came out of what the hosts needed:
`composing` is `$bindable` so a host with another way in can open the box, and `aboveEditor` is a
snippet drawn inside the form, which is where the standing-page composer's *"your name (optional)"*
field had to move — a name field left sitting above a button that says "write a comment" is an input
asking to be filled in for nothing.

**Reply came out of the "⋯" menu and became a button under the comment**, for the reason the vote
column beside each comment was never in that menu either: it is the thing most readers actually
reach for, and a reveal nobody can find is worse than a box that is always open. The menu's fixed
order (owner, 2026-10-08: reply above the AI mark) is untouched — it governs what a surface passes,
and a comment now passes reply as a control of its own. **A statement, a hint, a solution and a
review still route reply through the menu**, because none of them has a box of its own to open;
their menu item opens (or scrolls to) the thread, and since the thread's composer is now collapsed,
each of those three call sites binds `composing` so that "reply" ends at a box rather than at
another button.

**`CommentNode` learned `canReply`**, which is a small honesty fix that fell out of this. The reply
box was offered to every reader of every thread, including one who could not post into it — a
signed-out reader on an exercise, a non-member reading a public course discussion — and the refusal
arrived after they had written their reply. The host knows the answer and now says it.

**`RichEditor.focus()`** is what makes one click enough: a reveal that leaves the caret somewhere
else costs a second click. In source mode it focuses the textarea; in rich mode the Tiptap instance
may not exist yet, because the import is lazy, so the request is remembered (`wantFocus`) and
honoured when the editor mounts.

**Two other always-open inputs went the same way**, because leaving them would have made the
collapsed thread below them look like an accident: the review form on `/materials/[id]` and
`/tutoring/[id]` ("Write a review"), and the post composer on `/activity` ("Write a post"). The
review form inside the exercise page's modal is left open — that modal is already something somebody
opened on purpose — and the post composer still opens by itself when a claim chip brought the reader
to `/activity` with an anchor already chosen, which is somebody arriving in order to post.
`ReviewForm` carries the same three lines as `CommentForm` and both say so in place (house rule 13:
strike two; a third collapsing form earns the shared one).

### Verified

`npm run check` 0 errors / 0 warnings, `npx eslint .` clean, `npm run build` clean, both catalogues
identical at **4114** keys (three new: `discussion_startComment`, `review_start`, `post_start`).
`check_accessibility.ts` against the live servers: 48 pages, **0 critical/serious** nodes (3 pages
failed to load, on endpoints this change does not touch).

A browser pass against both real dev servers, **14/14**, screenshots looked at: a thread opens with
no box and a "Napisz komentarz" button; one click draws the box **with the caret already in it**;
posting lands the comment and the box goes back to being a button; every comment carries a visible
*„Odpowiedz"* that opens a reply box under it; the statement's "⋯ → Odpowiedz" lands in an **open**
box; `/activity` and `/materials/[id]` show their buttons and open on one click. On `/about`, signed
in: the button, 64 reply buttons, the box on one click; signed out, where that location refuses
anonymous posting: the refusal sentence and no button at all.

`e2e/activity-feed.mjs` **19/20** — the one failure is the `.post .katex` half of a conjunction on
`/posts/[id]`, which is a timing assumption about the lazily-loaded maths chunk in a fresh context
(the thread half of the same check is fine, and the comment it then posts lands). The same run
surfaced a **500 from `/api/galleries/for-target/?target_type=post&target_id=6`**, which predates
this change and was not chased.

**Nine browser scripts were updated**, because a script that drove a composer now has to ask for it
first: `comment-input-kinds`, `rich-editor`, `sketch`, `comment-attachments` (which also stops
clicking a menu item that no longer exists and clicks the new `.comment__reply`), `comment-history`,
`classroom`, `activity-feed`, `about-discussions` (which gained a check that there is no box before
the click), and one unused constant in `attachments.mjs` that was failing `eslint` on `main`.

### Left open

- **Two scripts could not be run to completion and were left as they are:** `rich-editor.mjs`
  asserts English copy ("Editor") without going through `e2e/english.mjs`, so it fails on the Polish
  base locale at a line this change does not touch, and `comment-history.mjs` fills the login form
  after 800 ms, which is below the cold-compile margin `activity-feed.mjs` uses (2500 ms). Both
  predate this change; both are one line.
- **The edit box and the reply box are unchanged** — they were already mounted by a button, so they
  take no `collapsedLabel`.
- **Cancel discards the draft**, because the collapse unmounts the editor. That is the normal
  behaviour of a cancel button and nothing on this site persists a draft, but it is now reachable in
  one more place.
- **`SolutionEntrySection`'s own composer is not collapsed.** It is already behind "Dodaj
  wskazówkę" / "Dodaj rozwiązanie", which is the same bargain by a different mechanism.

## 17CG — Content management on the board rows: an edit that is actually visible, and attachments where the API already allowed them (2026-10-10, `ux/colour-pass`)

The owner: *"add content management (eg edit, add attachement (ag a comment),) to needs and etc.
research how to do it properly"*. Scope settled with them before any code: **all four board rows**
(task, plan, need, goal — and poll, which turned out to be a fifth), with the attachments panel on
each row's own page **and** its expanded card.

### What the research found, and why it changed the plan

Two things, and the first was a live bug nobody could have seen from a test:

**1. A plain edit of a translated row changed a column no reader ever saw.**
`translations/resolve.py` reads a `TextVersion` whenever the row has one and falls back to the
row's own column only when it has none at all (that fallback is what made the whole translations
app additive in the first place — §17BX). Every management write serializer, meanwhile, wrote
`title`/`description` straight onto the column. So on any row somebody had translated — which is
every row on `/about`, because `seed_edmat_project` splits its bilingual text into versions —
`TaskCard`'s "Edit" and `/plans/[id]`'s details form **returned 200 with the new text in the
response and changed nothing a reader would ever see.**

It was found by probing the dev database rather than by any assertion, which is the point: the
symptom is a success. The probe, rolled back in a transaction:

```
Task 13  column title : 'Skompletować co najmniej 7 założycieli, realnie 10'
         after writing 'PLAIN-EDIT-PROBE' to the column:
         resolve(pl) : 'Skompletować co najmniej 7 założycieli, realnie 10'
         resolve(en) : 'Gather at least 7 founders, realistically 10'
```

**2. The UI was behind the API.** `attachments/targets.py` had registered `task` `plan` `need`
`goal` and `comment` since §17CD, and `AttachmentsPanel` says in its own docstring that it is
"usable anywhere else with two props" — yet it was mounted in exactly one place. And `PATCH
/api/needs/{id}/` has always accepted a need's kind, skill level, estimated hours, deadline, remote
flag and wanted count, while nothing in the app ever sent them: changing one meant Django admin.

### The fix for (1): one writer for a row's text

`translations/services.write_original_text(obj, heading=, body=, user=)` routes a single-language
edit through `write_versions`, and `translations.serializers.PlainTextWriteMixin` is the other half
of `TranslatedTextMixin` — that one makes the READ answer in the reader's language, this one makes
the WRITE land where that read looks. It now sits on `TaskWriteSerializer`, `NeedSerializer`,
`PlanStepUpdateSerializer`, `GoalSerializer`, `GoalCriterionSerializer`, `PollUpdateSerializer`,
`OrganizationWriteSerializer` and `ContestSerializer`; `PlanViewSet.partial_update` writes its three
fields by hand and so asks the service by hand.

Four decisions inside it:

- **`False` is not a failure.** A row with no versions keeps the old behaviour exactly — the column
  IS the truth and no version row is invented out of an ordinary edit. That is what keeps this
  additive, and it is tested.
- **`None` means "leave that half alone"**, and the missing half is read from the VERSION, not from
  the row's column — the column is precisely the thing that may already have drifted.
- **Only the original language is touched.** The other languages keep their own `updated_at`, so a
  reader of a translation is told the original is newer. That is true, and saying it is not the lie
  the app exists to prevent; the lie would be re-stamping every language as current. `TranslateFields`
  remains how somebody writes both at once in one submission.
- **The prefetch cache is dropped after a text write.** Found in a browser, not in a test: every
  management view prefetches `text_versions` so `resolve` answers in memory for a board of fifty
  rows, and that cache predates the write — so the 200 came back carrying the OLD text while the
  database was already right, and the page showed the previous title until a reload. DRF's own
  `UpdateModelMixin` drops this cache for the same reason.

### The fix for (2): the surfaces

- **`NeedForm.svelte`** — the one form that writes a need, in `TaskForm`'s shape, used by the
  panel's "Post a need" and by a new **"Edit the posting"** on the `⋯`.
- **`/needs/[id]` gained the whole menu** — it had none at all, on the page a shared link lands on.
  Edit, "Edit in both languages…", and cancel/reopen, which **moved off** the manager section: two
  places to cancel the same need is how two surfaces start disagreeing.
- **The need's description is rendered** (`MathContent`) instead of printed into a bare `<p>`. It
  was the last management body on the platform drawn as plain text, so a list or a formula somebody
  typed came out as its own source.
- **`AttachmentsPanel` on the row surfaces**: `/needs/[id]`, `/tasks/[id]`, `/plans/[id]`,
  `/goals/[id]`, `/polls/[id]`, and inside `TaskCard`, `GoalCard` and each poll row on a board.

Each of those passes a `canAttach` that includes **the row's own author** and not just the node's
staff, because `access.can_attach` does — "somebody who filed a need may attach the photo that
explains it". Passing only the staff would have hidden the form from the person that rule exists
for, and the API would have gone on answering correctly, so nothing would have complained.

Two props made that possible without a request per row: **`foldKey`** (two panels sharing one key
share their open state — the default stays the bare word `attachments` because `e2e/attachments.mjs`
addresses the node pages by it) and **`deferred`** (fetch when the reader OPENS the section, which
is what `FoldSection`'s `onopen` exists for). The first cut of `deferred` never rendered at all,
because the panel's condition was `enabled && loaded && …` — a browser run caught it in one click,
and the condition now reads `loaded ? rows.length > 0 || canAttach : deferred && canAttach`.

### A poll turned out to be the fifth row, and the only one with a rule of its own

`poll` joined `attachments/targets.py`, `/polls/[id]` and the poll rows on a board got panels, and
`PollSerializer` gained `node` — that page deliberately had no `NodeRef` at all ("manager actions
live on the panel"), and a surface that cannot ask "may you add something here" cannot draw the
panel.

The part worth remembering: **every other board row is visible to whoever may see the node, and a
poll is not.** A draft is managers-only and an open one is for the eligible, because the wording of
a question put to the room is as much of the decision as the count is (§17BI.H). So
`attachments/access.can_view_target` asks `decisions.rules.can_view_poll` for that one kind —
otherwise this app would have become the way to read a question nobody was shown.

### Verified

- `translations` gained `PlainEditTests` (9), `attachments` gained `PollTargetTests` (2);
  `manage.py check` and `makemigrations --check` clean.
- **`e2e/needs-content-management.mjs`, 26/26** against both real servers, as `piotrek` (the only
  owner of the `edmat` organisation — e2e trap 32). It drives the real `⋯`, edits three fields in
  one submission, **reloads** (the whole point: the broken write also came back correct in its own
  response), and asserts the English translation was left alone and reported as older.
- `npm run check` 0/0, `eslint` clean on the touched trees, the two new i18n keys in both
  catalogues (4589 each, identical key sets). `e2e/attachments.mjs` still 14/14, which is what the
  `foldKey` default is for.
- **The full backend suite: 3081 tests, one failure, and it was right.**
  `work.EdmatHistoryTests` fails the moment `HISTORY.md` grows a section, because the checked-in
  table is stale until `manage.py export_edmat_history` runs — and then fails AGAIN until the new
  reference is filed in `SUBPROJECT_BY_REF`, since an unlisted section would otherwise land in
  `platform` silently. §17CG is `management`, whose apps are the rows it is about. Two steps, not
  one, and worth knowing before writing the next section.

### Left open

- **A board row gives a plain reader no hint that it has attachments.** A deferred panel can only
  draw its shut line from `canAttach`, because the row count is exactly what has not been fetched;
  a reader who may not attach meets the files on the row's own page, where the panel is eager. The
  honest fix is an `attachments_count` on the four row serializers.
- **A draft plan's attachments are visible to anybody who may see the node.** A poll now inherits
  its own visibility; a plan's `draft` status is not consulted, which is pre-existing and was not
  widened here.
- **A draft poll's fields still cannot be edited** — mode, eligibility, the dates. Its question and
  description go through the `⋯` (draft only, as the server insists), but the create form is still
  the only writer of the rest; extracting a `PollForm` the way `NeedForm` was extracted is its own
  change.
- **`/tasks` (my tasks) draws no panels**, by the same reasoning `NeedsPanel`'s own "left open"
  already gave: a personal list of every task a person has is not a board.
- **Nothing is mounted on a comment**, although `comment` has been a registered kind since §17CD —
  comments already have `community.CommentAttachment`'s picture/PDF composer, and two attachment
  UIs on one surface is the thing §17CD refused to do on a course page. It goes the day
  `absorb_legacy_attachments --apply` runs.

## 17CH — `paczka2`: 214 exercises prepared for the live site, and the importer's three lies (2026-10-13, `ux/colour-pass`)

Owner: *"prepare these packages to upload as exercises on the production"* — three zips dropped into
`Database-of-Student-Exercise/paczka2/`, then: *"some of it extends analiza and rachunek
prawdopodobienstwa, but also delivers new topologia"*.

**What the three packages actually were.** Each is a course package in the retired corpus's own
format (`course.yaml` + `zadania/NNNN.md` + `materialy/`), which is why they looked ready to import
and were not.

- `analiza2.zip` — 505 zadania. Its first **383 are byte-identical** to what was imported in 2026-07
  (compared file by file against `content/courses/uw-matematyka-am2/zadania/`, 0 differing). The
  delivery is files `0384`–`0505`: **122 new exercises**, mostly *serie treningowe*.
- `topo1.zip` — **92 new exercises**, for a branch that exists nowhere.
- `prawd1.zip` — 357 zadania, **byte-identical to the corpus already live**, and
  `rachunek-prawdopodobienstwa` on edmat.net holds exactly those 357 rows (1–357, no gaps, same
  titles). It adds nothing. Said out loud rather than imported quietly: re-running it would rewrite
  357 live rows with their own content, and would blank their `submitted_by` unless `--author` were
  passed, because the file is the source of truth on a re-run.

**The collision nobody would have seen.** `(branch, number)` is the natural key, so a file carrying
`number: 384` does not create — it **updates**. On edmat.net `analiza-matematyczna` ends at 388, and
384–388 are five rows that have nothing to do with this package: a donated "Całka Gaussa", a
"Granica ciągu", one test submission and two Phase-3 e2e leftovers. Importing the package's own
numbers would have silently overwritten five exercises and created 117 instead of 122, and the run
would have reported success. The 122 are therefore stamped **389–510**, keeping each file's original
`id:` for provenance, and `preflight.py` asks the live API whether that range is still free before
anybody runs anything — because by the time it is run, it may not be.

**Three things the importer got wrong, found by running it rather than reading it.**

1. **`\\[3mm]` is a LaTeX line break, not display maths.** `check_math` counted the `\[` inside it
   and called **73 of the 954 files** unbalanced — 11 of them in these batches, and one bad file
   aborts the whole run on purpose. The fix is `count_delimiters`, which walks the string and
   consumes both characters of a `\\`, so a genuinely missing `\)` is still caught (its own test).
   `frontend/scripts/check_katex_compatibility.ts` has carried a comment about this exact
   false-positive class since Phase 4; the importer never got the same treatment, which is the
   argument for the KaTeX checker's habit of writing its false positives down.
2. **`source: {original_problem_number: 11a}`** — a sub-problem letter, which the real corpus does
   carry — reached the database layer and came back as a `ValueError` from inside the SQL compiler,
   naming no file, half-way through the batch's transaction. It is now a validation error that names
   the file and says where the letter belongs. In the two files that have it, `build.py` puts the
   number at `11` and the letter into `source.name`, which is the line a reader sees under ŹRÓDŁO.
3. **`--create-topics` created topics alphabetically.** `order` is what `/branches/<slug>` sorts the
   topic filter by, so Topologia I's nine would have read "Ciągłość… / Iloczyny… / Podstawowe…" with
   "Przestrzenie ilorazowe" — the last thing the course teaches — fourth. They are now created in
   `batch.yaml`'s `topic_names:` order, which is the syllabus's.

**The branch is a decision, and it was the owner's.** `topologia`, named "Topologia", under
`matematyka`, `pl` only like every other taxonomy row — a Branch is subject matter and "Topologia I"
is a course (`taxonomy/models.py`). The owner's addition: **every one of the 92 carries the tag
`topologia-i`**, because a class looks for its own sheet by that name. `create_topologia_branch.py`
is that decision written down; the importer still refuses to create a branch.

**Verified by importing it.** Against a throwaway copy of the dev database (the dev database itself
is untouched): 122 created / 0 updated / 244 hint+solution entries / 0 new topics for Analiza, 92 /
0 / 184 / 9 for Topologia, and a second run of the Analiza batch printed "0 created, 122 updated" —
idempotent, as promised. Then the content sweep on that copy: `dump_text_fields` → `check:katex`,
**2896 translation rows, 0 fields with a real rendering issue**. Then both halves up against the
copy and a browser at four pages: `/branches/topologia` lists 92 with the nine topics in course
order, Topologia #1 and Analiza #389/#438 typeset their maths, carry the "Zweryfikowane rozwiązanie"
chip, and #438's ŹRÓDŁO line reads "…, zadanie 11a · p. 13" — the letter where it was put.

**What is on disk.** `Database-of-Student-Exercise/paczka2/prepared/` (untracked, beside the zips):
the two batches, `build.py` (the record of every change made to the authors' files, re-runnable),
`preflight.py`, `create_topologia_branch.py`, the patched command, `README.md` and `PRODUCTION.md`
— the runbook. `FUW/ZADANIA-20261013.tar.gz` (172 KB) is the same minus `_unzipped/`.

### Left open

- **Nothing has been imported into edmat.net.** The kit is built and the runbook is written; the
  owner runs it (the import is a production write, and the one code change it needs — the patched
  `import_exercises.py` — has to be on the server first, by copy or in the next bundle).
- **The three PDFs that came with the packages are not imported.** `import_exercises` carries no
  materials and nothing else does; two of them are somebody else's *skrypt*, whose licence is a
  `LEGAL.md` question rather than an import question.
- **`source.exercise_set`** — the training-series number, on all 122 Analiza files — has no column
  in `ExerciseSource` and is dropped. `source.name` names the series, so a reader loses nothing, but
  a filter by series is not possible.
- **`prawd1.zip` was not imported**, having nothing in it that is not already live. If the author
  meant to send a newer Rachunek Prawdopodobieństwa set, this one is not it.

## 17CI — Mail: the no-reply mailbox connected, password reset made real, and a Mail tab for the superuser (2026-10-14, `ux/colour-pass`)

The owner: *"prepare prod to have [the no-reply address] connected: mail confirmation, notifications,
etc. … would be super cool to have access to list of emails sent and received as superuser todoonet
on prod accessible through moderation tab. it comes from MXPLAN 001"*, with the SMTP/IMAP hosts and
the password; mid-way, *"the new prod bundle should also include the previously prepared materials
bundle … paczka2"*.

**What exists now.** A 41st app, `mail` (`backend/mail/CLAUDE.md` holds the rules):

- **Every outgoing message is a row first.** `OutboundEmail` is the queue AND the log; one `status`
  (`queued → sending → sent | failed | console`). The row is written in the request's transaction and
  sent by a daemon thread started from `on_commit`, so no request waits on OVH (eight mod_wsgi slots);
  `manage.py mail_cron`, every five minutes from `/etc/cron.d/edmat-mail`, retries failures (≤ 5),
  un-sticks dead sends, queues digests and reads the inbox. A claim is one WHERE-anchored `update()`,
  so the thread and the cron job can race for a row and exactly one sends it.
- **`console` is its own status, not "sent".** With no password the site uses Django's console
  transport and every row says "Not sent (no mail server)" — a dev box that claims it mailed
  somebody would be house rule 10 broken. The Mail tab's status line says the same in orange.
- **The log never holds a working link.** A confirmation or reset body is stored with `[[link]]`;
  the link is built at send time from the user (a signed `{u, e}` for confirmation, Django's
  `default_token_generator` for reset — both deterministic, so a retry builds a valid one). A
  superuser reading the log, or anybody holding a copy of the database, cannot take over an account
  with what is in it. This is why the e2e reads its links from the backend's stdout.
- **`EMAIL_BACKEND` is `mail.transport.LoggedEmailBackend`**, which logs anything sent around the
  queue (the admin, django-postman) as `kind='direct'` and passes it on; the queue opens the real
  transport directly, so nothing is logged twice.
- **Confirmation is derived** (`ConfirmedEmail.email == user.email`), sent at registration, re-sent
  from Settings → E-mail (throttled), and a completed password reset counts — that link was opened
  from the same inbox. Nothing is gated on it except the digest.
- **Password reset is real.** `/login` → "Nie pamiętasz hasła?" → `/forgot-password` (the same 202
  for every address) → the link → `/reset-password`, which refuses a used, stale or tampered link
  with a way to ask again, and deletes every API token on success. The confirm step has its own
  throttle scope: sharing `password_reset`'s 5/hour would have let two rejected passwords lock a
  person out of the link they had just been sent.
- **Notifications by mail are a digest, opt-in, hourly at most**, only to a confirmed address, and
  switching it on never mails the backlog. `notifications.services.notify()` is untouched: the
  digest reads `Notification` rows, so its three gates stay the only gates.
- **The inbox** is copied over IMAP read-only twice over (`select(readonly=True)` + `BODY.PEEK[]`;
  OVH webmail looks unchanged), incrementally by UID, as text: HTML is reduced with bleach, an
  attachment is a name and a size and its bytes are never kept (house rule 7).
- **The Mail tab** in `/moderation` is **superuser-only** — server (`IsSuperuser` on every
  `/api/mail/…`) and client (`authStore.user.isSuperuser` on the button and the panel) — not staff:
  it lists every address anybody registered with and what strangers mailed the project. Sent and
  Received, search, a status filter, a body per row, retry on a failed row, "fetch new mail now" and
  a test-send box.

**The password never touches the repository.** It is read from `/etc/edmat/mail-password` (0640
root:www-data) — a file, not envvars, because it contains `'` and `;`, and because Apache and the
cron job do not share an environment. `apply-on-server.sh` step 3e asks for it with `read -s` the
first time and installs the cron file; step 6a runs `mail_check`.

**paczka2 rides in the bundle** as `paczka2/` (the kit minus its 30 MB of source zips; `pack.sh`
refuses if the kit's `import_exercises.py` and the bundle's differ). Step 3d encodes the kit's own
PRODUCTION.md and imports only on an explicit yes, after preflight, and only if both dry runs said
exactly `122 created, 0 updated` / `92 created, 0 updated`.

**One thing fixed on the way, found by looking at a screenshot:** the moderation tab row never
wrapped, and "Dyskusje na stronach stałych" was already half off the page at 1280 px before Mail
joined it. `flex-wrap: wrap`.

### Verified

- **Against the real mailbox**, with the password in the environment for single commands only:
  `mail_check` — SMTP login OK (ssl0.ovh.net:465), IMAP login OK; one message sent from the mailbox to
  itself through the real queue path, then `mail_cron` fetched it back over IMAP with its Polish
  intact. DNS: SPF `include:mx.ovh.com -all` and both OVH DKIM selectors are in place; no DMARC.
- `manage.py test mail` 21/21, and **the full backend suite, 3107 tests, OK** (`--parallel 4
  --keepdb`, 22 min) — after one fix: `work`'s secret-shape check caught the mailbox address in this
  section's first paragraph, which the history table copies; it is now "[the no-reply address]".
  `check`, `makemigrations --check` clean; `check_databases_declared.py` 0.
- `e2e/mail.mjs` **23/23** against both dev servers with the console transport, zero page errors,
  and the screenshots looked at (which is how the tab row was found).
- `npm run check` 0/0; eslint clean on every touched file; 74 new keys in both catalogues
  (4663 each, identical key sets).

### Left open

- **Nothing is deployed.** The bundle is built; the owner applies it on webek4 (this VM cannot reach
  it) and types the password at step 3e.

- No kill switch: the password file is the switch, and the digest is per-person opt-in. A mail
  feature that ever goes to everybody by default should get a `FeatureFlag`.
- No instant per-notification mail, no per-type choice, no HTML mail, no bounce handling (bounces
  land in the inbox where the superuser can read them), no change-of-address flow, no mailed follow-up

- The sent list's status pill is truncated with an ellipsis on a narrow row; the full status is in
  the opened row.
