## 17CJ — Consent-free analytics, the terms of use, a rewritten privacy policy, and sign-in with Google / Apple / Microsoft (2026-10-14, `ux/colour-pass`)

The owner: *"research what kind of analytics can we get from users with our functional cookies etc
without asking for their consent: the goal is to analyze the data we collect in order to improve the
service, so no google analytics, adds, and selling their data, but prepare new moderation tab button
thats going to redirect to the dashboard … also, prepare our term and conditions and privacy policy
to meet todays state, and be ready for authentication using google, apple, etc."* One orchestrating
session, four sub-agents in this worktree (research → `ANALYTICS-LAW.md`; `analytics`; `sso`; legal
texts), built on top of §17CI's still-uncommitted mail work.

### The research — `ANALYTICS-LAW.md`

- **The cookie rule is PKE art. 399** (in force 2024-11-10), with only the transmission and
  "strictly necessary" exemptions — **no analytics exemption in Polish law**. The Digital Omnibus's
  proposed audience-measurement exemption is not adopted as of October 2026. EDPB 2/2023: any script
  that makes the browser send something is device access.
- **So the answer to "what can we get without consent" is: everything the server already sees,
  aggregated** — route traffic, per-content views, referrer host, coarse browser/OS/device class
  (never combined with IP), latency and errors, search counts without the term (category A); logged-in
  activity counts and cohorts only as aggregates with k ≥ 10, minors excluded (B); a Web Vitals beacon,
  any visitor id in storage, and the hashed-IP+UA "Plausible" daily id need consent or contradict our
  own published promise (C). A minimal JS error beacon is B and waits for the IOD.
- **The legal basis is art. 6(1)(e), not (f).** UW is a public university and art. 6(1)'s last
  sentence probably bars it from legitimate interest; (f) is kept as the fallback analysis. The
  controller is probably Uniwersytet Warszawski, not the Ośrodek. `telemetry/models.py` and the
  policy now say so.

### `analytics` — the 42nd app, and the Analytics tab

- **Server-side only, aggregates only.** A nightly `rollup_analytics` reads every log shard and
  **recounts** a day (house rule 5) into `DailyRouteStat` (route template, audience, 4xx/5xx/429,
  p50/p95), `DailyContentView` (17 page kinds), `DailyReferrer` (host only), `DailyClient` (an
  in-house UA classifier, no dependency; bots apart), `DailyActiveUsers` and `WeeklyCohort` (counts
  only, adults only). No aggregate column holds an IP, a UA string or a user id —
  `test_no_visitor_fingerprint` now asserts it of these tables too. Aggregates are purged at 25 months.
- **`Sec-GPC: 1` / `DNT: 1` is an art. 21 objection.** `RequestLog.analytics_opt_out` (telemetry
  0002) is set from either header and every rollup skips those rows; the security log line is still
  written, and the dashboard says how many requests were left out.
- **Live counts from the main DB**, each one line in a registry: registrations and confirmation rate,
  the contribution funnel, eight moderation queues with median decision time where a timestamp exists,
  community activity, feature usage across 22 models, coverage per branch and per language.
- **`/moderation` → Analytics** is a tab button that navigates to **`/moderation/analytics`**:
  KPI tiles with the previous period, traffic, content, coverage, community, a retention heatmap,
  clients and referrers, health (7 days of raw 5xx with request ids, slowest routes), and "what this
  dashboard does not know, on purpose". Charts are inline SVG — no chart library. Staff only (401/403,
  as the Mail tab). People-counts under 10 read "<10".
- **`deploy/cron/edmat-analytics`**, nightly: rollup THEN `enforce_log_retention`, `&&`-chained.
  **Nothing in the repository had ever scheduled `enforce_log_retention`** — the privacy policy's
  30/90-day promise was not being kept by anything automatic. Run it with `--dry-run` once first.

### `sso` — the 43rd app, sign-in with Google, Apple and Microsoft

- OIDC authorization code + PKCE (S256; not for Apple, which does not document it) + `state` +
  `nonce`; id_token verified against the provider's JWKS (`PyJWT[crypto]`, a new dependency). The
  callback lands on the backend and the browser is redirected to the frontend with a two-minute
  single-use code, **never a token in a URL**. Identities are keyed on (provider, issuer, subject),
  Microsoft's `tid`/`oid` kept and its issuer checked against the tenant template.
- **Never linked by email.** An unknown identity whose email already has an account is refused with
  "sign in with your password and link it in Settings". A new one gets a 30-minute signup ticket and
  `/auth/sso/complete`: username, the same age question — the gate is now one function,
  `accounts/minors.py: self_registration_refusal`, called by both doors — and the terms.
- **Nothing shows without credentials**: a provider is enabled only when configured AND the new
  `social_login` flag (moderation 0054) is on. Settings → "Sign-in methods" links and unlinks, and
  refuses an unlink that would leave no way in. A password-reset mail now reaches an SSO-only
  account, which is how it sets a password. `deploy/SSO-SETUP.md` is the operator runbook (consoles,
  redirect URIs, Apple's Private Email Relay registration for the no-reply address, env vars, secrets
  under `/etc/edmat/`). `e2e/sso-stub.mjs` is a local provider that signs real RS256 tokens; settings
  refuse to start with it on and `DEBUG` off.

### Terms of use, the privacy policy, terms acceptance

- **`/terms` exists for the first time** (`lib/content/terms.ts`, EN + PL, equally authoritative,
  §§ 1–22 against `ANALYTICS-LAW.md` §5: u.ś.u.d.e. art. 8, DSA arts 14–23, the Polish DSA act
  Dz.U. 2026 poz. 1296, consumers, minors, the licence with its fields of exploitation, the
  AI-assisted mark, contests, tutoring and events, complaints, termination, changes). Footer and
  `/legal` link to it.
- **`/privacy` rewritten** (`POLICY_LAST_UPDATED = 2026-10-14`): controller and IOD, a
  purpose → basis → retention table, the full device-storage table, the server log, the statistics,
  sign-in providers as separate controllers, OVH as mail processor, the locale hint's IP→country
  lookup, children, every right. "Nobody outside the Faculty" — no longer true since OVH — is gone.
- **Registration requires `accept_terms`** (refusal code `terms_required`), written through
  `legal/terms.py: record_acceptance` into the append-only `legal.TermsAcceptance` (legal 0002), from
  every door: `register`, `sso:<provider>`, `guardian`. `/api/auth/me/` carries
  `terms_accepted_version`. `CURRENT_TERMS_VERSION` must equal `terms.ts`'s `TERMS_VERSION`.

### A real leak found on the way

**The API token was in the request log.** The notification stream authenticates with `?token=`
(an EventSource cannot send a header), and `redact_query_string` only knew search terms and
`/api/auth/` — so every live-notification connection wrote a full credential down for 90 days. The
dev shards held 4369 such rows. `CREDENTIAL_QUERY_PARAMS` now redacts `token`, `key`, `password` and
friends, and `telemetry.0003_scrub_logged_credentials` cleans the rows already written — it runs per
shard, which is how shards are migrated on deploy anyway.

### Verified

- `manage.py test analytics telemetry` 64 OK; `test sso accounts legal identity mail moderation`
  476 OK; `test legal accounts mail sso` 273 OK; `check`, `makemigrations --check` clean;
  `check_databases_declared.py` 0. The full suite was run once more over the merged tree — see the
  board entry for its result.
- `npm run check` 0/0; eslint clean on touched files; 4965 = 4965 keys.
- Real browser on separate ports per agent (env-var overrides, `frontend/.env` untouched):
  `e2e/analytics.mjs` 28/28, `e2e/sso.mjs` 27/27 against the stub, the register refusal and success
  in both locales, `/terms` `/privacy` `/legal` at 1280 and 390 px — screenshots looked at; that is
  how the 390 px privacy table, the 5xx table and a mislabelled gridline were found and fixed.

### Left open

- **Placeholders the owner must fill before publishing**: the contact e-mail and the IOD UW contact
  (`[… do uzupełnienia]` in terms, privacy and `/legal`); the controller identity and address need IOD
  sign-off; the legal bases need IOD sign-off.
- **Terms § 9 grants CC BY-SA 4.0**, which `LEGAL.md` §2–3 said needed a lawyer first. Cut it back to
  the operating licence if that review has not happened.
- **Promised by the terms, not built**: a mailer for terms-change and closure notices, an in-app
  art. 20 complaint against a moderation decision, an archive of past terms versions, the "please
  accept the new terms" prompt. Accounts older than today have no acceptance row.
- **No retention rule** for `ContentView`/`MaterialView`, the mail records, messages, anonymous-comment
  IP hashes; the door scanner's IndexedDB copy of attendee names survives logout. `sso_purge` has no
  cron line of its own.
- Analytics: zero-result searches (every list view filters `q` itself), real entry referrers (the SPA
  is static — Apache's log would be needed), an account-level "exclude me" switch, decision timestamps
  for five queues.
- SSO: Apple's server-to-server notifications and token revocation, a "set a password" form, GitHub
  (not OIDC). Audit rows reuse `password_change` rather than adding an action.

## 17CK — The owner's answers: students as provider, self-service export and deletion, a licence per item, GitHub and Facebook (2026-10-14, `ux/colour-pass`)

Same day as §17CJ, after the owner answered its questions. Four sub-agents again, plus the text
changes done by the orchestrating session.

### Who runs EdMat — decided twice in one afternoon

First answer: *"Ośrodek Komputerowy Wydziału Fizyki UW"*. An hour later, superseding it: *"It is run on
OKWF UW servers and overseen by them, but is run by students. so the service provider are students,
and OKWF is servers provider"*, then *"Usługodawcą jest grupa studentów Uniwersytetu Warszawskiego"*,
anonymous *"at least for now"*, reached *"through the website or OKWF"*.

- **Provider and GDPR controller: the student group.** The Ośrodek is the hosting provider and, in
  GDPR terms, a processor (art. 28 — no agreement signed yet). IOD UW (`iod@adm.uw.edu.pl`, as on UW's
  own privacy notices) is offered only for the University's servers.
- **The basis therefore moved from art. 6(1)(e) to 6(1)(f)** everywhere — `/privacy` in both locales,
  `telemetry/models.py`, `telemetry/middleware.py`, `analytics/`. `ANALYTICS-LAW.md` §4's (e)
  recommendation assumed a university controller; a student group is not a public authority, so
  art. 6(1)'s last sentence does not bar (f). The paragraph now says why a small student project has
  that interest (spam, abuse, knowing what helps people learn).
- **Contact: the "Zgłoś błąd" issues form** (private unless the reporter publishes it —
  `issues/models.py is_public`) or by post through the Ośrodek. The Dziekanat Studencki is no longer
  named anywhere as a contact point; it never agreed to be one.
- **Known gap, stated in `LEGAL.md` §1:** u.ś.u.d.e. art. 5 expects a natural-person provider to give a
  name and address, and GDPR art. 13(1)(a) the controller's identity. Anonymity is the owner's choice
  for now, not an oversight.

### Self-service data export and account deletion (`accounts/erasure.py`)

- **A registry of 199 rules** — every model that points at a user (or a `Profile`) is `delete`,
  `anonymise`, `keep` (with a reason) or `end` (future bookings, live enrolments — the other side is
  notified). **A completeness test fails on any new FK without a rule**; it caught the licensing app's
  `LicenceChange.changed_by` the afternoon it was added.
- **The `User` row becomes a scrubbed tombstone, not a deleted row.** A real delete cascades through
  other people's halves of conversations and threads, and `Contest.organiser` is PROTECT; a single
  shared "deleted user" breaks per-author unique constraints. Username `deleted-<pk>`, no email, an
  unusable password, display name translated per reader by `client.ts`. Limit, stated: the pk links an
  erased account's anonymised contributions to each other.
- **A 14-day grace**: the account is deactivated at once (tokens revoked, profile withheld), erased by
  `erase_due_accounts`; signing in offers "cancel deletion", and so does the notice mail. Re-auth is
  password + typed username. Owning a course, event, contest, organisation or project others are in
  is a 409 listing them (house rule 6). A guardian's delete of a child goes through the same module.
- **Export**: `GET /api/auth/me/export/`, one JSON built from the same registry (3/day), including
  decrypted messages and the last 90 days of the person's own request-log rows. Uploaded files are
  linked, not zipped.
- **Retention rules that did not exist**: view history 12 months, the mail log and inbox copy 12
  months, an anonymous comment's IP hash blanked at 30 days — `deploy/cron/edmat-retention` (nightly
  erase + retention + `purge_event_data`, hourly `sso_purge`).

### A licence per item (`licensing`, the 44th app)

- Seven keys: `cc0-1.0`, `cc-by-4.0`, `cc-by-sa-4.0`, `cc-by-nc-4.0`, `cc-by-nc-sa-4.0`, `edmat-only`
  (the default — nothing is opened without the author's choice) and `unknown` (never offered to a
  user). Exercise, SolutionEntry, Material and ConceptArticle carry their own; a translation is stamped
  with its parent's at write time; a material project's passes to its material at first publication.
- **Only towards more open**, by the author or staff, refused once somebody else's version is in the
  item; each change a `LicenceChange` row, shown as "since <date>".
- **Migration**: an exercise is `edmat-only` only with a kept `ExerciseSubmission` behind it —
  `submitted_by` alone is not evidence, because `seed_demo_content` credits corpus rows to demo
  accounts. On the dev DB: 742 exercises, all 1483 hints/solutions and 7 materials `unknown`.
- Pickers on `/submit`, `/submit-material`, the solution composer and the concept editor; a licence
  line on every detail page; `?licence=` on two lists; the importer's `licence:` key (default
  `unknown`, re-runs only widen). **Terms § 9 rewritten**: the author keeps copyright, grants the chosen
  licence for that item and, always, the minimal hosting licence with its fields of exploitation.

### Sign-in, round two; analytics, round two

- **GitHub** (OAuth App, PKCE, only the primary *verified* address from `/user/emails`) and
  **Facebook** (Graph, `appsecret_proof`, the address always treated as unverified) — same state,
  single-use codes, never-link-by-email. Microsoft stays, documented as "built, not requested".
  `deploy/SSO-SETUP.md` §0 answers "can Piotr register this himself?" per provider.
  `deploy/APPLE-REQUEST-OKWF.md` is the Polish e-mail asking the Ośrodek about UW's existing Apple
  Developer account (UW already publishes three App Store apps; Apple waives the fee for accredited
  educational institutions).
- **A password form** — `/api/auth/me/password/` and a Password card in Settings: set one without a
  current password if the account has none, change one with it.
- **Analytics**: staff are left out of every people-count (active accounts, cohorts, registrations,
  the funnel), not out of traffic. No per-account opt-out — the owner: the data is needed against spam
  and scams; GPC/DNT still keeps a request out of the *statistics* and never out of the security log.

### Verified

Per agent: `test sso accounts.test_password` 118, `test accounts identity mail legal` 319,
`test accounts.test_erasure` 45, `test licensing exercises materials coauthoring concepts moderation`
678, `test analytics telemetry` 67 — all OK; `e2e/sso.mjs` 40/40, `e2e/account-erasure.mjs` 21/21,
`e2e/licences.mjs` 27/27, `e2e/analytics.mjs` 28/28, screenshots looked at. Integrated: `check`,
`makemigrations --check`, `check_databases_declared` 0; `npm run check` 0/0, 5107 = 5107 keys,
`npm run build` OK. The full suite's result is on the board entry.

### Left open

- **Owner's decisions still waiting**: auto-linking a verified Google address (TBD); the JS error
  beacon (TBD); whether "EdMat only" content stays nameless or goes when its author leaves; whether a
  minor may delete their own account; the tombstone's pk linkage; a DSA notice's contact e-mail after
  its sender leaves; the licence list (no ND) and the default (`edmat-only` vs CC BY-SA); whether a
  staff-pinned corpus solution stays `unknown`; whether to bump `TERMS_VERSION` (§ 9 changed the same
  day the terms were first written, before any were published).
- **Before publishing `/terms` and `/privacy`**: a contact mailbox would still be better than the
  form alone; the art. 28 agreement with the Ośrodek; lawyer/IOD review.
- Facebook's deauthorize and data-deletion callbacks (the instructions URL is used instead); Apple's
  server-to-server notifications. Decks, galleries and sketches carry no licence; no compatibility
  check between licences on a remix. The export does not pack files; there is no "delete everything I
  wrote" option; blockers are checked when deletion is requested, not again at erasure.
- Neither `deploy/cron/edmat-analytics` nor `edmat-retention` is installed by `apply-on-server.sh`;
  each command should be dry-run on webek4 before its cron line goes in.

## 17CL — Round three: confirm-and-link sign-in, a first-party error reporter, CC BY suggested, a choice at deletion (2026-10-14, `ux/colour-pass`)

The owner's third set of answers, the same evening as §17CJ–§17CK. The session building it was cut
off at 20:27 with all five sub-agents mid-verification; a new session found their edits intact,
relaunched each to *finish and verify* rather than restart (each got its predecessor's brief and last
notes), and every one passed on re-run. Lesson kept: a toolchain in a session's `/tmp` scratch dir
dies with the session — Node 24 now lives under `~/.local/opt/`.

### Linking a provider to an existing account — option A (`LINKING-AND-ERRORS.md` §2.4)

Owner: *"lets research whats the correct way to do it (meaning industry standard)"*, then *"yes, go
with A"*. A provider identity EdMat has never seen, carrying an existing account's address, used to
end at `email_in_use`. It now goes to `/auth/sso/link?ticket=…` and **the person proves the account**
— by its password (throttled like login; five failures kill the ticket) or, only if the address is
confirmed, by a mailed single-use link that works in the browser that started. The ticket lives 30
minutes, is stored hashed, and is purged by the hourly `sso_purge`. Minors and guardian-managed
accounts are refused (`minor`) at the callback and again at the proof; two accounts sharing one
address are still `email_in_use`. Every link — from here or from Settings — mails the account.
**Still never linked by e-mail alone**: the address is how the account is *found*, never what
*proves* it. The mail log stores `[[link]]`, not a working link (`mail/` rule).

### A first-party browser error reporter — option B

Owner: *"if we dont have to get a special GDPR cookie like consent and keep being free of these cookie
popups its a green light"*. `POST /api/client-errors/` takes a `text/plain` `sendBeacon` from a
lazily imported reporter (≈1 KB gzipped, not in the entry chunk): kind, message, a path-only stack,
the route *template* (`/exercises/[id]`, never the id), the build id and the locale. No cookie, no
storage, no `Authorization`; GPC/DNT send nothing; at most five per page load, deduplicated. Grouped
on the Analytics dashboard by a normalised message (whole numbers masked — `\b\d+\b`, after an earlier
`\d+` turned `e2e` into `eNe` in a screenshot). Reports kept 30 days, counts and groups 90, purged by
the nightly `rollup_analytics`. Its own flag, `client_errors` (moderation 0055) — **39 flags**.
`ANALYTICS-LAW.md` row 8 and `/privacy` say what is sent. This is technique class A of that file: it
reads nothing from the device that the page did not itself produce, so PKE art. 399 does not apply.

### Licences: CC BY suggested where the work is plainly the author's own

Owner: *"for exercises without a source and materials created from scratch on edmat CC-BY should be
suggested"*. The picker pre-selects CC BY 4.0 with a "Suggested" tag and a reason line when an
exercise names no source (type "other", no name, no source material) and when a material version is
written in the editor with no source URL; naming a source moves it back to "EdMat only" with "may be
somebody else's work", until the author clicks — after that it never moves. **The API default is
still `edmat-only`**: a suggestion is the form's, never the server's. Terms § 9 point 3 no longer calls
"EdMat only" the default. Solutions and hints are not suggested CC BY: the composer has no source
field, so there is no way to tell an author's own answer from a copied key.

### Deleting an account: a choice for EdMat-only content, and minors are guardian-only

Owner: *"user is asked about it"* and *"guardian only"*. The deletion plan counts what the person
wrote under `edmat-only`/`unknown` and asks: keep it, anonymised, or remove it — **hidden**
(`published=False` / `is_removed`), never deleted, so threads under it stay whole. CC-licensed content
stays either way (the licence was irrevocable when granted), and so do co-authored items and
translations. No answer when there is something to answer is 400 `choice_required`. A minor deleting
their own account gets 400 `guardian_managed` and a line telling them to ask their parent or guardian;
the guardian's path answers "remove". `accounts` 0027; privacy (rights, deletion, publication row) and
terms § 19 in both languages.

### And one bug found by the next loop's first package

`/flashcards` told a brand-new account "3 cards waiting across 1 deck" while it owned none.
`flashcards.rules.my_study_decks` counted decks placed on any node the person could **see**, so a
deck on a public course was work waiting for everybody on the site. It now asks `is_node_member`,
which is what its own docstring ("placed where they study") always said; a regression test covers
it, and grading a card in such a deck still makes it yours to finish.

Also this evening: `TERMS_VERSION` and the privacy policy's date bumped to 2026-10-15 (owner: *"its
going to be deployed tomorrow, yes bump"*); `apply-on-server.sh` step 3f backfills the analytics
(`rollup_analytics --days 90`), prints dry runs of everything the first nightly retention will
remove, and installs `/etc/cron.d/edmat-analytics` and `edmat-retention` (owner: *"use cron, and
install them using the apply on server script"*).

### Verified

Per part, on re-run: `sso mail` 151, `analytics` 48 + `analytics.test_client_errors` 17, `licensing`
32, `accounts.test_erasure accounts.test_minors licensing` 100, `flashcards` 66 — all OK;
`e2e/sso.mjs` 45/45, `e2e/client-errors.mjs` 29/29, `e2e/licences.mjs` 36/36,
`e2e/account-erasure.mjs` 28/28, each against a migrated copy of the database, screenshots looked at.
The full suite after the courses merge (§17CM) is on the board entry and in the commit message.

### Left open

- Linking: the page reveals which proofs an account has (a password? a confirmed address?) — the
  price of offering them; a mailed link opened in another browser cannot hand the request across.
- Errors: SvelteKit's `handleError` path is tested at the API only; the reporter cannot know the flag
  until flags load (the server drops reports while it is off).
- Licences: no suggestion on the concept-article editor or the solution/hint composers;
  `/submit-material` cannot tell a file the author wrote from someone else's.
- Deletion: a hidden item can be restored only by staff; `unknown` follows the same choice as
  `edmat-only`; "ask us to remove one item" is text, not a form.

## 17CN — A prototype you can find your way around: empty states with a next step, a place to start, real screens in the showcase and the manual (2026-10-14 night, `ux/colour-pass`)

Owner: *"proceed with the next round/stage after this one's done → keep the loop going. when no tasks
on the horizon improve the prototype: make it more intuitive, and add more placeholders: show-off and
discuss modules - use our screens, and link them for users to be able to check them out by
themselves."* A read-only planning pass surveyed the showcase, the manual, the homepage, the navbar and
every hub's empty state, and cut eight packages; six were built the same night, each on its own branch
and worktree, each merged into `ux/colour-pass` after its own browser run. **None of it is in the
2026-10-15 bundle** — that was frozen first (§17CL/§17CM, branch `deploy/2026-10-15`).

### Where a first-time visitor got lost (the survey)

The homepage pointed nowhere but the content; nothing linked the manual except `/about`. Thirteen hubs
said "Nothing here yet." and offered no next step. The account menu was fourteen flat items, there was
no Help entry anywhere, no showcase page used a single real screenshot, the contests chapter of the
manual had none, and no manual step linked to the screen it described.

### What changed

- **Empty states that offer a next step** (WP1, `ux/empty-states`): one `EmptyState` component on
  thirteen hubs — a sentence saying what the page is for, at most one action (only when the reader can
  use it: creation gate, flag, signed in), and a "How this works →" link to a manual chapter or showcase
  page. "Nothing matches these filters" is a separate state that offers *clear filters*, never *create*.
  It found the flashcards due-list bug (§17CL).
- **A place to start** (WP2): a quiet three-door band under the homepage hero — the 5-minute guide, the
  showcase (`/about#showcase`), "just try it" (`/disciplines`) — prerendered, no service call, dismissal
  read in `onMount` so it can only collapse; a Manual link in the footer. Plus three small fixes the
  empty-states run saw: "New contest" shown to signed-out readers, the concepts Tag select past 390px,
  and `/my-set` flashing its empty state before its items arrived.
- **Real screens in the showcase** (WP3): `ShowcaseDoc` gained `tryIt` and `shots`; `ShowcaseShot` draws
  a screenshot outside the inert sample frame with "Open the real page →", dropped when its feature is
  off; every page has a "Try it yourself" row and its manual chapter. Stale pictures (the course pages,
  the exercise page, the navbar) were deliberately not used — each was compared with the live page
  first.
- **The manual photographs contests and opens its screens** (WP4): eleven contest pictures from three
  contests made through the real API; 25 "Open this screen →" links across all twelve chapters, typed
  as SvelteKit pathnames so a dead route is a `svelte-check` error; the "Not written yet" list made
  honest; the navbar pictures re-shot (one had shipped with its menu never opened).
- **Four new showcase pages** (WP5): `/about/goals-and-work`, `/about/tutoring`, `/about/materials`,
  `/about/conference` — twelve in all — each section a `DiscussableSection`, 13 new pictures in
  `static/showcase/`, each page saying what is *not* built.
- **The account menu in four groups, and Help** (WP8): Learning / Taking part / Working together / Your
  account; a group whose items are all switched off disappears with its heading; "Help & manual" in the
  menu and the drawer; the popover gained the arrow/Home/End keys its `role="menu"` promised.

- **The work dashboard in the reader's language** (WP9): `/work` printed raw codes (`todo`,
  `sole_owner`) and English-only strings built on the server (`3 due`, `1 pending`). Every provider now

  An unknown code reads "Status unknown", never the code. Also: `about-discussions.mjs` brought in line
  with today's `/about`, and plan step rows whose status select fell onto its own line.

- **`/about` tells a newcomer where to go** (WP7; owner, 2026-10-15: *"yes, put the strip above the
  organisation page"*): the homepage's three doors at the top of `/about`, the same `StartHere`

  about the visitor, not the page. Four more feature cards (flashcards, contests, help wanted,
  organisations; 13, each behind its flag) and one "Explore" section holding the manual and the
  showcase index. `about-page.mjs` was already broken by the folded panels and is 58/58 again.
- **Your account, licences and your data** (WP6): `/about/account` (the age gate, a guardian's child,
  sign-in providers — none configured on the dev database, so the page says so and draws no buttons —
  mail and password, export, deletion) and `/about/licences-and-data`, which presents **CC BY 4.0 as
  EdMat's suggestion for your own work** (owner: *"as for license cc-by"*), the other licences as
  facts, and the consent-free statistics and error reports, linking `/terms` and `/privacy` rather than
  restating them. Fourteen showcase pages; `/about/materials` reworded the same night so the two pages

- **Every picture matches the site** (WP10): all 61 manual pictures re-shot against a fresh database

### Bugs found by doing this, and where they went

- **`localizedPath()` wrote the prerenderer's origin into links**: `href="http://sveltekit-prerender/
  korki"` (and, since §17CM, `/materialy`) on 40 prerendered pages, broken until hydration — the Tutoring
  half probably live since 2026-10-01. Fixed, and **taken alone onto `deploy/2026-10-15`**, whose bundle
  was rebuilt.
- **`/contests/new` died on screen 3** for anyone who kept the pre-selected kind (the default never went
  through `applyPreset`). Also taken onto the deploy branch.

  waits and names the two boot requests and the one discussion-policy request it allows.

  worktree elsewhere; it is now the symlink's real path.

  server serves `/en/…` and loses `/korki` until it restarts. Production builds are unaffected.
- `pack.sh` named a bundle packed at 22:00 after the day, and overwrote the bundle applied that evening.
  It now refuses to overwrite one; `EDMAT_PACK_DATE` names one for another day.

## 17CO — "Pytaj" gets a destination: ask a question in a tag (2026-10-15, WP15, `ux/wp15-ask`)

The hero has said "Ucz się, ćwicz i **pytaj**" for weeks and nothing on the site answered the third
verb — the first-visitor audit's finding 16 and its owner question 1. The owner's answer, verbatim:
**"ask as ppl should be allowed to post in tags"**. So asking is posting into a tag, and this is the
smallest honest version of that.

### What changed

- **A question is a post anchored to a tag** — the same `POST /api/posts/`, throttle, `posts` kill
  switch, minors hold, report button, tombstone and `community.Comment` reply thread every post
  already had. **No `kind`/"is a question" field**: the owner's words are satisfied by "a post in a
  tag", a second kind would be a filter nobody asked for and one more thing to keep consistent, and
  the framing (the composer asks for a question; the tag page says "Pytania w tym tagu") does the
  rest. If questions ever need to be told apart from statements (an "answered" mark, say), that is
  the day for a field.
- **`GET /api/posts/?tag=<slug>`** (`PostViewSet.list`) — one tag's visible posts, newest first,
  id-cursor, ≤ 50. It reads the Post table rather than the feed, because the feed trims itself at 90
  days and a question must not fall off its own tag (a test pins exactly that). Tombstoned,
  auto-hidden and held posts are left out; the content-language rule applies with the usual header;
  the audience band deliberately does not, as on the feed. Reply counts are one grouped COUNT.
- **`/ask`** — the composer framed as a question (`AskComposer`): the question, a **searchable tag
  picker** (`TagPicker`, existing tags only; both the query and the tags are folded — lower case,
  diacritics off, spaces to hyphens — because most tags are ASCII slugs and some are not, "całka z
  1-formy"), the audience band (required, as on every submit form), the language. No anchor choice,
  no reference, no picture: a general post still lives on `/activity`. `?tag=` preselects. A signed-out
  reader gets "Zaloguj się, żeby zadać pytanie"; a minor's question comes back held and the page says
  a moderator will look first, instead of "published".
- **`/tags/[slug]`** — a tag finally has a page: `#tag`, "Zadaj pytanie w tym tagu" (the same composer,
  inline), Obserwuj/Przestań obserwować, a link to the tag-filtered feed for everything else, and the
  questions with their threads ("Dyskusja (n)"), load-more, an empty state with the ask action, and
  the hidden-languages notice. No request leaves the page until the flags are loaded and `posts` is on.
- **Every way in** (house rule 3, all behind `posts` with the moderator bypass): the hero's "Zadaj
  pytanie" beside "Przeglądaj dziedziny"; "Zadaj pytanie" first in the Add… menu's Content group;
  the tag chip's menu item, which now opens the tag page ("Pytania w tym tagu", previously "Wpisy z
  tym tagiem" → the filtered feed); a post's `#tag` anchor chip. With `posts` off a non-staff account
  sees none of them and both pages say the feature is unavailable (asserted, `e2e/ask.mjs`).
- 32 `ask_*` keys in both catalogues.

### Owner decision, answered by default — please confirm

**May people create a NEW tag when asking? Not in this version: existing tags only.** A tag is global,
free-form and already the one ungated label on the site (`exercises.Tag`'s own comment names the slur
risk); a question box that minted tags would be a second, busier way to put one on every chip. New
tags keep arriving the way they always have — with a submitted exercise (moderated) or a concept
article — and the picker's "no match" line says exactly that. There is no "suggest a tag" queue to
point at; if the owner wants one, it is a small moderation item (a pending `Tag` row the queue can
approve), not a change to asking.

### Verified

`manage.py test activity` (35, eight new), `check`, `makemigrations --check`,
`check_databases_declared` (0); `npm run check` 0/0, eslint and prettier on every touched file,
`check:plain`, `PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL=/api npm run build`; `e2e/ask.mjs` **59/59** on a DB copy (both
languages, 390 and 1280, dark theme, a reply, the minor's hold, the switch). Screens looked at: the hero
(pl/en, 390/1280), the composer (pl/en, 390/1280, the picker mid-search in dark at 390), the tag page
(pl/en, 390/1280, dark at 1280), the held message.

### Left open

- **Followers are not notified of a new question** — they see it in the feed's Followed view, but
  `notify_tag_followers` fires for tagged exercises and materials, not posts. One call in
  `PostViewSet.create` (after the hold check) would do it; left out because a notification per post
  on a busy tag is a volume decision for the owner.
- No "answered" state, no accepting an answer, no sorting by unanswered — see "no field" above.
- No tag index (`/tags`), and the tag page does not list the tag's exercises (there is no
  exercise-by-tag browse page to link; the chip's "save for later" is the nearest thing).
- The audit's other half of finding 16 — renaming "Szukamy pomocy" in the bar — is not this
  package's (Header structure was out of scope).
- A minor's held question is not visible to its author on the tag page (the list leaves held rows
  out for everybody); the `/ask` page says it was held, and that is the only place.

**Creating a tag while asking** (WP16, the same day; owner: *"tag creation is a must"*): the picker
offers "Utwórz tag „…”" when nothing matches, and the tag is made with the question in one place,
`exercises/tags.py: create_tag_from`. A name that folds (case, Polish letters) to an existing tag reuses
it; signed-in adults only (a minor reuses but does not create), 5 new tags an hour; a tag made by a
question is listed only while something visible uses it, so a withdrawn or hidden question leaves no
public orphan; staff rename, remove or merge in the Django admin. `exercises` 0016 adds `created_by`,
`created_at`, `from_question` to `Tag`, and the erasure registry's completeness test caught the new FK
the same hour (anonymise). `e2e/ask.mjs` 92/92; full suite 3488, the one failure that rule.
**Left open:** posting itself is not rate-limited — the `post_create` scope is set on a viewset with no
`throttle_scope`, so DRF never counts it (`community/views.py: _DiscussionThrottle` has the same shape).

## 17CP — Polish time: `TIME_ZONE = 'Europe/Warsaw'`, and the code that had assumed UTC (2026-10-15, `ux/tz-warsaw`)

Owner, 2026-10-15, on the WP11 bug above: *"stays poland"*. The bug was live on edmat.net: with
`TIME_ZONE = 'UTC'`, a tutor's weekly rule "14:00" became 14:00 UTC, and the browser drew the slot in
Polish time — so every reader in Poland was offered 16:00 (summer) or 15:00 (winter) for hours the
tutor's own list called 14:00. Goes into the 2026-10-15 deploy (`deploy/UPDATE-2026-10-15.md`,
*Polish time*, says what moves on production and what does not).

### What reads `TIME_ZONE`, and what each one now does

- **Booking** (`booking/availability.py`). A rule's clock time is Polish time. `_aware` is the one place
  a wall-clock time becomes an instant, and it now returns **UTC** — because Python adds a
  `timedelta` to a zoneinfo-aware datetime on its wall clock, and compares/subtracts two datetimes that
  share one tzinfo on the wall clock too. Left Warsaw-zoned, the slicing cursor would have offered two
  "sessions" at one instant on the March night and lost an hour on the October one. The two
  availability endpoints write instants back in Polish time (`views._local_iso`: `14:00+02:00`).
- **Every API datetime** now leaves DRF at the Polish offset (`+02:00`/`+01:00`) instead of `Z`. Same
  instants; the SPA's few `startsAt.slice(0, 10)` calls (the tutor calendar's day buckets, an event's
  clash check) now get the POLISH date — which is what they had always meant, and what they got wrong
  for a booking between midnight and 02:00.
- **Shifts** (`shifts/rules.py`): a minor's night 22:00–06:00 (Kodeks pracy art. 203) and the daily cap
  on the Polish clock; day and night bounds are UTC instants (`_at`), so a 25-hour October day
  measures 25.
- **Flashcards** (`flashcards/rules.py`): "due today" turns at Polish midnight, not 01:00/02:00.
- **Analytics**: the code hard-coded UTC in eleven places (`tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc`, `.astimezone(dt.timezone.utc).date()`), so it would have kept
  counting UTC days while `TruncWeek` (which follows the setting) moved — two zones in one dashboard.
  Now `rollup.day_bounds` gives a date's two Polish midnights and the rollup, `Period`, the browser-error
  counts, the cohorts and `live.week_starts` all use it (`week_starts` was a real catch: `.date()` of a
  Monday's 22:00-UTC bound is Sunday).
- **Seeds**: the persona sandbox now starts at 09:00 Polish time (it read 11:00 in a Warsaw browser);
  the demo conference already used `DEMO_TZ = Europe/Warsaw` and does not move; `seed_edmat_project`'s
  fixed deadlines become 23:59 Polish (were 01:59 the next day in Poland) on its next run.
- `/about/tutoring`, the manual's tutoring chapter and `/about/flashcards` now say the fixed state in
  both languages; `e2e/wp11-fixes.mjs` asserts the new sentence and the absence of "UTC".

### Verified

- New tests: `booking.test_week_schedules.TimeZoneTests` (summer 14:00 = 12:00 UTC, winter = 13:00, the
  March night offers two real hours, the October night four distinct instants, an all-day block covers
  all 25 hours, the endpoint's `14:00+0X:00` round-trips into a booking, and one test that IS about UTC:
  under `override_settings(TIME_ZONE='UTC')` the same rule is 14:00 UTC, so nothing names Warsaw),
  `shifts.tests.TimeZoneTests`, `analytics.tests.PolishDayTests`, `flashcards.tests.DueDayTests`.
- `e2e/booking.mjs` gained the proof (and English contexts — it had been failing on the Polish default
  since 2026-09-23): the API's first slot is `T14:00:00+02:00`, and a browser in `TZ=Europe/Warsaw` draws
  it as **14:00**, the hour on the tutor's "Weekly hours" list — 54/54. Under `TZ=UTC`, 53/53 and the
  slot reads **12:00**; in London it reads 13:00.

### Left open

- **Still no per-account time zone.** A reader abroad sees instants on their own clock, which is
  right for a student booking from London; a TUTOR living abroad publishes hours in Polish time and sees
  their own band drawn at their local equivalent beside a rule list that says 14:00 — the inverse of
  the old bug, for a much smaller group.
- Notification notes written before the switch keep their UTC clock time ("2026-10-20 14:00" meaning
  14:00 UTC); model `__str__`s (admin titles) still format the stored UTC value.
- About a dozen frontend sites sort API datetimes as STRINGS (`createdAt.localeCompare`, the rota's
  `startsAt <`). With every string at one offset (`Z`) that was exact; with `+02:00`/`+01:00` it is
  wall-clock order, which is wrong only inside the hour the October night repeats. Not worth a change
  today; comparing `Date` values would close it.
- Nobody tells tutors or students that the slots moved two hours earlier, or that requests made before
  today were offered at the wrong hour. An owner decision whether to.
- The manual's `04-requested.png` shows slots 18:00–20:00 from an unknown rule; it may have been shot
  under the old clock. Re-shoot with the next manual pass.

## 17CQ — What the first live dashboard showed: an import read as community activity, a slow plans list, a "worst day" that read as a slow route (2026-10-15, `fix/analytics-after-deploy`)

The 2026-10-15 deploy's step 3f ran the 90-day analytics backfill BEFORE step 4's permission fix, so
it died on "attempt to write a readonly database" (paczka2's step 3d had died the same way the day
before). The owner ran it by hand afterwards and sent two screenshots of `/moderation/analytics`. The
script now runs it as step 4a, after the fix; `pack.sh` no longer packs an import kit that carries an
`IMPORTED` marker, and step 7 skips one (`deploy/UPDATE-2026-10-15.md`). Then, from the screenshots:

### An import is not a submission

"Submissions 642, previous 7 days: 0" was exactly paczka2: 214 rows in the translations queue and 428
in the hints-and-solutions queue, and the community table counted the 428 again. Neither queue had
received anything. `import_exercises` writes each exercise's own-language text row and its pinned,
unreviewed hint and solution; the queue counted every row created in the period.

- **Translations queue**: what came in is a row in a language other than the exercise's own — the
  rule the community counter already had (`_not_original`), now applied to the queue's `submitted`.
- **Hints and solutions**: `exercises/entries.py: came_with_exercise()` names the entries that are part
  of their exercise — no author (the corpus), pinned and never reviewed (an import, and the
  2026-08-27 migration out of the old columns, whenever the exercise was made), or written within 60
  seconds of the exercise (an approved submission's fast path). `analytics/live.py` excludes them from
  the queue's `submitted`, the community activity count and the contribution funnel. It lives in the
  entries module because it is a fact about entries; the dashboard asks.
- Pinned by `analytics.tests.ArrivedWithTheExerciseTests` (an import-shaped pair, a fast-path founding
  entry, one later hint and one translation → 1 and 1, and the KPI says 2).

### The plans list: 518 queries for 18 plans

`/api/nodes/:kind/:pk/plans/` had a median of 879 ms on production (71 requests in a week — it is the
`/about` page's roadmaps). The view prefetched steps, sub-steps and their text, and the serializer
threw all of it away: `plan.steps.filter(parent__isnull=True).order_by(…)` and
`step.substeps.all().order_by(…)` are new querysets, and `rules.progress` ran `values_list` per plan.
On the dev copy of EdMat's organisation (18 plans, ~165 steps): **518 queries → 9**, 479 ms → ~110–170
ms. The serializer now filters and sorts the prefetched rows in Python; `progress` counts prefetched
steps when it has them; the view also prefetches `node` and selects `created_by__profile`, `goal` and
each step's `done_by__profile`. The tasks board had the same shape (`.prefetch_related()` chained on
`obj.subtasks.all()`, two COUNTs per card for progress): **92 → 20** queries. Both responses were
compared byte for byte against the old code, anonymous and as a superuser: identical.

### "95th, worst day" → "95th, typical day"

The busiest-routes table showed each route's worst single day's 95th percentile. On production five
routes that answer in 9–75 ms all read about 1.1–1.2 s — one moment (most likely the Apache restart),
not five slow routes. `TrafficView` now also sends `p95_ms`, the request-weighted mean of the daily
95ths (the median column's own method); the table leads with it and names the worst day under it only
when that day was more than twice as slow AND at least 500 ms.

### Chart dates at an even stride

Five evenly spread positions rounded onto seven days labelled 9, 11, 12, 14 and 15 Oct.
`TimeSeriesChart`'s labels now step back from the last day at a whole-number stride, in whole weeks
past fourteen days (7 days: every other day; 30: weekly, every label the same weekday).

### Demonstration accounts are not people

"176 registrations, 34 accounts": the owner confirmed the ~165 accounts made in the week of 21 Sep
are the demo conference's seeded attendees (`seed_conference_demo`, 2026-09-25). They had filled the
registrations, a cohort of 165 at 0 % and a funnel of 176 with nobody contributing. Every demo seeder
gives its accounts an `@edmat.example` address — a reserved domain, so nobody who registered can
hold one (`testing/personas.py` already called it "the only thing that marks them").
`analytics/rollup.py: without_demo` leaves out those accounts and a pupil whose guardian holds one
(a seeded pupil has no address of its own); `counted_people` (active accounts, cohorts and their
sizes) and `live.accounts` / `live.contribution_funnel` use it. Like staff, their requests still
count as traffic. The cohort note and the "what this panel does not know" list say so in both
languages. The stored aggregates (active accounts, cohorts) change only when re-rolled: after
deploying, `rollup_analytics --days 90` once. Pinned by
`RollupTests.test_demo_accounts_are_not_people_but_their_requests_count` (`manage.py test analytics`: 55
OK). On the dev copy 45 of 91 accounts are demonstration accounts.

### Verified

- `manage.py test analytics plans tasks translations goals exercises work accounts.test_erasure
  --parallel 4`: 453 OK. `check`, `makemigrations --check`, `check_databases_declared`: clean.
- Plans and tasks responses diffed against the old code (`/api/nodes/organization/3/{plans,tasks}/`,
  an event's plans, anonymous and as superuser): byte-identical.
- `npm run check` 0/0, keys 5386 = 5386. `e2e/analytics.mjs` 28/28 against the dev copy after a
  30-day rollup; the screenshot shows weekly date labels (17 Sep … 15 Oct) and "95th, typical day"
  with a worst day only under the routes where it stands out. `/about` in a browser: all 18 roadmaps
  with their progress and next step, no page error.
- **`e2e/plans.mjs` FAILS — with the old code too** (stashed and re-run): it waits for

### Left open

- **Demo content still counts as USE.** The demo conference's 149 registrations and its events sit
  in the feature-usage table ("Zapisy na wydarzenia 149"); those are rows, not people, and leaving

  without review and then pinned by staff is read as part of its exercise. A `SolutionEntry.origin`

## §17CS — Courses inside courses, outside content in a programme, and a board on every course (2026-10-21)

Owner: *"make it so that courses can have their own courses (subcourses). incorporated in the ui and
having parent-child relationship. besides we want external courses (from edmat itself or as a link)
to be able to be linked to course's content. also lets have some sort of discussion board (maybe lets
utilize current portal's tags page for that) for poeple to be able to post pdfs, imgs, notes, comments
(with our builders), links, etc, and link and be linked to specific courses/subcourses."* Three
things, each built on a shape that already existed rather than beside it.

**1. The course tree (`courses/rules.py`, the tree section; no migration).** `Course.parent` existed
since §17CK as a one-level "university version of a general course". It is now the course this one is
PART OF, any depth to `MAX_COURSE_DEPTH` (4), and the relation is READ from the two rows
(`relation_to_parent`): a `university` child of a `topic` parent is still a *version*; anything else
with a parent is a *subcourse*. Nothing is stored for it, so every older row keeps its meaning. The
refusal words changed with the shape — `parent_is_subcourse`, `parent_not_general`, `has_subcourses`
and `parent_fixed` are gone; `parent_is_descendant` (a loop), `not_parent_staff` and `too_deep` came —
and **who may add a child differs by relation, which is the reason to tell them apart at all**: a
version by anybody who can see the general course (§17CK's decision, kept), a subcourse only by somebody
who curates the parent, because "weeks 1–7 are Analiza 1" is a statement about the parent. The parent
may now be MOVED by the child's administrator (the §17CK "left open"), through the same refusals, and
`placing` keeps a visibility-only PATCH from being refused as a placement. The serializer carries
`parent_relation`, a `kind` on `parent_summary`, and `ancestors` root-first, cut at the first course
the viewer may not open — which is the breadcrumb. `descendant_ids` walks a subtree one query per
level; the materials index now gathers the whole subtree. A school still may not run a course in the
tree, with `course_is_subcourse` as its own word.

**2. Three more item kinds (`courses` 0022).** `CourseItem` takes `linked_course` (another EdMat
course the curator can see, not this one; a participant who cannot see it is not shown the pointer),
`link_url` + `link_title` (an address outside EdMat, http(s) only — the one target that is a text
column, which is why the exactly-one check constraint is now BUILT from `ITEM_TARGET_COLUMNS` instead
of eight hand-written branches) and `post` (a board post, filed into the week it answers; leaves with
its tombstone the way a removed thread does). `LinkedContentEditor` offers all three; a `link` row opens
in a new tab.

**3. The board (no new table).** "Utilize the tags page" was taken literally: a board post IS an
`activity.Post` — the thing the tag page lists and `/ask` writes — with its existing `ref_course` set.
`GET /api/posts/?course=<id>` lists the posts about a course AND its subcourses (each row naming which),
404 for a course the caller may not see; `/ask?course=<id>` sets the reference and lands back on the
Board tab; the course page's Board tab (`CourseBoard.svelte`, behind `posts`) is a view of the same
posts, so a question still lives in its tag where the people who follow it see it. PDFs, pictures,
notes and links are `attachments/` rows with a new `post` target kind — the comment's shape (no node,
the public tier only, the author attaches) with the post's own visibility — offered on the ask form
(uploaded after the post exists; a failure is said, never swallowed) and on `/posts/[id]`. The post
serializer carries `attachment_count` (one grouped COUNT per page) so a board row says it carries a
PDF before it is opened. "Comments with our builders" were already there: `RichEditor` is the ask
form's body and the reply thread's.

**Not built, said here:** a course picker (the move field and the content editor take a pasted
address or id, as every other link field here does); a tree-wide hub view (the hub lists roots; the
tree reads one level per page); the read-time visibility filter still looks one level up (a
grandparent narrowed after the fact hides the parent, not the grandchild); the attachments panel on
`PostCard` in a list (the count links to the post's page); a subcourse's board does not fold its
parent's posts in (the parent's does its children's); sketch and chem attachments still have no picker.

**Also that afternoon (owner: "change the api of local edmat to 0.0.0.0"):** `run.sh` takes
`BACKEND_HOST`; `0.0.0.0` binds both halves to every interface, writes the machine's first address
into `frontend/.env` as the API base and adds that origin to CORS, and `settings.py` reads a new
`EDMAT_DEV_HOSTS` under DEBUG only — a separate variable from the production `DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS`,
so the half-applied-production guard keeps its meaning. Checked by a request addressed by the LAN IP.

**Verified:** backend `manage.py test courses.test_subcourses courses.test_kind
courses.test_content_links courses.test_school_mode activity attachments organizations --parallel 4
--keepdb` → 293 OK (two earlier runs found that a visibility-only PATCH on a subcourse whose parent
the administrator cannot see was refused as `parent_not_found` — the `placing` split is the fix —

`testing/check_databases_declared.py` clean. Frontend: `npm run check` 0 errors / 0 warnings, eslint

## §17CU — Four things the owner asked for in one afternoon (2026-10-21, after the second bundle)

**1. CC BY-SA 4.0 on everything posted** (*"i want to add CC BY-SA 4.0 to all currently posted
content"*). `manage.py relicense_content --to cc-by-sa-4.0 --by <staff> --note "<basis>"`
(`licensing/management/commands/`) walks every posted exercise, hint/solution, material and concept
article and calls `rules.change_licence` on each — the same function the item page's control
calls, so it adds no authority. On a copy of the dev database: 742 exercises, 1483 entries and 7
materials moved out of `unknown`; 4 exercises already CC BY left alone; 4 exercises, 15 materials
and 15 concept articles REFUSED with `licence_other_contributors`, because they are other people's
`edmat-only` work and `/terms` § 9 point 2 never gave the operator the right to grant the world a
licence on them — those authors widen it themselves, or a CLA comes first (LEGAL.md §2, §3 item 4).
The one thing the command cannot do is make the corpus's rights clear: moving it out of `unknown` is
a statement that they were, and the `--note` on every `LicenceChange` row is where the basis is
written. The owner runs it on the server with their own note (bundle `-c`, step 9). 3 tests.

**2. An Edit option for the author and staff** (*"even though im a superadmin and author of a
specific exercise, there's no edit option based on submit subpage: and there should"*). Until now
the only change path for a published exercise was a suggestion into the moderation queue — right
for a stranger, absurd for the author. `exercises/editing.py` is the rule (author or staff;
`exercise_not_editor` otherwise), `PATCH /api/exercises/{id}/` the write: title/statement/answer
onto the original-locale translation with each text change recorded as an APPROVED `EditSuggestion`
by the editor (so the history reads the same whichever path a change took), difficulty, audience,
topics (branch-checked), tags and the source straight onto the row. The detail carries `can_edit`.
Frontend: `/exercises/[id]/edit` mirrors the submit form field for field (rich editors with the
insert strips, topic chips, source fields), the exercise page shows **Edit** instead of "Suggest an
edit" to an editor, and `/submit/mine` offers Edit on every approved row — the "submit subpage" the
owner named. Found on the way and closed in the same change: `ExerciseViewSet` was a `ModelViewSet`
with `IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly` and no write guard, so **any signed-in account could PATCH
`difficulty` (or `published`) on any exercise** — confirmed with a stranger's token against the dev
server before the fix (200, and the row changed). PUT and DELETE are gone, PATCH asks the rule.
5 backend tests; `e2e/exercise-edit.mjs` 20/20 with screenshots looked at.

**3. AI-assisted, and not verified** (*"as for the content created by me (user todoonet) mark it
as ai assisted and remove the verified solution"*). Two pieces. `manage.py declare_ai_assisted
--author todoonet` makes the author's own `AuthorMark` on every exercise and every hint/solution
that account wrote, through the same table the page's control writes. And one rule change in
`recount_verified`: a solution its author declared AI-assisted no longer makes the exercise
verified on the strength of a pin or the author's contributor tier — only a reviewer's accept does.
A pin and a tier both say "a person stands behind this"; the disclosure says they do not fully.
`provenance/signals.py` recounts on every mark. On the server (bundle `-c`, step 9) the 64 imported
exercises lose their "verified solution" chip the moment the marks land. 2 tests.

**4. Sub-exercises** (*"analyze exercises that are small sets of exercises … let's design a way"*).
Designed, not built: `SUBEXERCISES-BRIEF.md` — `ExercisePart` + a translation table for its text,
`SolutionEntry.part` (null = the whole exercise, which is how a hint can be statement- or
part-specific), `verified` covering the whole OR every part, labelled sections in the import
format, a Parts editor on the new edit page, and 964's siblings regenerated from their sources
rather than cut by a regex. The build order is in the brief.

### Left open

- The author's own unpublished exercise is still edited through the queue (`PATCH` 404s on the
  public queryset).
- `relicense_content` does not touch a translation somebody else wrote (by design) and does not
  notify the refused authors that they could widen their own — a notification type is its own change.
- The AI-assisted mark is not in the import format; a `paczka` written with an assistant has to be
  marked after import with the command.

## 17CV.A Sub-exercises, step A — the rules and the writes (2026-10-21, `parts/a-backend`)

The prep commit made parts readable (`ExercisePart`, `ExercisePartTranslation`, `SolutionEntry.part`,
`EditSuggestion.part`, `parts` on the detail, `part` on an entry POST). This step made them REAL on
the write side and in every derived rule, so that C's page and B's importer have a backend that
keeps its promises. Brief: `prompts/20-parts-a-backend.md`; design: `SUBEXERCISES-BRIEF.md`.

**1. `verified` for a set.** `exercises/signals.py` now has `passed_solutions(exercise_id)` — the ONE
definition of "passed" (pinned, reviewed or verified-authored; AI-assisted only once reviewed) — and
`recount_verified` asks two questions of it: a passed solution with `part IS NULL`, or
`parts.verified_by_parts` (the exercise has parts and EVERY one has a passed solution of its own).
(a)–(c) solved and (d) not is unverified. `ExercisePart` post_save (on create) and post_delete
recount: a part added to a verified set unverifies it until solved; deleting the unsolved part may
verify it. For an exercise without parts nothing changed (a part-entry cannot exist without a part —
CASCADE). `verified` is now also read-only in the Django admin (admin rule 1; it was editable).

**2. Licence.** A part has no licence column, by design, and needs none: it is the exercise's text,
covered by `Exercise.licence` the moment that moves. `_carry_to_own_text` carries nothing more; its
docstring says why. `licensing/test_parts.py` runs the endpoint and `relicense_content` over
exercises with parts. No column was added; the one day it would be needed is named below.

**3. `PATCH /api/exercises/{id}/` takes `parts`.** `ExercisePartEditSerializer` (`id?`, `label` ≤ 20,
`statement` required, `answer` may be blank) under `ExerciseEditSerializer.parts`; the rule is
`parts.parts_payload_refusal` + `parts.apply_parts`, in the same transaction as the rest of the edit.
The list is the whole set: absent leaves parts alone, no `id` creates, a known `id` updates label and
text, a known part left out is deleted with its entries and edit suggestions (CASCADE), `[]` deletes
all, `order` = position (1-based; survivors are parked above the highest order first so a swap never
trips `(exercise, order)`). Text lands on the part's original-locale published row; each changed field
(a new part's statement and non-blank answer included) is an approved `EditSuggestion` with `part`,
by the editor. Resending the same list records nothing. Refusals: `part_not_of_exercise`,
`part_label_duplicate`, `parts_too_many` (> 26), and one the brief did not name, `part_id_duplicate`
(the same id twice — the form cannot send it, a hand-built body can, and no listed word was true of it).

**4. `POST /api/edit-suggestions/` takes `part`.** `part_and_entry`, `part_not_of_exercise`,
`part_field_invalid` (a part has no title); the locale must still be one the exercise speaks. Decided in
the queue like a shared-statement suggestion (the entry decide path still refuses anything without an
entry). Applying writes the part's row for `locale` through `parts.write_part_text`; a missing row is
created as a COPY of the fallback text the reader already saw with the one field changed — otherwise
a suggested English answer would leave an English reader an empty statement where a Polish one stood.
The serializer shows `part` and `part_label`; the queue `select_related('part')`.

**5. Entries.** An entry PATCH with a DIFFERENT `part` is **refused** 400 `part_immutable` (chosen over
ignoring: a client that tries learns it failed); the part it already has is a no-op. Visibility and
ordering (`entries.py`) untouched and tested.

**6. Admin.** `ExercisePart` page with its translations inline; parts inline on the exercise;
`SolutionEntry.part` and every `EditSuggestion` FK `raw_id_fields`. The detail now prefetches
`parts__translations` (two queries, not one per part).

**7. The KaTeX sweep sees parts** (B's board item): `dump_text_fields` emits every
`ExercisePartTranslation` as an `exercise` row (empty title), so `npm run check:katex` covers part
statements and answers without the hand-appending B's rehearsal needed. `parts.MAX_PARTS` (26) is
where the importer can read the same limit the edit form is held to (B's other board item — the
importer is B's file, so it is not wired here).

### Left open

## 17CV.B — The importer's part sections, and paczka4: fifteen paczka3 sets rewritten with parts (2026-10-21, `parts/b-import`)

Step B of `SUBEXERCISES-BRIEF.md` §6 (brief `prompts/21-parts-b-import.md`). Two halves: the import
format learns parts, and the set-shaped files of `paczka3` are rewritten by hand with them.

**The format.** `## Podpunkt <label>` / `## Part <label>` (any case; the label is the trimmed free
text after the keyword, ≤ 20 characters, shown as written) opens a part, and every section after it
— `## Treść` (required), `## Wskazówka`, `## Odpowiedź`, `## Rozwiązanie` — belongs to that part
until the next part heading. Whole-exercise sections come first; the shared `## Treść` is still
required. Refused, each with its reason and filename: no label, a label over 20, two parts with one
label, a part without a statement (or an empty one), unbalanced maths in any part text, text straight
under a part heading (it would have been dropped), and **a section named twice in one scope** — which
is how "a whole-exercise section after the parts" shows up once every section after a part heading
is that part's; none of the 1,974 corpus files names a section twice, so that refuses nothing that
used to import.

**The apply.** Parts by `(exercise, order)`; the text as the published `ExercisePartTranslation` in
the file's locale; each part's hint and solution as pinned published entries with `part=`. The whole
exercise's own pinned upsert gained `part=None` in its key — without it a part's pinned solution is
indistinguishable from the whole's and gets overwritten (or, with two parts solved, the second run
raises `MultipleObjectsReturned`); a test removes `part=None` and fails. For a file WITH parts the
file is the truth: parts beyond its count are deleted with their entries (named per file), and — a
rule the brief did not have, found by rehearsing 964 — a pinned entry an earlier import wrote with
the same `--author` for a section the file no longer has (the whole exercise's or a part's) is
deleted too. Without it, re-importing 964 with parts left the old one-solution-for-all-four standing
beside the four new part solutions, and the old combined hint beside the split ones. It touches
nothing somebody else wrote (staff may pin a reader's solution) and nothing readers have commented
on or voted on (house rule 12) — both are left with a warning. A file without parts leaves parts
alone. `parts: N created, M updated, K removed.` is printed on every run and counts CHANGES (compared
against the sanitized file text), so an unchanged re-run prints zeros and does not even re-save an
entry. `_relicense` already moved every pinned entry; a test pins that part entries move with it.

**paczka4.** Read all 64 files: **15 are set-shaped**, not the 23 the design guessed — algebra 0005
(964), 0006, 0011, 0022, 0023; fale 0001, 0004, 0005, 0006, 0009, 0019, 0026, 0029, 0031, 0034 (43
parts). Labels follow the sheets: `1`–`4` for algebra s1/5 and s1/6 (unlabelled on the sheet; the
solutions numbered them), `a`–`d` everywhere else (the sheets' (a)/a)). Not rewritten on purpose:
algebra s2/4a–4j and 1a–2b, which paczka3 had already made separate exercises, and physics problems
that ask several things in one sentence without an enumeration. Each file rewritten by reading it:
the shared statement keeps the lead sentence, hints go to the part they are about (964: "square
first" → 2, the conjugate → 3 and 4), a derivation every part stands on stays the whole exercise's
solution (fale 0001, 0019, 0026; algebra 0022), a one-line convention ("Oś y w dół…") is repeated in
each part that uses it rather than becoming a fake whole-exercise "solution". Every math segment and
prose fragment of each old file was searched for in the new one; the only misses are combined
displays cut into parts and sentences split per part. What was ADDED is listed in the kit README
(one lead sentence for fale 0005, whose sheet has none; short "(podpunkt a)" cross-references).
The same 15 files are written into the owner's presentations repo
(`presentations/algebra/edmat/algebra/zadania/`, `presentations/fizyka_3/edmat/fale/zadania/`; that
directory is not a git repository, nothing else there touched). `preflight.py` now checks the
exercises EXIST with the same titles and that the API has `parts`; `PRODUCTION.md` is the same
command as paczka3 and says the kit must land AFTER A and C are deployed — with the backend but not
the page, 964 would show only "Przedstawić w postaci a+bi następujące liczby zespolone:".

### Verified

- `manage.py test exercises.test_import_parts` — **27 tests OK** (13 parser, 14 apply), and with the
  existing `ImportExercisesCommandTests` 40 OK; the mutation (drop `part=None` from the key) fails one.
- `manage.py test exercises --parallel 4 --keepdb` — **182 tests OK** (30 s of tests; ~10 min with the ten in-memory DBs built).
- `manage.py check` clean; `makemigrations --check --dry-run` "No changes detected";
  `testing/check_databases_declared.py` 0.
- Rehearsal on a COPY of the worktree database, rebuilt as production is (fale "Waves", `algebra` via
  `create_algebra_branch.py`, `todoonet`, paczka3 imported: 23/46/5 and 41/82/8 as on the server):
  `--dry-run` and the real run both **algebra 0 created, 5 updated, 26 hint/solution; parts 17
  created, 0 updated, 0 removed; 5 stale pinned removed — fale 0 created, 10 updated, 48; parts 26
  created; 13 stale removed**; the second run **parts: 0 created, 0 updated, 0 removed** for both;
  the kit files byte-identical after (no write-back); 64/64 verified.
- `dump_text_fields` on the copy + the 43 part rows appended (see Left open) + `npm run check:katex`:
  **2537 rows, 0 issues** (2494 without the part rows).

### Left open

## 17CV.C — Sub-exercises, the page: part blocks, "For:" on the composer, the part on "Suggest an edit", the Parts editor (2026-10-21, `parts/c-page`)

Step C of `SUBEXERCISES-BRIEF.md` (brief `prompts/22-parts-c-page.md`), on top of the prep's types,
mappers and `submitSolutionEntry(…, {partId})`. Everything here is under `frontend/`.

**The page** (`routes/exercises/[id]`). After the shared statement and the whole-exercise Hints,
one `[data-part]` block per part in order: a card with "Part a" and its sub-statement, then its own
Hints, Answer (its own reveal, keyed by part id, so (b)'s reveal shows (b)'s answer only) and
Solutions, set in a little so they read as that part's. Then the whole-exercise Answer and
Solutions. Each stage lists only `entry.partId === part.id`; the whole-exercise ones only entries
with no part. "for the whole exercise" sits beside the whole-exercise Hints, Answer and Solutions
headings **only when parts exist** — an ordinary exercise is pixel-identical to before (four
full-page screenshots of exercise 1, anonymous and signed in, stages closed and opened, diffed
against shots taken before the first edit: **0 differing pixels in all four**).

**The composer** (`SolutionEntrySection`): two optional props, `parts` (the "For:" options) and
`part` (the block it sits in). "For:" (`[data-entry-for]`) appears only when parts exist and is
re-set from the block every time the composer opens, so "Add a hint" under (b) starts at (b). The
card (`SolutionEntryCard`) takes `partLabel` and shows "for part b" in its meta line; the section
passes it only for an entry that is NOT its own block's — which, since every block lists only its
own, never happens on the exercise page. The surfaces that list entries outside their page are
(checked): **the moderation queue's "Solutions & hints" tab** and its **"Edit suggestions" tab** —
both now say "for part c" under the heading, the label read from the same bulk exercise resolve
that already gave the titles. `/submit/mine` lists submissions, not entries; the activity feed and
notifications name the exercise only and link to its page — unchanged.

**Suggest an edit** (`EditSuggestionForm`): each part adds "Part b — statement" and "Part b —
answer" to the field choice (named in full, not an optgroup: a closed select shows the option alone,
and "Statement" under a "Part b" group read exactly like the shared statement in the first
screenshot). The form now awaits `onSubmit` and shows a refusal sentence (or the generic error)
instead of an unhandled rejection. `submitEditSuggestion(…, reason, partId)` sends `part: <number>`
only when a part was chosen; `RawEditSuggestion.part` → `EditSuggestion.partId`.

**The Parts editor** (`/exercises/[id]/edit`, `[data-parts-editor]`, between the answer and
Details): a row per part (`[data-part-row]`) with a label input, a `RichEditor` + `InsertStrip` for
the statement and another for the answer, Move up / Move down / Remove, and "Add a part". Removing a
SAVED part leaves a dashed line "Part c will be deleted when you save, together with its hints and
solutions" with Undo; a never-saved row just goes. Save with a known part dropped opens an in-page
confirm (`[data-parts-confirm]`, `role="alertdialog"`) naming each part with its hint and solution
counts — "Part c — hints: 1, solutions: 1" — and nothing is sent until "Delete and save".
`updateExercise` passes `parts` through as `[{id?: number, label, statement, answer}]` in display
order; the page sends `parts` **only when the exercise had parts or now has some**, so an ordinary
exercise's PATCH is byte-for-byte what it was (asserted). A refusal anywhere in the body — flat,
`{parts: ['…']}` or nested per item — is found by `labels.ts: firstRefusalWord` and said through
`PART_REFUSAL_LABELS` (the six words step A answers with: `part_not_of_exercise`,
`part_label_duplicate`, `parts_too_many`, `part_and_entry`, `part_field_invalid`, `part_immutable`).

**Keys**: 32 `parts_*` in one block at the end of both catalogues (5502 = 5502, 0 missing either way).

### Verified

- `npm run check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings (8090 files). `npx eslint .`: clean. `npm run build`: green.
- `npx prettier --check .`: the 28 files it flags are the same 28 before and after this change
  (contests, analytics, …; listed by diffing the two runs) — none of them is touched here, and every
  file this change touches is formatted. Left as found: reformatting 28 unrelated files on a branch
  that merges beside two others is a conflict, not a fix.
- `e2e/exercise-parts.mjs` on 8183/5283: **53 passed, 0 failed**, zero page/console errors. Seven
  screenshots in `e2e/screens/exercise-parts/`, looked at: the three blocks and the labelled
  whole-exercise stages (1), "For: part b" pre-set in (b)'s composer (2), the new hint under (b) only
  (3), "Part b — statement" chosen in Suggest an edit (4; the first run showed a bare "Statement",
  which is why the options are named in full), the confirm naming (c) (5), the refusal sentence (6),
  "for part c" in the moderation queue (7).
- **Two requests are intercepted, on purpose**: `PATCH /api/exercises/{id}/` with `parts` and
  `POST /api/edit-suggestions/` with `part` are step A's, built at the same time, so the script
  catches them with `page.route`, asserts the payload and answers with a stand-in (nothing written).
  The entry POST with `part` is real. The integrator removes the two interceptions after the merge.
- `e2e/exercise-edit.mjs` was NOT re-run: it needs an exercise u-michal wrote and this worktree's
  database has none. `exercise-parts.mjs` step 5 covers the one thing it could have caught (an
  ordinary exercise's PATCH carries no `parts`).

### Left open

- **Parts in `TranslateForm`**: a translation of a set-shaped exercise carries no part text yet;

## 17CV — Sub-exercises: the integration (2026-10-21, `fix/analytics-after-deploy`)

The three branches of `prompts/README.md` §12 came back the same afternoon and were merged in the
order the plan named — A (`75fa99c` + `84a52b9`), B (`07f98b6`), C (`fb4e16e`) — with the only
conflicts the expected "both appended" ones at the end of this file and of `test.md`. What the
integration itself changed, beyond the merges:

- **One cap, asked twice.** A put `MAX_PARTS = 26` in `exercises/parts.py` for the edit form; B's
  importer had no cap. The importer now reads the same constant and refuses a file with more parts
  in its usual sentence ("27 parts; the most is 26 …"); `test_import_parts.py` pins it (28 tests).
- **The browser script runs against the real backend.** C's `e2e/exercise-parts.mjs` answered the
  PATCH with `parts`, the suggestion POST with `part` and staff's ordinary PATCH with `page.route`
  stand-ins, because A was being built at the same time. All three are gone. The script now captures
  each request with `waitForResponse` registered before the click — a `page.on('response')` listener
  missed the PATCH whose success navigates away, and the PATCH URL carries `?lang=`, so the match is on
  the pathname — asserts the status, and reads back through the API what the backend holds: parts
  `b1,a2,d3` after the save with (b) and (a) keeping their ids, (d)'s text landed, (c)'s hint and
  solution gone with it, the set unverified while (d) has no solution; ola's suggestion listed as
  pending for part (b); staff's ordinary exercise still without parts. Two consequences of making it
  real: staff's edit is on a SECOND seeded exercise (a real PATCH on corpus row 1 would have been a
  real write), and the queue check files a fresh pending hint for (a), because the seeded one for (c)
  was deleted by the real cascade in step 4 — which is the behaviour the design asks for, seen end to
  end. The duplicate-label refusal is provoked for real by renaming (d) to "b". **65/65**, zero
  console errors, seven screenshots looked at: whole-exercise hints above the part blocks, the
  whole answer below them, the delete confirm naming "Part c — hints: 1, solutions: 1", the queue
  row reading "for part a".
- **The verified question A left for the integrator** is answered by the same script: with (d) added
  and unsolved, the API says `verified: false` on the real page's data.
- **Formatting.** Twenty-seven analytics and contests files predating this work failed
  `prettier --check`; a formatting-only commit (`965c907`) cleaned the tree so the next person's
  Prettier run reports only their own files.

**Verified after the merge, on the main checkout:** `manage.py test exercises moderation licensing
provenance --parallel 4 --keepdb` **401 OK**; `check` 0 issues; `makemigrations --check` no changes;
`check_databases_declared` 0; the dev database and the nine log shards migrated (0017, 0056 applied);
catalogues 5502 = 5502; `npm run check` 0/0; eslint clean; `npm run build` green;
`e2e/exercise-parts.mjs` 65/65 and `e2e/exercise-edit.mjs` 20/20 against `run.sh`'s servers (the
latter needs an exercise with an approved submission row behind it, so the integration seeded one and
removed it after); `dump_text_fields` + `check:katex` 2259 rows / 0 issues (parts included, A's item).
**The paczka4 rehearsal** on a copy of the post-paczka3 database migrated through the merged code (the
server's own path): algebra dry run and real run `0 created, 5 updated; parts: 17 created, 0 updated,
0 removed; 5 pinned rows removed`, fale `0 created, 10 updated; parts: 26 created; 13 removed`, a
second run of each all zeros, 15 exercises with 43 parts, all 15 still verified. The dry run prints
the parts line before any import, which is what `apply-on-server.sh` step 10 greps for.

**Shipped as `FUW/UPDATE-20261021-d.tar.gz`** (`deploy/UPDATE-2026-10-21.md`, the `-d` section):
the two migrations, the rebuilt frontend, and the paczka4 kit behind step 10, which runs only after
the code is deployed and migrated — the order the kit's own `PRODUCTION.md` insists on, because a
parts backend under the old page would show 964 its lead sentence and nothing else. Nothing pushed.

**Left open by the integration** (the three branches' own lists stand in §17CV.A–C and on the board):
- `TranslateForm` has no part rows (A and C both named it); a part cannot be translated through the
  form yet, only through a suggestion for a locale the exercise already has.
